Miami Dade County by the numbers

How big is Miami-Dade County, and who pays the tax?

The county covers 1,899.90 land square miles and held an estimated 2,802,029 people in mid-2025, per the Census Bureau. Housing units total 1,125,274, and owners live in 52.2 percent of them.

Owner-occupied homes carried a median value of $463,000 across 2020 to 2024. Households earned a median of $71,753 in 2024 dollars. Tax follows value, and values here sit above many Florida counties.

Which Miami-Dade offices handle property tax?

Three county offices divide the work, and every office handles one part of the bill.

  • The Property Appraiser sets values and rules on exemptions. Its main office is 111 NW 1st Street, Suite 710, with a south branch at 10710 SW 211 Street in Cutler Bay. Phone 305-375-4712.
  • The Tax Collector mails bills and takes payment at 13 locations, online and through mobile offices.
  • The clerk's office records deeds, and state law gives it the filing desk for value petitions and the tax deed auctions.

The appraiser states plainly that it mails no tax bills.

What did the 2026 Miami-Dade tax roll look like?

The appraiser's June 1 estimate put countywide taxable value at $540.7 billion, up 5.5 percent from 2025. That growth rate was 3.2 percentage points lower than the prior year's rate, according to the appraiser.

The Board of County Commissioners ordered the roll extended on September 1, 2026, and the appraiser certified it on October 16, 2026. That initial certification excludes changes the Value Adjustment Board may make after tax appeals.

Miami-Dade 2026 roll milestones from the appraiser
MilestoneDetail
June 1 estimate$540.7 billion, up 5.5%
Extension orderedSeptember 1, 2026
Initial certificationOctober 16, 2026

What are the millage rates across Miami-Dade municipalities?

Rates differ a lot by city. The 2026 adopted chart lists totals from 14.9007 on one North Miami Beach line up to 24.1893 for Biscayne Park, while unincorporated areas total 16.8983.

Examples from the chart: Miami totals 19.9544, Miami Beach 18.6681, Coral Gables 18.1518, Hialeah 18.6134 and Doral 16.9487. Some rows carry extra debt or district lines, so read each row on its own.

Always use the chart row for your actual taxing area. Our city pages cover Miami and Miami Beach in more detail.

Which municipalities appear on the Miami-Dade millage chart?

The 2026 chart covers more than three dozen taxing areas. The list runs from Aventura, Bal Harbour and Bay Harbor Islands through Coral Gables, Doral, Hialeah and Homestead to Key Biscayne, Pinecrest, Sunny Isles, Surfside and West Miami, plus unincorporated areas.

  • Lowest city lines: Doral at 1.5994 mills, Sunny Isles at 1.6514, Aventura at 1.7261.
  • Highest city lines: Biscayne Park at 9.2000, Opa-Locka at 8.9797, El Portal at 8.0500.
  • Mid-range: Hialeah at 6.3018, Homestead at 5.9604, Miami Gardens at 6.9363.

Cities with a low rate may still show other lines such as fire and rescue or library. Always read your total, not the city figure alone.

What does the Miami-Dade economy add to the tax base?

Census figures for 2023 count 98,394 employer establishments employing 1,055,440 people, with total annual payroll of about $71.6 billion. Employment grew 4.6 percent from 2022 to 2023.

For 2022, the Census shows $67.1 billion in retail sales, $15.4 billion in lodging and restaurant sales, $30.3 billion in health care revenue and $38.5 billion in freight and storage receipts. Building permits for 2025 numbered 16,535.

Business property is taxed too. Tangible personal property owners file Form DR-405 by April 1, and the appraiser runs a searchable tangible personal property tool by business name, address or folio.

When are Miami-Dade property taxes due?

Statements are mailed in November, and the discount shrinks monthly from 4 percent down to 1 percent in February. By state law, whatever is unpaid on April 1 turns delinquent.

  • The proposed-tax notice reaches owners in August, per the state calendar.
  • Value challenges are filed at the clerk's desk inside 25 days of that notice.
  • If an exemption is denied, the board petition is due 30 days after the letter is mailed.
  • Anyone wanting installments must ask the tax collector by May 1.

How do Miami-Dade tax certificates and tax deeds work?

When a bill stays unpaid, the tax collector sells a certificate to whoever bids the lowest interest rate, in quarter-percent steps. Certificates nobody wants go to the county at the maximum rate, and all sales wrap up by June 1.

Homestead property with under $250 owed goes to the county instead of auction. The collector keeps a 5 percent commission.

  • No holder may press an owner until two years after April 1 of the issue year.
  • A tax deed application costs $75.
  • At auction, the winner posts the larger of 5 percent or $200 and pays the rest within 24 hours, not counting weekends and holidays.

The tax collector's homepage lists a Tax Certificate Sales service, and the clerk runs the deed auction. Ask either office for the current sale schedule.

What limits how fast Miami-Dade tax bills can grow?

State law limits non-homestead assessed value growth to 10 percent each year. Taxing authorities also face a revenue growth cap tied to Florida per capita personal income growth plus new construction, unless a super-majority, unanimous vote or referendum overrides it.

Final millage comes from public hearings. Taxing authorities hold hearings on tentative budgets in September and October and on final budgets in October and November.

What relief programs exist for Miami-Dade homeowners?

The base exemption is up to $50,000, filed with the appraiser by March 1. Seniors 65 and older may qualify for up to $50,000 more if a local ordinance allows it and household income is within the limit.

Veterans have several paths. A disabled ex-servicemember rated 10 percent or more gets a $5,000 reduction, and a veteran 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability may receive a discount that matches the VA disability percentage.

Deferral is another option. File Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31 to defer the part of the tax above 5 percent of household income, or 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older.

What else can the property appraiser's office do for me?

The appraiser now accepts widow(er) exemption and veteran disability exemption filings online, plus agricultural classification applications on form MD-482 with uploaded documents. In-person visits can be booked online to skip the line.

The office also runs a property tax estimator and a hotline for suspected homestead fraud at 305-375-3402.

What happens to the tax bill when a Miami-Dade house sells?

The title agent gets a balance statement from the tax collector and settles the year's tax from the seller's proceeds. Your contract decides how that year's tax is divided between buyer and seller.

Deed stamps here run 60 cents per $100, plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax that the revenue department says is not due on a document moving only a single-family dwelling. The clerk collects them at the counter or by e-filing.

More questions about Miami-Dade County, FL Property Tax Guide

What is the unincorporated Miami-Dade millage rate for 2026?

The adopted chart lists 16.8983 mills in total for unincorporated areas, with a municipal-services line of 1.9090.

How can I pay a Miami-Dade tax bill?

Pay the county tax collector online, at one of its 13 locations, or through a mobile office. The property appraiser does not take payments.

When does the Miami-Dade value appeal window close?

Twenty-five days after the notice of proposed taxes, which arrives in August. The 2026 window has already closed.

Does Miami-Dade offer a discount for early payment?

Yes. It starts at 4 percent for November and drops one point each month through February.

Does Miami-Dade have a Save Our Homes cap?

Yes. Homestead assessed value can rise by no more than the lower of 3 percent or CPI each year. For 2026 the state chart lists 2.7 percent.

Broward County by the numbers

Which Broward offices value and bill property?

The Broward County Property Appraiser (BCPA) values property and approves exemptions. The Broward County Tax Collector sends the bills and collects payment.

BCPA says plainly that it neither sends tax bills nor sets or collects taxes. The tax collector can be reached at (954) 357-4829 or revenue@browardtax.org, a contact BCPA prints on its home page. Deeds are recorded through the county's Official Records system, and BCPA asks owners to use its FAQ page for questions about recording.

What are the Broward homestead filing dates?

For 2027, BCPA says the timely filing period runs from March 3, 2026 through March 1, 2027. Owners who held title and made the home their permanent residence after January 1, 2026 may file for 2027 now.

If you miss March 1, a late filing is still possible until September 20, 2027, the absolute last day under s. 196.011(8), whatever the reason for the delay. Filing can be done online, by email at CSEmgmt@bcpa.net, by fax at (954) 357-6188 or by mail to 1801 NW 49 Street, Suite PA1, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33309. For help, call the office at (954) 357-5579, where staff can also set a virtual meeting.

The 2027 dates above are printed on the appraiser's page, so use them as the reference for that tax year and ask BCPA for later years.

What is the Florida tax calendar for a Broward owner?

Value is fixed on January 1 and bills arrive in November. April 1 is the delinquency date.

Key Florida tax dates for Broward County property owners
Date or windowEvent
March 1Exemption filing deadline
April 1Tangible personal property return due (Form DR-405)
AugustNotice of proposed taxes mailed
25 days after that noticeValue petition deadline
NovemberTax bills sent
November to FebruaryDiscount of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent by month
June 1Tax certificates sold on unpaid items

How does a Broward sale change the assessed value?

BCPA warns buyers that a change in ownership resets assessed value to full market value, which can mean higher taxes. It offers a Home Buyer's Tax Estimator on its site so a buyer can approximate the new bill.

That reset removes the Save Our Homes cap. The cap limits yearly increases on a homestead to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change, and Revenue's chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026. Rentals and other non-homestead parcels face a 10 percent annual limit. Sellers of rentals in Broward therefore carry a smaller gap, while a long-held homestead can carry a large one.

Can I keep my Broward homestead benefit if I move?

Portability lets a seller move part of the benefit to a new Florida homestead. Establish the new one within three years of January 1 of the abandonment year of the old homestead, and file Form DR-501T with the DR-501 by March 1.

BCPA runs a Portability Estimator on its site. Statute text caps the reduction at the lesser of $500,000 or the difference between just and assessed value on the old home, and a 2026 act amends the section for the 2027 roll, so confirm the rules with BCPA before you file.

What relief programs exist for Broward owners?

BCPA lists senior, veteran and other exemptions on its site. A Broward homestead exemption tops out at $50,000, and only the first $25,000 touches the school levy.

  • Seniors 65 and older: a local ordinance may add up to $50,000 for households inside the income limit. BCPA can say whether Broward or a city inside it uses that option and what the income cap is.
  • Disabled ex-servicemembers: a $5,000 reduction.
  • Veterans past 65 with a permanent service-connected disability: a discount matching the VA rating.
  • Deferral: file Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31, for taxes above 5 percent of household income.

BCPA also posts a catastrophic structural damage report form for a home left uninhabitable for 30 days or more after a catastrophic event, which can matter to a Broward owner selling a storm-damaged house. Its Senior Citizens tab is the place to start for age-based relief.

What if a Broward owner falls behind on taxes?

Unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1, and the tax collector sells certificates by June 1 to the bidder offering the lowest interest rate, in quarter-percent steps. The holder stays quiet for two years from April 1 of the issue year.

After that, a holder can apply for a tax deed with a $75 fee, and the clerk runs the auction (s. 197.542). The high bidder posts a deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is more, and pays in full within 24 hours excluding weekends and holidays. A homeowner who sells before then can get a payoff number from the collector's office.

Where do I challenge a Broward value?

BCPA has an Appeals and Petitions section, and its Property Owner Bill of Rights is on the home page. The clerk receives a formal value petition, due 25 days after the August notice. Exemption denials get 30 days after the letter was mailed.

What taxes apply when a Broward house is sold?

The real estate tax stays with the parcel until paid, and the deed carries documentary stamp tax at a rate of $0.70 for every $100 of the price and debt transferred under state law. Every party on the deed answers for the stamp tax.

  • Real property tax: billed each November by the collector.
  • Documentary stamp tax: paid at recording.
  • Tangible personal property: a Form DR-405 return is due to the appraiser by April 1, and BCPA has a Tangible Property section for landlords with furnishings.

What should a Broward heir know before selling an inherited house?

The homestead exemption ends when the owner has stopped living there, so the next year's bill can differ. Contact BCPA at (954) 357-5579 to ask how an inherited transfer will be treated. Some transfers on death are exceptions to the change-of-ownership reset in the Save Our Homes rules.

Estate paperwork runs through probate court. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is not on the stamp tax list of taxable deeds, and no Florida estate tax applies to deaths after 2004.

What does a Broward homeowner do about unwanted occupants or tax deed notices?

If someone is occupying a Broward house without permission, state law lets an owner submit a verified complaint to the sheriff to remove persons unlawfully occupying residential property, with conditions such as no tenancy and no pending litigation (s. 82.036). Adverse possession needs seven years of possession and payment of taxes (s. 95.18).

If a tax deed notice arrives, contact the tax collector right away, because the list of people noticed includes titleholders, mortgagees and contract-for-deed vendees. A homestead owner owing under $250 has the certificate issued to the county, and a tax deed opening bid on a homestead includes half of the latest assessed value (s. 197.502). Ask the tax collector how those rules apply to your parcel, and keep the notice with your sale papers.

More questions about Broward County, FL Property Tax Guide

Which office collects Broward tax?

The county tax collector's office. BCPA says it does not send bills and directs questions to that office at (954) 357-4829.

What is the late-filing limit for a 2027 Broward homestead?

September 20, 2027 is the absolute deadline for any 2027 exemption, per BCPA citing s. 196.011(8). The timely date is March 1, 2027.

Can I file my Broward homestead online?

Yes. BCPA accepts online homestead filing, plus email, fax and mail. Forms are under its Download Forms tab.

Will a buyer inherit my Broward assessment cap?

No. A change of ownership resets value to market on the next first of January, so a buyer should use BCPA's tax estimator.

What is the delinquency date in Broward County?

April 1. State law puts the certificate sale on or before June 1.

What we could not confirm

  • Mail date for bills
  • Installment plan terms

Hillsborough County by the numbers

Which Hillsborough County office does what?

Billing and collection belong to the Hillsborough County Tax Collector, and the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser sets values and rules on exemptions. A question about value belongs with the appraiser, and a question about paying goes to the collector.

The appraiser's main office is in the County Center at 601 E. Kennedy Boulevard in Tampa, on the 15th floor, on weekdays between 8:00 am and 5:00 pm at (813) 272-6100. Tax bills, payment options and a property tax search run through the tax collector's property tax page. Deeds and liens that affect a sale are filed with the clerk, covered on our Hillsborough County property records page.

  • Property Appraiser: value, homestead, Save Our Homes cap, portability, TRIM notice.
  • Tax Collector: bills, payments, installment plan, tax certificates.
  • Value Adjustment Board: hears value and exemption petitions.

What are the Hillsborough County due dates and early payment discounts?

Hillsborough tax notices arrive in November with a November 1 due date, and April 1 is the delinquency date. The tax collector's FAQ says delinquent accounts pick up 3% interest plus advertising costs on that date.

A November payment trims 4 percent from the bill, and the break shrinks a point each month until February's 1 percent. Pay in March and there is no reduction. A payment that arrives after March 31 is late even if the bill was never opened, so a seller listing in winter should find out which month's discount a closing date will fall in.

Owners who want smaller payments can apply for the installment plan before May 1. The first payment is due in June. If June is missed, July still works but the discount is lost, and an account with no payment by July 31 is dropped from the plan. Full payment is then due in November with the 4 percent discount. Current-year bills can be paid in part under the collector's partial payment plan, and delinquent real estate bills cannot.

What dates matter on the Hillsborough County tax calendar?

Seven dates cover almost every Hillsborough County property tax decision, from the January 1 valuation to the April 1 delinquency.

Hillsborough County tax calendar with the office that publishes each date
DateWhat happensSource
January 1Valuation date; homestead status fixedFlorida Revenue
March 1Statutory deadline for exemption applicationsProperty Appraiser
May 1Last day to apply for the installment planTax Collector FAQ
Before June 1Tax certificate sale for delinquent accountsTax Collector FAQ
AugustTRIM notice mailed; value petition due within 25 daysFlorida Revenue
November 1Bills payableTax Collector FAQ
April 1Unpaid taxes delinquentTax Collector FAQ

The appraiser mails an Official Notice of Denial by July 1 when an exemption is refused, and that notice opens the right to a hearing before a magistrate hired by the Hillsborough County Value Adjustment Board.

What homestead and senior exemptions apply in Hillsborough County?

A Hillsborough County homeowner can deduct up to $50,000 from the assessed value of a permanent residence. The first $25,000 lowers every levy. The second $25,000 covers value from $50,000 to $75,000 and leaves the school levy untouched.

After the first year, assessed value can rise each year by no more than 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is lower. The appraiser says applications are taken year round, the statutory deadline is March 1, and a late application can be accepted up to the 25th day after the TRIM notice is mailed.

  • Low income senior exemption: the City of Tampa and unincorporated Hillsborough County allow up to $50,000, and Temple Terrace allows up to $25,000.
  • Long term resident senior exemption: offered by the City of Tampa and unincorporated Hillsborough County for homes with a just value under $250,000 and 25 consecutive years of residence.
  • Veteran, disability, widow and blind exemptions: papers required; Hillsborough County Veterans Affairs is listed at 813-635-8316 for help with discharge papers.

An owner who keeps a homestead exemption after the house stops being the permanent home faces a lien for the exempted taxes from the prior 10 years, plus a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest, according to the appraiser. Report the change before a sale if the owner has moved out.

Does the 2026 Florida property tax amendment change the Hillsborough County homestead exemption?

The appraiser's legislative update page describes the amendment on the 2026 ballot as setting homestead exemption amounts of up to $150,000 beginning in 2027 and up to $250,000 beginning in 2028, and it directs the Legislature to schedule later increases. The appraiser's home page also carries a statement issued after the vote.

Ask the property appraiser how the amendment applies to your parcel and which taxes it reaches, because the legislative update page says the exact savings differ by property and cannot be calculated in advance. The Hillsborough County Tax Collector also posts a property tax reform page for the same ballot item. Until a bill shows a new exemption amount, plan a sale around the exemption printed on your current bill.

How does a Hillsborough County sale deal with the tax bill?

Because the lien runs with the land, any open Hillsborough County bill comes out of the seller's money at the closing table. The tax collector notes that the name on the bill does not block payment, because the appraiser may not yet have received a recorded deed when the roll was certified.

A sale also ends the owner's homestead benefits. Any sale or transfer of title counts in Florida as a change of ownership, so on the following January 1 the home is assessed at just value and the incoming owner must file a fresh application. Portability of the capped value belongs to the seller and attaches to a new homestead, not to the house being sold.

  • Escrowed loans: the servicer pays from a list sent to the tax collector, and after payoff the bill comes to the owner once November 1 passes.
  • Documentary stamp tax: Deed stamps: 70 cents for each $100 of the price everywhere but Miami-Dade, with every party to the deed answerable.
  • Portability: the new homestead must be set up inside a three year window that runs from January 1 of the year the old one was given up, with Form DR-501T filed with the DR-501.

What if Hillsborough County tax is never paid?

Nonpayment leads first to a tax certificate, and about two years later to a possible tax deed sale. The tax collector runs the certificate sale as an online auction, with bidding that starts at 18 percent and drops in 0.25 percent steps, and the lowest rate wins.

The certificate is a first lien that ranks ahead of other government liens. The tax collector says an owner has up to 22 months after the certificate is issued before a tax deed foreclosure can begin, and the Florida statute counts two years from the April 1 of the issue year. A homestead parcel owing under $250 has its certificate issued to the county, so no bidder gets it. At the deed stage the clerk holds the auction, and the opening bid on a homestead parcel adds half of the latest assessed value.

Being behind does not stop a sale. Paying the bill at closing redeems the lien and clears the title for the buyer.

More questions about Hillsborough County, FL Property Tax Guide

When is Hillsborough County property tax due?

Bills are payable November 1 and become delinquent April 1. Payments made in November earn a 4 percent discount, December 3 percent, January 2 percent and February 1 percent. After the delinquency date, the tax collector adds 3% interest and advertising costs.

Can I pay Hillsborough County property tax in installments?

Yes, if you apply before May 1. June brings the first payment. A July payment keeps you on the plan without the discount, and a missed July 31 deadline drops the account, which then owes the full amount in November with the 4% discount.

Who decides my Hillsborough County homestead exemption?

The Hillsborough County Property Appraiser decides it. Filing closes March 1, and a denial notice is mailed by July 1 and points to the Value Adjustment Board. The tax collector has no say over eligibility.

Does the tax collector accept partial payments on delinquent bills?

No. Current-year bills can be paid in part under a separate plan, yet delinquent real estate bills cannot. Ask the office before sending less than the full balance.

What if I sell my Hillsborough County house before the bill arrives?

The tax still has to be paid when the sale closes. The closing agent asks the tax collector for the figure and deducts it from the seller's funds. The seller's homestead exemption ends with the sale, and the buyer applies for a new one by the following March 1.

Palm Beach County by the numbers

Which office bills Palm Beach County property tax?

The Palm Beach County Constitutional Tax Collector sends the bills and accepts payment, while the Property Appraiser sets the value and decides exemptions. Two offices, two jobs, and a mix-up between them is the most common reason an owner calls the wrong number.

The tax collector's page says its office mails more than 600,000 property tax bills by November 1 each year, and that bills go to the address the Property Appraiser has on file. If you moved or sold, fix the address with the appraiser, not the collector. The appraiser's exemption desk is at 561.355.2866, and the collector's delinquent-tax line printed on the bill page is (561) 355-2264.

The clerk and comptroller is the third office you will meet. It runs the Value Adjustment Board that hears appeals, and it conducts tax deed sales if a certificate ever reaches that stage.

  • Palm Beach County Property Appraiser: values, exemptions, caps, the TRIM notice.
  • Palm Beach County Tax Collector: bills, payment, installment plan, deferral, certificates.
  • Clerk and Comptroller: Value Adjustment Board petitions and tax deed sales.

What is Palm Beach County like for owners and sellers?

QuickFacts lists 1,575,726 people living here in mid-2025. The page's 2020 density figure is 759.7 residents for each square mile.

Its 2020 to 2024 figures show a $447,300 median home value among owners and a 70.1 percent owner-occupied rate. Median household income was $83,581 in 2024 dollars. Residents 65 and over are 26.1 percent of the population, so senior and veteran benefits shape many bills.

The property appraiser's municipality list shows how many separate taxing authorities exist. Its codes run from 00 for unincorporated areas through towns and cities such as Atlantis, Belle Glade, Boca Raton, Boynton Beach, Delray Beach, Jupiter, Lake Worth Beach, Palm Beach, Pahokee, Tequesta, Wellington, West Palm Beach and Westlake. The first two digits of a 17-digit parcel control number carry that code, so the number on your bill tells you which city levies on your lot.

What is the Palm Beach County payment window and discount schedule?

Bills are payable from November 1 through March 31, and an early payment discount shrinks each month. The tax collector's schedule starts at 4 percent off in November and drops one point per month through February, leaving the gross amount due in March.

April 1 is the delinquency date. After that the bill carries penalties and interest, it cannot be paid online, and the collector says money must be in hand by month end, since a postmark stops counting once the tax is delinquent. When a deadline lands on a weekend or holiday, state law moves it to the next business day.

The county's installment plan lets you prepay in pieces. The tax collector's 2026 calendar lists an application deadline of April 30, a first payment that earns a discount due June 30, a hard cutoff of July 31 for the first payment, a second payment September 30 and a third December 31. Enrollment for the following year opens November 1. Check the tax collector's calendar for the year you are in before relying on those days.

Property tax calendar as printed by the Palm Beach County offices
WhenWhat happensSource
January 1All property valued as of this dateProperty Appraiser
March 1Deadline to file homestead and other exemptionsProperty Appraiser
April 1Tangible personal property returns dueProperty Appraiser
May 1Income information due for limited-income senior exemptionProperty Appraiser
Mid-AugustNotice of Proposed Taxes mailedProperty Appraiser
Mid-SeptemberDeadline to appeal market value to the Value Adjustment BoardProperty Appraiser
November 1Bills open for payment, 4 percent discount period beginsTax Collector
March 31Final day before delinquencyTax Collector

How do the homestead exemption and the assessment caps work in Palm Beach County?

A homestead exemption lowers the taxable value of your primary home, and a cap limits how fast its assessed value can climb. The county appraiser says you must be a permanent Florida resident holding title to the home and living in it on the first of January, and you must file by March 1 and a late filer loses the exemption for that year.

The appraiser describes a $25,000 exemption sitting on the first $50,000 of assessed value, and it reaches every tax including the school levy. State rules add a second tier of up to $25,000 above the $50,000 mark, but only for non-school taxes. Filing is done online, in person at a service center, or by mailed form, and once approved the exemption renews itself each year. A receipt card arrives by mail at the end of each December.

Save Our Homes limits a homestead's yearly assessment growth to 3 percent or the inflation change, whichever is smaller. The state's chart shows a 2026 cap of 2.7 percent. Non-homestead property, such as a rental or second home, has a 10 percent cap on every taxing authority except the school board, and the appraiser notes that the cap falls away the year after a sale.

  • Tell the appraiser about any change in ownership, marriage, divorce, death or use of the home to the appraiser at 561.355.2866 or MyExemption@pbcpao.gov.
  • An exemption does not move to a new house on its own. A new application is required, and portability can carry part of your capped savings over if you start a new homestead within three years.
  • Renting out the home, or ceasing to live in it, ends the homestead.

How does the tax get paid when a Palm Beach County home sells?

Back tax stays with the parcel, so closing is where it ends. The closing agent reads any open bill and deducts the payoff before the seller is paid.

Work out with the closing officer how the buyer and you will divide the current year's bill, since the bill is issued in November and closings happen all year.

The deed itself carries the state documentary stamp tax. The statute sets it at seventy cents for each hundred dollars of price everywhere but Miami-Dade, and each party on the document is liable whoever agrees to pay. The clerk collects it at the recording counter. Statute also sets a per-page recording charge, with extra per-page fees added.

For the buyer, the sale moves the assessed value to market value at the following January valuation. The seller's capped homestead savings do not transfer to the buyer, which is why the neighbor's bill can look so different from the new owner's.

What if I am behind on Palm Beach County property taxes?

Missing the March 31 deadline starts a chain that ends, after two years, with a possible tax deed sale. It moves in clear steps, and you can stop it by paying at any point before the sale.

The tax collector says it is required to hold an annual tax certificate sale, no earlier than 60 days after delinquency or June 1, whichever is later. A certificate is a first lien that an investor buys by paying your tax. To redeem one, you pay the delinquent tax, accrued interest, advertising costs and an added $6.25 collection fee. Certificates the investors skip become county held and accrue interest at 18 percent a year, which the collector also states as 1.5 percent monthly.

If two years pass from the delinquency date without payment, the certificate holder can file a tax deed application, and the clerk's office runs the sale. Redemption stays open right up until the sale. The collector's resources list also names a homestead tax deferral program, which has its own qualification rules and a March 31 filing date in state materials.

  • Delinquent payments cannot be made online; use the collector's listed delivery options.
  • Call (561) 355-2264 if the bill shows a delinquent notice.
  • An owner behind on tax can still sell. Closing settles the payoff.

How can an owner contest a Palm Beach County value?

Call the Property Appraiser first. A petition to the Value Adjustment Board is the next step if that call leaves the dispute open. The appraiser's FAQ encourages the call first, with records searchable on its site or by phone at 561.355.3230.

The calendar the appraiser publishes says market value appeals and denied portability applications are due to the board in mid-September, while denied exemptions must be appealed by July 31 or inside the 30 days after the denial notice. The state tax-payer page separately gives 25 days from the Notice of Proposed Taxes for a value petition. Read the dates on your own notice, since the notice controls.

The Value Adjustment Board is run by the clerk and comptroller, independent of the appraiser. Ask the Palm Beach clerk for the current filing fee before you file.

More questions about Palm Beach County, FL Property Tax Guide

Where does a Palm Beach County tax payment go?

Pay the Palm Beach County Tax Collector. That office sends bills by November 1, takes payment through its online portal and service centers, and handles delinquent accounts at (561) 355-2264. The Property Appraiser sets value but does not collect.

Is there a discount for paying early in Palm Beach County?

Yes. November payers get 4 percent off, and the break shrinks a point each month until February's 1 percent. March has none. April 1 starts delinquency, with penalties and interest.

Do I lose my homestead exemption if I sell my Palm Beach County home?

Yes, the exemption ends with the sale and does not transfer to the buyer. Start a new homestead with a filing by the first of March in the year you want it, and ask the appraiser at 561.355.2866 about portability if you buy another Florida home within three years.

Is a sale possible while Palm Beach County tax is unpaid?

Yes. The tax is a charge on the parcel, and the closing agent deducts it before the seller is paid. If a tax certificate has already been sold, the redemption amount includes interest, advertising costs and a $6.25 collection fee.

Which office records a Palm Beach County deed?

Record it with the clerk and comptroller, who keeps the official records. Florida statute sets a per-page recording charge with added fees, and the deed also needs the 70 cents per $100 documentary stamp tax.

Orange County by the numbers

Who answers questions about an Orange County tax statement?

Orange County divides the job three ways, so the right call depends on the problem. A wrong value or missing exemption belongs to the Property Appraiser at 200 S Orange Ave, Suite 1700 in Orlando. A bill, a payment or a delinquency belongs to the Tax Collector. The rate itself is a product of local boards.

  • Value, ownership, legal description and mailing address: Property Appraiser
  • Millage: the county commission, school board, cities and special districts
  • Statements, payment plans, certificates: Tax Collector

The Tax Collector's own page says it passes the money on to 63 taxing authorities. Items such as streetlights, sewers and road work are non-ad valorem charges, priced per unit and printed on the same statement.

What is the Orange County property tax calendar?

The year's value is pinned to January 1. Statements reach owners by the first of November, and the balance must arrive at the Tax Collector before April begins.

Key tax dates in Orange County, per the Tax Collector and Florida revenue pages
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date
March 1Last day to file an exemption request
AugustProposed tax notice mailed
By November 1Statements mailed
November to FebruaryFour, three, two and one percent discounts
March 31Gross amount and deferral applications due
April 1Delinquency begins
By June 1Online certificate sale

A check postmarked March 30 but delivered in April is late, because the office goes by receipt.

How much can an early payment save in Orange County?

Pay in November and the bill drops four percent. Each month after that trims one point less, ending at one percent in February, and March pays the gross figure.

Sellers who close in winter can pay the whole year at the closing table, so the month on the contract changes the net. Your title agent can quote the number for your actual closing day. When a lender escrows your taxes it may ask for the statement, and you receive a copy stamped with the lender's request. That copy does not call for a second payment.

Owners who are current and whose prior bill topped $100 can ask for the quarterly installment plan, which is applied for online at the Tax Collector's site.

Which exemptions apply to a home in Orange County?

Homestead leads the list, and the Property Appraiser says it can lower taxable value by as much as $50,000. In the state's description, the opening $25,000 touches every levy, and a second slice reaches only non-school levies above $50,000 of assessed value.

File with the Property Appraiser before March 1, and live in the house as your permanent home on January 1. Widow, disability, senior and military exemptions also exist. Once homesteaded, the assessed figure may rise each year by no more than the smaller of 3 percent or the inflation change. A sale wipes out that gap on the following January 1, so a buyer's first bill can be well above yours. The Property Appraiser's tax estimator is aimed at people weighing a purchase or sale.

Can a house with old tax debt change hands in Orange County?

You can still sell. The title agent requests a payoff from the Tax Collector, and every open balance gets cleared as part of closing.

Once April arrives, the Tax Collector adds a 3 percent minimum charge and advertising cost. Parcels are listed in a local paper for three straight weeks, then certificates go up for competitive bids that start at 18 percent and drop. To clear a certificate, pay the tax, accrued interest and advertising cost. Late payers must use certified or cashier's funds, a money order, certain attorney, title or escrow checks, or cash at the counter; personal and business checks are refused.

  • Ask for the payoff before you list
  • Confirm whether a certificate already exists
  • Compare escrow records with the county account

How long before a certificate threatens the house?

Two years. Only then can the certificate holder apply for a tax deed, and the Tax Collector says Orange County routes those sales through the Comptroller's Office.

Before that, state law bars the holder from pressing the owner for payment. Homestead land gets one more cushion, because the opening bid must include half of its latest assessed value on top of the money due. Even so, an owner facing this stage should call the Tax Collector's property tax department early and ask for a redemption total.

Can I defer homestead tax in Orange County?

Qualifying homesteaders can postpone part of the bill by applying to the Tax Collector before April. This is a different program from the exemption.

Postponed tax remains a lien on the property. Before listing, put this question to the Tax Collector: how is a postponed balance, with interest, paid off in a sale? The state ties the amount to household income and lets a permanent resident aged 65 or older defer the share above 3 percent of that income.

What can I look up on the Orange County Property Appraiser site?

The Property Appraiser's home page offers a property search by address, owner name, sale history, property use and foreclosure status. It also links a tax estimator, a map site, downloadable forms, a tax roll and millage page, an income survey for commercial owners, code tables and a property fraud alert.

  • Use the search to confirm the parcel, owner and exemptions on your record
  • Run the estimator when you want a buyer to see a likely tax picture
  • Download the exemption forms if a new owner needs to file
  • Sign up for the fraud alert to watch your record

The estimator should be treated as a planning aid, since a new owner may not keep the seller's exemptions.

Do landlords owe a second tax in Orange County?

Yes, if the rental holds furniture, fixtures or equipment. The Tax Collector describes tangible personal property tax as a levy on those items in businesses and rental property, and on structural additions to mobile homes.

These statements arrive alongside the real estate statements and carry the same discounts. Past March 31 a monthly charge of 1.5 percent accrues, and a collection firm under contract adds 15 percent on accounts left unpaid. Selling a furnished rental means asking the Tax Collector how any open account is handled.

What do Orange County numbers say about owners?

QuickFacts lists 1,528,002 people in July 2025, spread over 527,776 households. Owners live in 56.8 percent of the homes, whose middle value is $390,100. A median mortgage holder spends $2,055 monthly, against $1,775 for a typical rent.

A statement's lines shift with the home's location: inside a city, in unincorporated Orange County, or within a special district. Read those lines on your own account before quoting a tax figure to a buyer.

More questions about Orange County, FL Property Tax Guide

Until what date can Orange County owners pay without a late charge?

March 31, counted by the day the Tax Collector receives it. A check that lands in April is delinquent.

What does a November payment save?

Four percent. The discount shrinks by a point each month until February, and March has none.

Which Orange County office fixes a wrong value or missing exemption?

The Property Appraiser. The Tax Collector bills what the certified roll shows and cannot change value, ownership or exemptions.

Can a homeowner with unpaid taxes still sell in Orange County?

Yes. Request the Tax Collector's payoff, then let the title agent settle it at closing, with certified funds if the bill is already delinquent.

Does a tax certificate transfer my house to an investor?

No. It is a lien, and you can redeem it by paying the tax, interest and advertising cost. A tax deed application cannot come until two years have passed.

Duval County by the numbers

Which Duval offices answer property tax questions?

Two offices do most of the work. The Duval County Property Appraiser sets values and rules on exemptions, and the Duval County Tax Collector sends bills and takes payment. Both offices publish on Jacksonville.gov, the consolidated city's website.

The Property Appraiser's customer service and exemptions division is at 231 E. Forsyth Street, Suite 260, Jacksonville, FL 32202, phone 904-255-5900. The Tax Collector's main address is 231 E. Forsyth Street, Jacksonville, FL 32202, phone (904) 255-5700, with weekday counter hours that start at 8:30 a.m. For value appeals, the Value Adjustment Board answers at (904) 255-5124.

  • Questions about ownership, exemptions or an assessed value: Property Appraiser.
  • Questions about a bill, a payment or a delinquent account: Tax Collector, taxcollector@coj.net.
  • Questions about a petition against your value: Value Adjustment Board.

A seller touches all three at different stages, and the clerk of the court records the deed.

Which taxing districts apply to a house in Duval County?

The district code on your parcel decides which millage applies, and Duval County has six of them. The Property Appraiser lists them as GS and USD1 for the City of Jacksonville, USD2 for Jacksonville Beach, USD3 for Atlantic Beach, USD4 for Neptune Beach and USD5 for Baldwin.

Each district's total millage is built from several authorities. For the county the listed authorities are the county, the public schools, the Florida Inland Navigation District and the St. Johns River Water Management District, with the beach cities and Baldwin adding their own levies where they apply. The Property Appraiser states that homeowners and business owners pay the same millage inside one district unless a statute or local ordinance exempts them.

A Jacksonville Beach house and a Jacksonville house of equal value can therefore receive different bills. The Property Appraiser posts millage charts by year, including 2025, on its Millage Rates page.

What are the key property tax dates for Duval County owners?

The year runs on a fixed Florida calendar, and the table below pairs each step with what the Duval offices print.

Property tax calendar as printed by Florida DOR and the Duval County Property Appraiser
WhenWhat happensSource
January 1Value and ownership are fixed for the tax yearFlorida DOR
March 1Exemption applications due; the Property Appraiser gives March 1, 2027 for the 2027 rollProperty Appraiser
April 1Tangible personal property returns dueProperty Appraiser
Mid-AugustTRIM notices mailed; in 2026 they went out August 14Property Appraiser
SeptemberPublic hearings to set budgets and millageProperty Appraiser
October 13, 20262026 final tax roll certifiedProperty Appraiser
NovemberTax bills mailed, with a 4 percent discount for November paymentFlorida DOR
April 1Unpaid taxes become delinquentFlorida DOR

Florida DOR gives the discount ladder as 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. After delinquency, tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1.

How does the Duval County homestead exemption work?

Homestead removes as much as $50,000 of taxable value on a permanent residence you owned and occupied by January 1. The first $25,000 applies to every levy including school taxes, and the second $25,000 applies only to value above $50,000 and only to non-school levies. Florida DOR notes the second slice is adjusted for inflation each year.

The Duval Property Appraiser accepts an online application for owners who moved in after January 1, 2026, and the deadline to file on time for the 2027 roll is March 1, 2027. Late filing is allowed until the 25th day after TRIM notices go out, which falls in early September. A paper application can be mailed to Suite 260 at 231 E. Forsyth Street, faxed to (904) 255-7963 or emailed to pacustserv@coj.net.

  • Save Our Homes holds yearly growth in assessed value to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. DOR's chart prints 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • After a sale the parcel is reassessed at just value, so a buyer does not inherit your capped value.
  • Portability lets you carry some of the cap to a new Florida homestead if you set it up within three years.

What is the route to dispute a Duval value?

Request an informal review first, then petition the Value Adjustment Board if needed. The deadline is printed on your TRIM notice, 25 days after mailing under state law.

A petitioner usually has to pay 75 percent of the ad valorem tax and all non-ad valorem charges before delinquency, or the petition risks denial. The Value Adjustment Board, at (904) 255-5124, confirms the amount. The Property Appraiser posts the record card for a petition online in Property Search, under the TRIM section, instead of mailing it. An exemption denial runs on a 30 day clock from the denial letter.

What happens to the property tax bill when I sell a Duval County house?

The bill follows the parcel, so unpaid tax must be cleared or settled at closing. State law leaves it to the owner to know that tax is due and to pay ahead of the April delinquency date; the owner on January 1 is the one billed.

A few points matter at a Duval closing:

  • Get the parcel's balance from the Tax Collector ahead of a signed contract, and include any delinquent years.
  • If a mortgage servicer escrows your tax, confirm with them what has been paid and what a refund looks like after payoff.
  • Duval deed stamps are charged at 70 cents for each $100 of price, and the statute makes both sides liable even when the contract assigns it to one. The clerk takes payment at recording.
  • Do not rely on aerial photos on the Property Appraiser's site for boundaries. The office tells buyers and sellers to use a surveyor and a title company.

Duval's Clerk runs a free fraud alert: a recording that matches a name you monitor triggers a notice within 48 hours. Owners of empty or inherited houses gain the most from it.

Does a rental or short-term rental change Duval property tax?

Yes. Renting a home can end the homestead, and furnishings in a rental count as taxable personal property. Florida DOR states that homestead is lost when the unit is rented or stops being the permanent home.

The Property Appraiser explains that household goods are excluded from tangible personal property only for an owner's own use. Once the home is a short-term or long-term rental, the furniture and appliances are treated as tangible personal property, and anyone owning such property on January 1 must file a return by April 1. Short-term transient rentals also owe additional sales and use tax to the Tax Collector monthly, and hosting sites such as Airbnb and VRBO do not remit it for owners. Email TouristTax@coj.net for the rules.

Does Duval County offer relief for older, disabled or veteran owners?

Yes, through separate applications at the Property Appraiser. The Duval office takes questions at 904-255-5900.

  • A disabled ex-servicemember (10 percent or more) gets $5,000 off assessed value.
  • A total and permanent service-connected disability can reach a full homestead exemption.
  • Deferral requests go to the Tax Collector on Form DR-570 by March 31.

Ask whether Duval's older-owner ordinance applies to your parcel.

More questions about Duval County, FL Property Tax Guide

When are Duval County property taxes due?

Notices arrive in November, and paying that month earns a 4 percent discount. Unpaid tax becomes delinquent April 1, and certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1. Call (904) 255-5700 for the amount on a specific parcel.

By what date must a Duval homestead application arrive?

March 1 of the tax year. For the 2027 roll the Property Appraiser lists March 1, 2027, with late filing allowed until early September, the 25th day after TRIM notices are mailed.

Do I pay the same millage anywhere in Duval County?

No. Millage depends on your taxing district: Jacksonville (GS and USD1), Jacksonville Beach, Atlantic Beach, Neptune Beach or Baldwin. The Property Appraiser's Millage Rates page lists each year's charts.

Which side covers deed stamps on a Duval sale?

Both sides to the deed owe 70 cents for each $100 of price, whatever the contract says. The clerk collects it at recording, so settle in writing who covers it before closing.

Where can I report suspected exemption fraud in Duval County?

Call the Property Appraiser's exemption fraud hotline at (904) 255-7964. For billing problems, contact the Tax Collector at taxcollector@coj.net or (904) 255-5700.

Pinellas tax steps, taken from the state revenue department's list
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date for all property
March 1Last day to file for exemptions or classifications
April 1Tangible personal property returns on Form DR-405
AugustTRIM notice of proposed taxes mailed
25 days after that noticeValue challenge petition due
NovemberBills sent, with a 4% early discount
December through FebruaryDiscount steps down to 3%, 2%, then 1%
April 1 after billingUnpaid tax is delinquent
By June 1Certificates sold on unpaid items

The August notice is the owner's one chance to react to a proposed value and proposed rates before bills exist, so read it when it arrives. Public budget hearings follow in September and October, and final budgets and millage rates are adopted in October and November. A denied exemption has its own clock of 30 days from the letter's mailing, and petitions go to the clerk.

What can reduce a Pinellas tax bill?

Filing for homestead if you live in the home does the most, and a value challenge helps if the August notice looks off. Both have fixed deadlines.

  • Homestead: $25,000 off every levy, plus up to $25,000 off non-school levies on assessed value above $50,000. File Form DR-501 after making the house your permanent home by January 1.
  • Save Our Homes: yearly growth in a homestead's assessed value stops at 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is smaller. The state's chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • Other property: assessed value may rise no more than 10 percent a year.
  • Extras for older owners and veterans: cities or counties can add senior exemptions, and a veteran with a service-connected disability may get a $5,000 reduction. The appraiser can say which ones cover your address.

If a big bill is a cash problem, the collector can set up an installment plan for owners who apply by May 1 of the tax year. A homestead owner can also file Form DR-570 by March 31 to defer part of the tax.

What did Amendment 3 change for Pinellas owners?

Voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026, and homestead exemption changes begin with the 2027 tax year. The Escambia tax collector's notice says it leaves 2026 bills alone, and the Pinellas appraiser's home page says its website is being updated for the amendment.

The 2026 bill reflects January 1, 2026 values and exemptions and follows the normal schedule. Before you quote next year's taxes to a buyer, check the appraiser's updated pages on the new exemption amounts.

What should a Pinellas owner know about the county itself?

The county's fast facts page calls Pinellas Florida's densest county, with 3,425 residents per square mile across 280 square miles. It runs 38 miles north to south and 15 miles at its widest, with 588 miles of coastline and 35 miles of beaches. The 2020 Census counted 959,107 people.

St. Petersburg is the biggest city, and Clearwater holds the county seat. The county reports about 4,500 miles of paved road and more than 400 bridges. The Gandy Causeway of 1924 was the first span over Tampa Bay, and the Sunshine Skyway followed in 1954 to join Pinellas to Manatee County.

The appraiser's roll shows what people live in: 241,442 single family units, 103,445 condo units, 22,112 townhome or PUD units, 44,323 manufactured home units and 101,180 multifamily rental units. A condo owner and a single family owner can face quite different bills.

The appraiser's courthouse office is at 315 Court Street, 2nd Floor, Clearwater, open 8AM to 5PM Monday to Friday, phone (727) 464-3207. North County, Mid County and South County offices also exist, and Mid County shares space with the Tax Collector at 13025 Starkey Rd in Largo.

How did Pinellas become a separate county?

Pinellas became Florida's 48th county on January 1, 1912, after a local referendum to split from Hillsborough County. The name comes from the Spanish Punta Pinal, point of pines, a description tied to the area's first European visit by Panfilo de Narvaez in 1528.

Tarpon Springs was the first city incorporated, in 1887. In 1914, Tony Jannus flew the world's first scheduled airline flight from St. Petersburg to Tampa. Today the county names financial services, life science and medical technology, tourism, manufacturing, defense, aviation and information technology as key sectors.

The county parks department also maintains more than 20,000 acres of parks and preserves, and the county lists 117 miles of recreational trails. For an owner, that history explains why Pinellas has so many small cities with their own boundaries. Selling a house in Dunedin, Largo, Pinellas Park or St. Petersburg runs through the same county tax collector and appraiser, but city lines decide which local levies apply.

What if I sell with tax still owed in Pinellas?

The unpaid amount comes out of closing proceeds, so ask the collector early for what is owed. Delinquency starts April 1, after which a certificate can be sold on the debt.

Bidders for certificates offer lower and lower interest rates in quarter point steps. The holder cannot press the owner for payment until two years after April 1 of the issue year, and may then apply for a tax deed at a $75 application fee. At the clerk's auction the certificate holder's bid accrues 1.5 percent monthly.

  • A homestead with under $250 delinquent goes to the county, not to auction.
  • The opening bid on a homestead adds half of the latest assessed value.
  • Notice before a tax deed sale goes to the titleholder, mortgagees and contract for deed buyers.

Selling before a deed application is cleaner, since the buyer's closing agent clears the certificate at the table. A sale also resets the assessment, so your old bill will not predict the buyer's.

More questions about Pinellas County, FL Property Tax Guide

Which office handles the Pinellas bill?

The tax collector's office. The appraiser sets values and exemptions, and the collector issues the bill and takes the money.

What early discount applies in Pinellas?

Four percent in November, then 3, 2 and 1 percent in December, January and February. The collector's home page advertises the 4 percent November discount for 2026 taxes.

When does Pinellas tax turn delinquent?

On April 1 following the November billing. Tax certificates on unpaid items are sold by June 1.

What is the route for disputing a Pinellas value?

The clerk takes petitions for 25 days after the August proposed tax notice. If an exemption is denied, the value adjustment board accepts a petition for 30 days after the letter goes out.

Does Amendment 3 touch the 2026 Pinellas bill?

No. The Escambia tax collector's notice says the 2026 bill is unchanged and homestead changes begin with the 2027 tax year. Confirm details for your parcel with the Pinellas appraiser.

Lee County by the numbers

Who bills Lee County property tax, and who sets the value?

Lee County runs property tax through two desks. The appraiser answers anything about worth, exemptions and where mail goes (239-533-6100), while the collector answers anything about paying (239-533-6000).

Sellers hit this split at closing. Neither office can do the other's job: the collector will not alter a value or exemption, and the appraiser takes no payments. Questions about a special assessment for roads, fire, water or sewer go to the authority that levied it, whose contact details sit on the tax bill itself.

  • Appraiser: parcel records, value, exemption files, mailing address.
  • Collector: bills, receipts, quarterly and partial plans, deferral.
  • Clerk: deed recording, stamp tax, and the petition filings for value disputes.

What are the Lee County tax deadlines, and does early payment pay off?

Real estate bills in Lee County open for payment on November 1 and must be settled by March 31 of the next year. April 1 turns any balance delinquent.

The state's early-pay scale starts at 4 percent off for November and shrinks by a point each month through February. A lender still printed on the notice after a payoff does not block the November discount, the collector says. March payments get nothing off.

Every Lee city shares this one calendar, from Cape Coral to Sanibel. Six ways to pay exist: web, phone, mail, in person, kiosks, and 24-hour lockers at four centers. Late tax needs more secure funds than a personal check or eCheck, so line up certified money before a closing.

What payment plans does the Lee County Tax Collector offer?

Three options exist: quarterly installments, partial payments and homestead deferral. The installment plan closes first.

Lee County Tax Collector plans, from the office's payment options page
PlanApplyKey rule
Quarterly installmentsBy April 30 of the tax year (applications open November 1)Estimated tax must exceed $100 per notice; payments due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31
Partial paymentsNovember 1 to March 31Up to five payments per account; none online; no discounts
Homestead deferralBy March 31Age, income and lien rules apply; deferred tax becomes a lien and fire insurance is required

Discounts step down from 6 percent on installment one to 4.5 percent, then 3 percent, then nothing on the last. Skip the first payment past July 31 and the enrollment ends. Partial payments cover only the live tax year, never delinquent tax, and an owner already on installments cannot combine the two.

A sale midway through does not end the plan, since the incoming owner carries it to year end. Mention it to the closing agent early.

How do homestead and senior exemptions work in Lee County?

Homestead wipes out the first $25,000 of assessed value for every levy. A second slice, printed by the Lee appraiser as up to $26,411 for 2026, reaches only non-school levies on value over $50,000.

File Form DR-501 with the appraiser by March 1, online at leepa.org, by email to exemptions@leepa.org, by mail to PO Box 1546, Fort Myers, FL 33902, or in person at 2480 Thompson Street, 4th Floor, Fort Myers, on weekdays during business hours The office finishes processing by July 1. Save Our Homes, the cap on yearly assessment growth, starts the year after the grant.

Each Lee taxing body picks its own senior exemption amount for income-qualified owners aged 65 and over:

  • City of Sanibel, City of Bonita Springs and City of Fort Myers: $25,000.
  • City of Cape Coral: $50,000.
  • Town of Fort Myers Beach and Village of Estero: $50,000 and up to $250,000.
  • All Lee County millages: $50,000 and up to $250,000.

The appraiser also lists exemptions for disabled veterans, disabled first responders, surviving spouses, deployed service members, and $5,000 exemptions for widows, widowers, blind owners and others with disabilities. Most renew each January 1 unless ownership or residency changes.

What happens to a homestead exemption when you sell a Lee County house?

A buyer gets nothing automatically, so a new application is needed, and the seller's exemption drops off at the next turn of the year.

The appraiser warns that a TRIM notice showing homestead in the year of purchase reflects the seller's benefit, which will be removed. Sellers should also know that renting the property long term, or changing how title is held (certain trusts or LLCs), can end the exemption, and the office asks to be contacted when ownership changes in any manner.

If you move to another Florida home, homestead and the Save Our Homes portability benefit must be applied for again at the new address. Florida's state portability rule gives a three-year window counted from January 1 of the year the old homestead was given up, and the form is DR-501T filed by March 1.

How does a Lee County TRIM notice differ from the tax bill?

TRIM is the appraiser's mid-August preview. The bill, sent by the collector generally in November, is the real charge and the only one listing non-ad valorem items like garbage, fire or water.

The notice shows market value, exemptions, Save Our Homes status and proposed tax. A value dispute goes to the Value Adjustment Board within 25 days of the notice; a denied exemption has a separate 30 days from the denial letter. Keep both papers handy for buyers who ask about carrying costs.

On the Amendment 3 question, the collector's FAQ answers that it begins January 1, 2027 and leaves the 2026 bill alone. Millage differs by address across school, city and district levies, so rely on your parcel lookup and your own notice instead of any county average.

Who pays Lee County tax at a sale?

On the settlement statement the closing agent apportions the year between the two parties. The year's bill still goes to the owner of record when the roll reaches the collector, so a former owner may receive one.

Its advice: pass the bill to the new owner or the closing agent. A transfer is recorded with the clerk and then relayed to the appraiser, so lag is normal. Unpaid tax appears in the title search and is cleared from seller funds.

Lee County deeds carry the standard Florida stamp rate, 70 cents per $100 of consideration (Miami-Dade differs). Each party to the deed answers for it, and the clerk takes payment at recording.

Who lives in Lee County, and what are homes worth?

Lee County sits on the Gulf Coast and holds about 875,607 people by the Census Bureau's latest estimate, 15.1 percent more than in 2020, across 781 square miles.

Of 479,540 housing units, 74.3 percent are lived in by their owners, and for 2020 to 2024 the Census reports a $362,200 median home value and $76,107 in median household income. Residents 65 and over make up 29.2 percent of the population, which is one reason the senior exemptions above matter in sales. The county's municipalities named by the appraiser are Cape Coral, Fort Myers, Bonita Springs, Estero, Sanibel and Fort Myers Beach, and most owners outside those limits sit in unincorporated areas billed by the same offices.

More questions about Lee County, FL Property Tax Guide

Is Lee County property tax due every year on the same dates?

Yes, the calendar repeats yearly: open November 1, due March 31, delinquent April 1, with a shrinking discount from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February.

Can I still join the Lee County installment plan after April 30?

No. The window runs November 1 to April 30, and a late applicant is left with the partial plan, open through March 31.

Does the buyer get my homestead exemption in Lee County?

No. Buyers apply themselves. A TRIM notice listing homestead right after a purchase shows the seller's old benefit, which is removed.

Whom should I contact if my Lee County value looks wrong?

Ring the appraiser at 239-533-6100. A formal petition on a DR-486 form is lodged with the clerk inside 25 days of the proposed-tax notice.

What happens if Lee County property tax is unpaid when I sell?

The title company clears it from seller funds, along with any added charges. Because personal checks and eChecks are refused for late tax, ask the collector which funds it takes.

Pasco County by the numbers

Who does what on a Pasco property tax bill?

Value, billing and appeals sit with three different elected offices. The appraiser sets values, the collector sends bills and takes payment, and the clerk staffs the appeals board and records the deed.

The Property Appraiser's homepage tallies 335,946 real property parcels: 206,994 single family, 11,888 condominium units, 11,347 commercial and 3,906 agricultural. The county covers 747 land square miles plus 122 of water. Its offices are in Dade City (352-521-4433), Land O' Lakes (813-929-2780) and New Port Richey (727-847-8151).

The Tax Collector lists offices in New Port Richey, Gulf Harbors, Land O'Lakes, Wesley Chapel and Dade City, with a sixth at Suncoast Parkway and SR 52 marked as coming soon. Its tax department answers at 352-521-4338, prompt 3.

  • Pasco County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, taxing districts list, records search.
  • Pasco County Tax Collector: bills, online payment, installment plan, partial payment, delinquent taxes.
  • Pasco County Clerk and Comptroller: Value Adjustment Board petitions and the Official Records.

When are Pasco County property taxes due?

Pasco follows the statewide cycle of a November bill, a discount window through February and April 1 delinquency. The collector's pages add the local penalty and installment details below.

Pasco also offers an installment plan for estimated tax above one hundred dollars. For tax year 2027, the collector's page says forms are available beginning November 1, 2026, with a filing cutoff of April 30, 2027, and no applications accepted May 1 through October 31. Payments fall in June with a 6 percent discount, September with 4.5 percent, December with 3 percent and March with none. The first payment must arrive by July 31 or you are out of the plan. Each parcel needs its own application, and renewal after that is automatic.

A partial payment application also appears on the collector's menu. State law leaves partial payments before the delinquency date to the tax collector's discretion, so ask the office before sending less than the full bill.

Pasco County installment plan schedule as printed by the Tax Collector
PaymentMonth dueDiscount printed
FirstJune6 percent
SecondSeptember4.5 percent
ThirdDecember3 percent
FourthMarchNone

How does a Pasco County homestead exemption work?

One filing with the Property Appraiser by March 1 lowers the taxable value of your primary residence. The Tax Collector's own page says it does not handle homestead filings and sends owners to the appraiser, who takes applications year round but applies the March 1 cutoff.

The appraiser's exemptions menu is organized into six groups: Homestead, Disability, Veterans, Military and First Responders, Agriculture, Parent and Grandparent, and Senior Aged 65 and older. State rules put the base homestead benefit at up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 applying to school taxes and the second $25,000 reaching only value above $50,000 for non-school taxes. Some seniors can qualify for an added exemption if the county has adopted it and income falls under a limit; ask the appraiser whether Pasco has.

A sale or deed ends the capped assessment. Under state rules a change of ownership brings the parcel back to market value at the next valuation date, with exceptions such as transfers between spouses. The state's 2026 Save Our Homes cap is printed at 2.7 percent.

  • File by March 1 of the year you want the benefit, with the home already your permanent residence by January 1.
  • Renting the home or moving out ends eligibility.
  • A servicemember may rent out the homestead without losing it, under state law.

What other Pasco County resources help an owner who plans to sell?

Beyond the three main offices, the Tax Collector's menu links several pages worth a look before you list the house. They include a change of mailing address form, an electronic bill and receipt signup, instructions for printing a paid receipt, and a page on tax deed sales.

The Property Appraiser's site has a catastrophic event page and a taxing authorities and districts list. Pasco's appraiser also publishes a reporting page for possible homestead fraud. If you are selling because the house is storm-damaged or inherited, those pages explain what relief exists and which districts levy on your parcel.

  • Update your mailing address with the right office before you move so notices reach you.
  • Print the paid receipt for your closing file once the tax is cleared.
  • Use the taxing districts list to see which local districts tax your parcel.

What follows if a Pasco County tax bill is not paid?

The bill becomes delinquent on April 1 with a late penalty, then a lien is sold, and after two years the property can go to public auction. The Pasco Tax Collector's delinquent page gives each step.

It states a late penalty of 3 percent of the tax amount added on April 1, followed by advertising charges. By the first of June a tax certificate, a claim against the parcel, is issued for the unpaid tax, penalties and costs. Interest on the certificate runs from a minimum of 5 percent to a maximum of 18 percent. If the taxes remain unpaid after two years, the property may be sold at public auction.

For delinquent bills the collector wants a money order, cashier's check or wire, and takes cash only at its offices. A personal or business check comes back, and the delay can add interest. Attorney, title company and mortgage broker escrow checks are accepted.

State law also bars a certificate buyer from contacting you to demand payment for two years after April 1 of the year the certificate was issued, so an early call from a stranger about your lien is a red flag.

How is the tax settled when a Pasco County house sells?

The closing agent deducts what is owed on the parcel, so you rarely walk a check to the collector yourself.

The collector's recent purchases page explains the follow-up. The appraiser reports ownership changes through the year; unpaid tax produces a duplicate notice to the new owner, and delinquent tax a reminder. The page also notes that the owner shown on the website is the owner as assessed on the certified tax roll, which is usually finished in early October.

Outside Miami-Dade the state deed tax runs 70 cents per $100 of price, and each party to the deed is on the hook whoever agrees to pay. Pasco's clerk quotes a recording charge in its FAQ, covered on our Pasco records guide.

The buyer's side changes too. Because a sale resets assessed value, the new owner's bill can be well above the seller's capped bill. Anyone buying to live in the house files for homestead by the next March 1.

What if I think my Pasco assessment is too high?

Talk to the Property Appraiser first, then petition the Value Adjustment Board, which the Pasco Clerk and Comptroller staffs, if you still disagree. Board petitions carry a non-refundable $50.00 filing fee under the clerk's FAQ.

The clerk lists two exceptions: a portability petition on the DR-486PORT form costs $15.00, and a petition over a denied homestead application, deployed military exemption or tax deferral has no fee. State rules allow 25 days from the proposed-tax notice for a value petition and 30 days from a mailed denial letter for exemption denials. That notice arrives in August, and the dates printed on it control.

Business equipment and rental furnishings fall under a tangible personal property return, which the appraiser's site covers on its own page. If you rent the house before selling, ask the appraiser whether one applies.

More questions about Pasco County, FL Property Tax Guide

Which Pasco County office takes my tax payment?

The Pasco County Tax Collector collects it, through five working offices and an online portal. Tax questions go to 352-521-4338, prompt 3. The Property Appraiser sets value and exemptions but takes no payments.

What does late Pasco County tax cost?

The Tax Collector's page says a 3 percent late penalty is added on April 1, followed by advertising charges. A tax certificate is issued on or before June 1, carrying interest between 5 percent and 18 percent.

Does Pasco County offer a payment plan?

Yes, when the estimated tax tops one hundred dollars. The 2027 plan needs an application by April 30, 2027. Payments fall in June, September, December and March, and the first must arrive by July 31.

Does a Pasco homestead pass to the buyer?

No, it stays with the owner. The buyer files by March 1, and the sale moves the assessed value up to market level at the next valuation date.

Can I sell a Pasco County house with delinquent taxes?

Yes. Delinquent tax, with any certificate redemption costs, is settled from your proceeds before the deed passes. The payoff figure comes from the Tax Collector's tax department.
