Polk County by the numbers

Which Polk County offices send the bill and value the house?

In Polk County one elected office decides what a parcel is worth and another one collects the money. A third office, the Clerk of the Courts, runs tax deed auctions and records deeds.

The appraiser's site at polkflpa.gov carries the parcel search, the map search, the tax estimator and the exemption filing pages. Its old address, polkpa.org, now redirects, so use the new one when you bookmark it. Its parcel statistics page counts 231,135 single family residential parcels and 329,750 housing units countywide. The Tax Collector at polktaxes.com handles bills, discounts, delinquent accounts and the annual certificate sale.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, portability, address changes. Main office phone 863-534-4777.
  • Tax Collector: tax bills, payment, delinquency and certificate sales.
  • Clerk of the Courts: tax deed sales and the free Property Alert Service that the appraiser's site recommends against deed fraud.

What does the Polk County payment calendar look like?

Bills go out around the start of November, and paying early earns a discount that shrinks each month. Unpaid taxes go delinquent April 1.

The state revenue agency prints the early-payment schedule that county tax collectors follow. The Tax Collector's delinquency page confirms that taxes unpaid after the year-end cycle go delinquent April 1 and carry 3% interest plus an advertising charge.

Polk County real estate tax payment calendar, from Florida state revenue agency and Polk Tax Collector pages
When paidWhat applies
November4% discount
December3% discount
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchGross amount, no discount
April 1Delinquent: 3% interest and an advertising charge are added
On or before June 1Tax certificate sale on unpaid parcels

The Tax Collector also notes that when a mailed payment carries a postmark showing it was late, the date the office receives it decides the amount owed. Mail early or pay online if you are near a month end.

What happens to unpaid Polk County property tax?

After April 1 the parcel is advertised and, by June 1, a tax certificate is sold against it. The certificate is a lien held by an investor, and it does not transfer the house.

Polk's Tax Collector says back taxes plus interest and fees are what the certificate covers. Bidding opens at 18% interest and goes down until a bidder wins at the lowest rate, which can fall as low as 0%. Certificates that draw no bid are struck off to the county. When a certificate is redeemed, the person paying owes the bid rate or a mandatory 5% charge, whichever is greater. The office also states that certificates are dated from opening day of the sale and expire after 7 years.

  • Once two years have run from April 1 of the issue year, the holder may file a tax deed application, and applications are filed online at realtda.com.
  • The Clerk of the Courts then holds a public auction.
  • Until the deed sale, the record owner can keep the property by paying everything owed: taxes, fees, interest, commissions and costs.

Florida's statute summary says the holder of a certificate cannot demand payment from the owner for two years after April 1 of the issue year, and homestead parcels carry a higher opening bid at a tax deed sale because it includes half the latest assessed value. An owner who already has a certificate against the house should get the collector's payoff in writing before listing.

How do Polk County homestead and senior exemptions work?

A Polk homeowner who is the permanent resident on the January 1 assessment date can file for homestead, which the appraiser says lowers assessed value by up to $50,000. Filing is free, and the appraiser warns residents to watch for third-party sites that charge for it.

For 2026 the filing deadline was March 2, and the appraiser accepted late applications until the value adjustment board petition deadline of Friday, September 11, 2026. Each later year follows the same pattern: a March deadline, then a late-file window. Once approved, the exemption renews itself every year, and approval letters are not mailed; only a denial is.

  • Limited income senior exemption: for homeowners aged 65 and over with homestead and adjusted gross household income no higher than $36,614 as the appraiser printed it, adjusted yearly by the state. Polk has authorized the full $50,000.
  • Extra 25-year residency exemption: applies to the county general millage only, needs a just value under $250,000 and 25 continuous years in the home.
  • $5,000 widow or widower, $5,000 disability, and $5,000 service-connected disability reductions.
  • Total and permanent service-connected disability and first responder exemptions for qualifying owners.

Homestead does not move on its own. A resident who buys another Polk home files a fresh application, and the portability form (DR-501T) can carry as much as $500,000 of the Save Our Homes benefit to the new homestead.

What does selling a Polk County house do to the tax bill?

After a sale the appraiser raises the parcel to full just value the next January 1, which often pushes the buyer's bill above yours. Spouse-to-spouse transfers are among the exceptions.

The assessment cap limits yearly assessment growth on a homestead to 3% or the CPI change, whichever is smaller. The revenue agency's cap chart lists a 2.7% cap for 2026 and 2.9% for 2025. The seller's protection ends with the sale, and the appraiser's exemption page encourages owners who moved in after January 1 to pre-file for the following roll.

Closing costs also include state documentary stamp tax. Florida's deed stamp rate is $0.70 for each $100 of price, and the state revenue agency adds that every party on the deed answers for it, whoever the contract says will pay. Polk is not one of the counties with a different rate. Stamps are paid through the Clerk's recording desk.

Disabled veterans who qualify under the total and permanent exemption may get a prorated first year if they buy between January 1 and November 1 and file the prorate worksheet, according to the appraiser. If you are the seller, ask the closing agent how the current-year bill will be split and whether any delinquent amount must be cleared first.

Where do I get Polk County millage and value figures?

Polk's property appraiser mails the proposed-tax notice (TRIM), in mid-August. It lists each taxing authority's proposed rate, your value and the dates of budget hearings.

Treat the notice as an estimate, since no payment is due on it. Final rates come in October, after each taxing authority certifies them to the appraiser, the Tax Collector and the state. The appraiser's tax roll page lists the statute steps: estimates by June 1, certification of value by July 1, TRIM in August, final rates in October, and the value adjustment board close-out in March or April.

For the rate on your own parcel, use the appraiser's tax estimator or the Tax Collector's parcel search. A rate for a Lakeland address differs from one in a county fire district or another city, because each municipality and special district levies its own. If a bill looks wrong, ask the collector's office for the line-by-line breakdown. A value dispute goes to the value adjustment board: the state revenue agency sets the petition window at 25 days after the TRIM notice goes out mailing.

Which Polk County cities matter when you sell?

Most sales in Polk County happen in or near Lakeland, Winter Haven and Haines City, and the county tax bill follows the parcel wherever it sits. City lines change which municipal levy appears on the bill, so give your title company the parcel ID.

The same appraiser, collector and clerk serve all of them. If you are comparing a sale in Lakeland to one in a smaller town, the process and dates are identical and only the line items change.

More questions about Polk County, FL Property Tax Guide

Are Polk County property taxes paid in advance or in arrears?

They are paid in arrears for the calendar year. The bill arrives in November and covers that year, with a discount of 4% for November payments falling to 1% for February and none in March.

What is the Polk County tax delinquency date?

April 1. Interest of 3% and an advertising charge are added then, and a tax certificate sale follows by June 1.

Can I pay Polk County property taxes in installments?

Ask the Tax Collector. The state revenue agency notes that partial payments before the delinquency date are at the tax collector's discretion under s. 197.374, and the state's four-payment installment plan needs an application by May 1.

How can I check whether my Polk County home has homestead?

Open the parcel detail page on the appraiser's site and read the Exemptions section. The office does not write individual letters, and it says to print that page for your mortgage servicer.

Does a tax certificate mean I lose my Polk County house?

No. A certificate is a lien an investor buys by paying your taxes. Loss of title can only follow a tax deed application after at least two years and a public auction run by the Clerk, and you can pay in full before the sale.

Brevard County by the numbers

Who does what on a Brevard property tax bill?

Three offices matter: the Brevard County Property Appraiser (BCPAO), the Brevard County Tax Collector and the county clerk, who files deeds. Each does a separate job, and mixing them up costs sellers time.

  • The appraiser values property each January 1, mails the August notice of proposed taxes and decides exemption eligibility.
  • The collector mails the November bill, takes payment and handles installment and deferral applications.
  • The clerk, whose offices are in Viera, Titusville, Melbourne, Palm Bay and Merritt Island, files the deed and takes the stamp tax.

Brevard's tax collector website says its office answers questions about property taxes, vehicle registration and business services, and it keeps branch offices around the county. Its homepage also offers appointments and Publix kiosks for vehicle renewals.

When do Brevard bills arrive and come due?

Bills are issued in November, and early payment earns a discount that shrinks each month: 4 percent for November, then 3, 2 and 1 percent through February. April 1 is the line after which an unpaid Brevard bill is delinquent.

Florida property tax calendar as it applies to Brevard owners
WhenWhat happens
January 1Value is set for the year
March 1Exemption and classification filing deadline
AugustNotice of proposed taxes mailed
Within 25 days of that noticeValue petition due at the clerk
NovemberTax bills sent
April 1Unpaid taxes delinquent
By June 1Tax certificates sold on unpaid items

Brevard's collector holds the figures for your parcel, including the millage rate, and can also explain installment prepayment. Ask them about it early in the year, well ahead of the November bill.

What does Brevard homestead exemption cover?

The exemption can remove up to $50,000 of taxable value. School taxes see only the first $25,000, while the other layer of up to $25,000 reaches assessed value above $50,000 for non-school levies. The second layer is adjusted each January 1 for inflation when the CPI change is positive.

Form DR-501 goes to the appraiser by March 1, and you must live there as your permanent residence by January 1. For 2026 the BCPAO home page showed midnight Monday, March 2, since March 1 landed on a Sunday.

Renting the house out, or moving out, ends the exemption. The BCPAO and the tax collector both display a notice about a homestead exemption ballot item, Amendment 3, which was on the November 3 ballot. Check the appraiser's Amendment 3 page for the result and any new rules before you file.

How does selling change a Brevard bill?

Title changing hands sends the parcel back to just value on the following first of January. That ends the Save Our Homes cap, which holds annual homestead assessment growth to 3 percent or inflation, whichever is lower.

The Department of Revenue's chart shows the cap was 3.0 percent for 2024, 2.9 percent for 2025 and a 2.7 percent cap for 2026. A long-time Brevard owner can therefore have a taxable value well under market, and a buyer should expect a higher bill. If you buy again in Florida, portability can carry part of the old benefit to the new homestead, up to $500,000, if the new homestead is set up inside three years counted from the first of January of the year the old one ended (Form DR-501T).

Can I sell a Brevard house with tax still owed?

An outstanding balance does not block a Brevard sale, yet the title agent needs the collector's payoff. Collect the payoff number, interest and any certificate costs from the Brevard collector so the closing date fits.

If taxes are delinquent, the lien process moves in a set order. A tax certificate is sold on unpaid taxes by June 1, and the holder must wait two years, counted from April 1 of the issue year, before asking the owner to pay. A deed application can follow after that period, and a homestead tax deed opens at an amount that includes half of the latest assessed value (s. 197.502).

  • Homestead owners with a small delinquency under $250 have the certificate issued to the county, not auctioned.
  • Seniors who want to defer part of the tax file Form DR-570 with the collector by March 31, and the deferral covers the portion above 3 percent of household income.

Where does a Brevard value challenge go?

If the appraiser's record shows a factual error, such as the wrong square footage or bedroom count, call BCPAO first. A formal challenge goes to the value adjustment board: file the petition, on the DR-486 series, with the clerk inside 25 days of the August proposed-tax notice.

If the appraiser denied an exemption, classification, portability or deferral, the petition window is 30 days after the denial letter was mailed. A rental owner in Brevard faces a different limit: non-homestead assessed value may climb 10 percent a year.

Which discounts and relief programs exist in Brevard County?

Some senior and veteran relief depends on a local ordinance, which Brevard's appraiser can confirm. A homeowner 65 or older may qualify for an extra homestead exemption of up to $50,000 if the local ordinance applies and income fits the limit, so ask BCPAO whether Brevard has adopted it and what the income cap is.

  • Disabled former servicemembers: $5,000 off assessed value.
  • Older veterans with a lasting service-related disability: a homestead discount that tracks the VA rating.
  • Total and permanent disability: a full homestead exemption may be possible.
  • Servicemembers deployed on a designated operation: a partial exemption on Form DR-501M.

A servicemember away on deployment can rent the house without giving up the exemption. Brevard's appraiser runs several offices, including one in Titusville, and its home page says no appointment is needed for in-person service.

Which taxes ride along with a Brevard sale?

Real estate tax follows the parcel, so an unpaid Brevard bill appears in the title search. Before closing, the buyer's title agent checks the status with the collector.

Documentary stamp tax is separate. It applies to the deed at a rate of $0.70 for every $100 of price and debt, collected by the Brevard clerk at filing.

  • Real property tax: owed to the Brevard tax collector.
  • Deed stamp tax: owed to the clerk at recording.
  • Tangible personal property return for rental furnishings or business equipment: due April 1 to the appraiser (Form DR-405).

How do property tax records help me sell a Brevard inherited house?

When an owner dies, the homestead exemption ends because the home is no longer a permanent residence, and the next first of January assessment can rise. Ask the appraiser how the transfer is treated, since some transfers upon death are among the exceptions to the change-of-ownership reset.

Heirs who want a quick sale should get a payoff quote from the collector and the exemption status from the appraiser ahead of listing.

More questions about Brevard County, FL Property Tax Guide

Which Brevard office mails the tax notice?

The Brevard County Tax Collector sends it in November. The property appraiser sets value and exemptions but does not bill.

What is the Brevard delinquency date?

April 1 following the November bill. Brevard certificates for unpaid items go on sale by the first of June.

What is the Brevard homestead filing deadline?

March 1 under state law. The appraiser posted midnight on Monday, March 2 for 2026 because March 1 fell on a Sunday.

Do I lose the homestead cap if I sell my Brevard home?

Yes for the buyer. A sale resets value to just value on the next first of January. You may carry part of the benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability.

Where can I find the current Brevard millage rate?

Read the notices from the Brevard tax collector or appraiser, which carry the rates for each taxing authority. The rate is set after budget hearings in September and October.

Volusia County by the numbers

Who mails the bill in Volusia County?

The Volusia County Tax Collector mails and collects the bill, while the Volusia County Property Appraiser sets the value and decides exemptions. The collector's site adds that the appraiser sends the Notice of Proposed Taxes in August, which carries your values and the public hearing dates.

Millage rates come from a third group: the county council, the school board, city commissioners and other taxing bodies each set their own. A mill is a dollar of tax on each thousand dollars of value. The bill you receive is the sum of every body that levies on your parcel, so two houses in the same county can owe very different amounts.

If you pay through a mortgage escrow account, the lender normally requests the bill. The tax collector says escrow owners get an informational notice that the original went to the escrow trustee. A seller with escrow should still confirm the payoff figure before closing.

What discounts and due dates does Volusia County use?

Bills go out on or about November 1, and the cheapest time to pay is November. The tax collector lists the following schedule for payments postmarked or made in person or online.

Volusia County tax collector payment schedule
PeriodWhat the tax collector page says
November4% discount; bills mailed on or about Nov. 1
December3% discount
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchNo discount; the final penalty-free day and the deferral filing cutoff
April 1Taxes become delinquent and a 3% minimum charge is added
April 30Deadline for new installment plan applications

Source: Volusia County Tax Collector, due dates and discounts. A deadline that falls on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday rolls to the next working day for walk-in payments.

What happens if a Volusia County bill goes unpaid?

After April 1 the bill carries the 3% charge, and the amount due depends on the date the office receives the payment, not the postmark. If payment has not been received and processed by close of business on April 30, the account is advertised three times, in print or electronically and on LienHub, and an advertising and listing fee lands on the bill.

Next comes the tax certificate sale. Volusia County states that the tax collector holds it by June 1, and that it is currently conducted over the internet through LienHub. The certificate is a first lien on the property, not a sale of the land.

  • The maximum interest a certificate buyer can collect is 18% a year, simple interest, and the minimum is 5% unless the bid is zero.
  • A certificate nobody bids on is issued to the county at 18%.
  • An owner redeems by paying the certificate amount plus the interest rate it sold at, counted from the month of the sale, and a $6.25 redemption fee applies from June 1 onward.
  • A certificate expires 7 years after the sale opens.

The county page adds that certificate holders may not contact the owner to demand payment until two years after April 1 of the year the certificate was issued.

Can a Volusia County tax certificate lead to a tax deed sale?

Yes. If the certificate is not redeemed within two years of the delinquency date, the holder may apply for a tax deed. The tax collector's own example: 2020 taxes became delinquent April 1, 2021, so an application can be made after April 1, 2023.

The holder files through LienHub and must also clear other open certificates and taxes on the parcel. Running the tax deed sale falls to the circuit clerk, and the collector sends questions there (clerk.org). Statewide, the clerk holds a public auction where the successful bidder posts a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater, per s. 197.542.

A homeowner who sees a certificate on the parcel has two clean choices: redeem it before an application is filed, or have the closing agent pay the redemption figure from sale proceeds. Get the exact payoff from the collector in writing.

What payment options help Volusia County owners who cannot pay in full?

Volusia County offers an installment plan, and a homestead deferral exists under state law. Both have deadlines that fall well before the bill is due, so they work only for owners who plan ahead.

  • Installments: available when the estimated tax exceeds $100, based on the prior year's gross tax. File Form DR-534 so it reaches the tax collector before May 1. Bills then come in June, September, December and March, and the first payment must be made by June 30 to stay in the plan without reapplying.
  • Escrow warning: the office says owners with a mortgage escrow account should not use installments, because the lender pays in November for the maximum discount.
  • Deferral: the March 31 date on the Volusia page matches the state rule that a homestead owner files Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31, and that the deferral covers the part of the tax above 5 percent of household income. The state spells out the formula on its taxpayer page.

The tax collector also has a partial payments page. Ask the office whether a partial payment is accepted before the delinquency date.

How do homestead and exemptions affect a Volusia County sale?

Homestead lowers the taxable value only for the owner who qualifies, and it ends with the sale. The Volusia County Property Appraiser lists homestead, senior, disability, veteran, widow or widower, granny flat, first responder, agricultural and several other categories on its exemptions page, and its records department takes questions by phone.

The state rules sit behind those categories. State guidance puts homestead at up to $50,000 in exemption, the first $25,000 reaching all taxes including school taxes and the second slice applying to assessed value over $50,000 for non-school taxes. Filing with the appraiser closes March 1, and the owner must have made the home a permanent residence by January 1, per its homestead guide.

For a buyer, the sale resets the home to just value the following January 1. Under Save Our Homes guidance, a change of ownership ends the capped assessment. That is why a seller's old bill rarely predicts what the new owner pays.

Who pays the tax when a Volusia County house is sold?

The seller owes taxes through the day of closing in the usual contract, and the title company settles them from the proceeds. The tax year runs January to December and is paid after it ends, so a mid-year closing splits the year between the parties.

The county tax collector's page warns that owners carry the duty of knowing taxes are due even when a bill goes missing. That duty comes from s. 197.122, which charges owners with knowing taxes are due, finding the amount, and paying before delinquency. If you changed your mailing address, update it with the property appraiser so bills do not go to an old location.

Recording happens at the clerk's office. Deed stamps in Florida run 70 cents for every $100 of price, as shown on the Department of Revenue, so Volusia County follows the standard rate. Ask your title agent who pays it under your contract.

What should a Volusia County seller with back taxes do first?

Get the payoff in writing, then decide whether to sell before April, during the advertising window, or after a certificate is issued. Each step adds cost, so earlier is cheaper.

  • Look up the parcel on the tax collector's online search to see the balance and any certificate.
  • Call the tax collector for the figure good through your closing date.
  • Confirm homestead status with the property appraiser before the March 1 filing date if you are staying through the January 1 cutoff.
  • Ask the clerk about any tax deed application if a certificate is more than two years old.

No matter who buys, any lien must be cleared at closing, so the amount comes out of your proceeds.

More questions about Volusia County, FL Property Tax Guide

Until what day can Volusia owners pay with no penalty?

March 31 ends the penalty-free period, per the county collector, and April 1 brings a 3% minimum charge.

What discount does Volusia County give for early payment?

4% in November, 3% in December, 2% in January, 1% in February and none in March, according to the Volusia County Tax Collector.

Can I redeem a tax certificate on my Volusia County house?

Yes. Pay the certificate amount, the interest rate it sold at counted from the month of sale, and a $6.25 fee that applies on or after June 1. Funds must be cash, cashier's check, certified check, money order or card.

How long before a Volusia County certificate can become a tax deed?

Two years after delinquency. The holder applies through LienHub, and the circuit clerk then runs the public sale.

Does the Volusia County installment plan have an application deadline?

Yes. The application must reach the tax collector before May 1 of the tax year, and the first payment is due by June 30. The form is available November 1 to April 30.

Sarasota County by the numbers

Which Sarasota County office does what with your tax bill?

Two elected offices split the job. The property appraiser at 2001 Adams Lane in Sarasota decides what your parcel is worth and who gets an exemption, and the tax collector mails the bill and takes the money. The rate itself is voted by each taxing body, and neither office controls it.

On the collector's site the real estate notice is described as a single document that merges ad valorem taxes with non-ad valorem assessments, with fire protection and solid waste given as examples. Personal property tied to a business gets its own ad valorem only bill. If the mail brings nothing by mid-November, the collector asks to hear from you and also offers a printable copy online.

Links on the collector's page point to four municipal sites: Sarasota, North Port, Venice and Longboat Key. Counter locations are listed for downtown Sarasota, Venice, North Port and Mid County. Related pages here: Sarasota, North Port and Venice.

What are the Sarasota County tax dates for payment and delinquency?

Bills open for payment on November 1 and the gross amount is due by March 31. Whatever is still unpaid on April 1 is delinquent. The collector gives a plain example: 2025 tax not paid by then went delinquent on April 1, 2026.

Discounts step down by month: 4 percent for November, 3 for December, 2 for January, 1 for February. Lenders that collect escrow must pay within the 4 percent month, per the collector. For 2026, the appraiser certified the roll on September 29 and the collector reports bills mailed or emailed by October 30.

Hardship tools exist at state level. An owner can ask the collector for an installment plan by May 1 of the assessment year, and a homestead owner may file Form DR-570 for a deferral by March 31.

Key dates published by the Sarasota County Property Appraiser and Tax Collector
DateWhat it means
January 1Valuation date and the day exemption eligibility is judged
March 1Last timely day for homestead, senior, disability and nonprofit filings
April 1Tangible personal property returns due; earlier-year tax delinquent
June 1Income papers due for the extra senior exemption
July 1Disapproval notices mailed
Mid-AugustTRIM notices mailed, 2026 on August 17
First week of OctoberCertified roll goes to the collector

How can a Sarasota County owner contest a value?

Talk to the appraiser first if you like, but you are free to file with the Value Adjustment Board or sue in circuit court without doing so. The appraiser's page lists all three paths and says they need not be taken in order.

A value petition is due 25 days after the TRIM mailing, a date printed on your notice. After a denied exemption or denied assessment transfer, you get 30 days from the letter's mailing date. The Clerk to the Value Adjustment Board answers filing questions at (941) 861-5279.

Disagree with the board's ruling? A circuit court claim may be filed within 60 days of roll certification. Remember the board looks at value, classification and exemption only. If the tax rate bothers you, speak up at the budget hearing printed on the notice.

What should you bring when you dispute a Sarasota County value?

Documents win these discussions. The appraiser says most issues end in informal talks, and offers sales comparisons and damage records as examples of helpful proof.

  • Your TRIM notice and parcel number.
  • Closing figures for similar houses sold close by.
  • Contractor estimates or photographs for storm or structural damage.
  • Residency papers if a homestead was denied.

The appraiser's phone is 941.861.8200. Hurricane damage has its own page on the appraiser's site.

How does the Sarasota County tax roll move from estimate to bill?

The appraiser's calendar ties each step to a Florida statute. It starts in June and ends in the spring after the bills go out.

  • By June 1: estimates of taxable value go to each taxing authority (s. 200.065(8)).
  • July 1: the appraiser certifies taxable value to each authority.
  • Within 55 days of that certification, which the page puts at August 24: TRIM notices go out by first class mail.
  • Within 101 days of certification: each authority certifies its final adopted millage to the appraiser and the state revenue department.
  • First week of October: the certified roll is delivered to the collector and the state.
  • March or April: the appraiser tells each authority how the Value Adjustment Board and corrections changed the roll.

The sequence explains why a TRIM notice shows proposed rates while the November bill shows adopted ones. Hearing dates for each authority's tentative budget appear on the TRIM notice, which is why the appraiser points rate complaints to those meetings. Keep the notice until the final bill arrives so you can compare the two.

Which exemptions can shrink a Sarasota County bill?

Homestead leads the list. You need to live in the house as your permanent home on January 1 and apply by March 1, although the office reviews late filings.

State figures describe homestead as up to $50,000, with $25,000 reaching school taxes. Afterward, Save Our Homes caps yearly growth at 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower. The appraiser's guide adds:

  • $5,000 for a widow or widower who has not remarried.
  • $5,000 for total and permanent disability.
  • $5,000 for blindness.
  • $5,000 for a veteran rated at least 10 percent disabled.
  • A homestead discount matching the VA percentage for veterans 65 and over with a permanent combat-related disability.

The collector says voter-approved Amendment 3 reaches the 2027 bill and leaves the 2026 bill as issued.

What follows when Sarasota County tax stays unpaid?

A tax certificate is sold, and eventually a certificate holder can ask for a deed. The collector's own wording is blunt: nonpayment can mean losing the property.

Certificates go on sale by June 1. Bidding is on interest, lowest wins, in quarter-point steps (s. 197.432). A deed application can come two years after April 1 of the issue year, with a $75 fee (s. 197.502). Winning bidders at the clerk's sale put down the larger of 5 percent or $200 (s. 197.542). Our tax deed page goes deeper.

An owner who is behind can pay through closing; the title agent asks the collector for the balance.

How is Sarasota County tax handled at a sale?

The buyer answers to the collector for the whole bill. Between buyer and seller, the closing statement credits the buyer for the months the seller held title, and nothing is wired to the collector as a seller part-payment.

Mailing matters afterward. Tell the appraiser where to send your notices once you move, and forward any real estate bill for a house you sold. Business equipment is different: if you held it on January 1, that year's bill remains yours. Recording details sit in our Sarasota County records guide.

More questions about Sarasota County, FL Property Tax Guide

When is Sarasota County property tax due?

Payment opens November 1, and the tax is delinquent after March 31. Early-pay discounts are 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February.

Where can I pay what I owe in Sarasota County?

Use the Sarasota County Tax Collector, through its website payment options or at offices in downtown Sarasota, Venice, North Port or Mid County.

Can I appeal my Sarasota County value?

Yes, with a Value Adjustment Board petition filed within 25 days of the TRIM mailing. A denied exemption allows 30 days from the denial letter.

Who pays the tax bill when a house sells?

The buyer answers to the collector. The seller's months are credited to the buyer on the closing statement.

What if I cannot pay in full?

Ask the collector about an installment plan, which needs an application by May 1 of the assessment year, or a homestead deferral on Form DR-570 by March 31.

Manatee County by the numbers

Who sends the Manatee County property tax bill?

Two Manatee County offices split the job: the property appraiser sets the value and the tax collector sends and collects the bill. In the collector's own words, the appraiser mails each year's TRIM notice, the collector mails the bill, and the money then flows to the local taxing authorities.

That split matters when you plan a sale. A question about an exemption, a parcel record or an assessed value goes to the Manatee County Property Appraiser. A question about what is owed, which discount applies or whether a certificate has been issued goes to the Manatee County Tax Collector. The clerk of court, at manateeclerk.com, keeps the Official Records where deeds and liens are recorded.

  • Property appraiser: parcel search, homestead e-filing, tangible personal property returns, TRIM notices, value reviews and Value Adjustment Board information.
  • Tax collector: bills, payments, installment plans, delinquent accounts and the annual tax certificate sale.
  • Clerk: recorded deeds, mortgages and liens, plus tax deed sales run for the county.

When do Manatee County property taxes have to be paid?

Manatee bills go out in early November, and the discount shrinks month by month until the gross amount comes due on March 31. The tax collector's page describes the 2026 roll as opening for collection with the November 2 mailing of 220,594 annual bills and informational notices.

The collector prints a month-by-month discount schedule, shown below for the 2026 bills. Its deadline rule has three parts: in person by 5:00 p.m., postmarked, or paid online by 11:59 p.m.

Discount periods for annual payment of 2026 Manatee County bills, as printed by the Tax Collector
Payment windowDiscount
November 2 to December 34%
December 4 to December 313%
January 1 to January 312%
February 1 to February 281%
March 1 to March 31No discount, last day before delinquency

The state's revenue department describes the same ladder.

Can Manatee County owners pay in installments?

Yes. Under section 197.222 of the Florida Statutes, the tax collector offers a plan of four quarterly payments, and the prior year's taxes must have exceeded $100 to join. State guidance puts the application deadline at May 1 of the assessment year.

Manatee's installment page prints this ladder:

  • June 30, first installment: 6% discount. A first installment paid by July 31 earns no discount.
  • September 30, second installment: 4.5% discount.
  • December 31, third installment: 3% discount.
  • March 31, fourth installment: no discount, and the last day before delinquency.

A seller partway through a plan year should tell the collector, since the closing payoff must cover whatever remains.

Does the Manatee County Tax Collector send reminders?

Yes. The collector offers free property tax email alerts that go out when taxes are due, when a payment posts, when a discount period is about to end and when taxes turn delinquent. A tutorial on its site explains the signup, and a separate management page lets you change or delete alerts.

Sellers can use this during a listing period. An alert on a parcel you are about to sell confirms that a payment posted before the closing agent orders a payoff. The collector's help center also carries checklists and answers for a visit to the office, and the office lists appointments on its website.

Escrow customers should confirm with their servicer who is paying, since a lender payment and an owner payment can overlap.

What happens if Manatee County taxes are not paid?

Anything unpaid after March 31 turns delinquent on April 1 and can pick up fees, interest and collection costs. From then on, the collector counts a payment only when it is received by the month's last business day, and postmarks do not count.

Florida's revenue department says certificates are sold on all unpaid items by June 1. Manatee's collector runs one annual sale and issues a certificate against any parcel still unpaid at that point, and paying the taxes cancels it. Certificates that nobody buys at the sale default to the county, and investors can buy those later from the county-held list.

A certificate is not a deed. Under section 197.502, a holder who waits out two years can ask for a tax deed, and the collector then lists the owner, lienholders and any contract-for-deed buyer for notice. A homestead property carries a higher opening bid, because one-half of the latest assessed value is added.

Which exemptions can lower a Manatee County bill?

Manatee owners apply for exemptions at the property appraiser, whose website offers electronic filing for homestead. Paper work is Form DR-501, and the state sets the first deadline in early March.

  • Homestead takes up to $50,000 off taxable value. Only the first $25,000 reduces school taxes.
  • Once a home is homesteaded, a state cap limits how fast its assessed value can climb. The state's published chart shows 2.7% for 2026.
  • Investment and second-home parcels face a different ceiling of 10 percent a year.
  • Portability lets a long-time homesteader carry that cap benefit to a new home, using Form DR-501T.
  • Homestead tax deferral goes through the tax collector, on Form DR-570, for owners who qualify.

Renting the home out or moving away ends homestead. The appraiser also takes reports of suspected exemption fraud through a confidential form.

How can a Manatee County owner dispute a value?

Begin with the August TRIM notice. The Manatee appraiser's homepage invites owners who believe a value is wrong to request a review of their property data and assessed value, and it links the Value Adjustment Board page for owners who want a formal hearing.

The state's revenue department puts the formal petition clock at 25 days from the notice date, with one of the DR-486 forms filed through the clerk. A turned-down exemption has its own 30-day clock. Both are counted from mailing dates printed on the paper you receive, so read it the day it arrives.

Business owners with tangible personal property report to the appraiser each year by April 1 and can request a 30-day extension from the same office.

What happens to the Manatee County tax bill at a sale?

An open bill rarely stops a sale. The closing agent can settle it out of what the buyer pays, and the title company can order the payoff. The collector confirms the account standing and any certificate. Treat a certificate as a title issue to settle early.

The state's deed stamp rate is 70 cents for each $100 of price, taken by the clerk as the deed goes on record. A cash sale shortens the timeline, since no lender appraisal or underwriting has to finish first, and it leaves the tax items as they were.

Where a parcel already carries back taxes or a deed application, get the figure from the collector in writing before the closing date is set.

Will the next owner pay the same Manatee County tax?

Probably not. The seller's capped assessment ends with the sale, and the parcel moves to full market-based value the next January. A buyer who budgets from the old bill can be surprised.

The appraiser's site publishes the preliminary roll, reports and earlier years' millage for anyone who wants to compare. For the rate on one address, ask the collector or appraiser, since each taxing authority sets its own.

More questions about Manatee County, FL Property Tax Guide

Who answers questions about a Manatee County tax bill?

The Manatee County Tax Collector handles bills, payments, installments and delinquent accounts. The property appraiser handles values and exemptions, and the clerk handles recorded deeds and liens.

Does Manatee County reward early payment?

Yes. The collector's schedule for the 2026 bills gives 4% from November 2 to December 3, 3% from December 4 to December 31, 2% in January and 1% in February. March has no discount.

When do Manatee County taxes become delinquent?

April 1. Unpaid parcels then go into the collector's yearly certificate sale, and paying the taxes cancels a certificate.

Can a Manatee County owner list a house while tax is unpaid?

Yes. Closing can absorb what is owed. The title company orders the payoff, and the collector confirms whether a certificate exists.

When must I apply for a homestead exemption in Manatee County?

Apply to the Manatee County Property Appraiser by the March 1 deadline. The home must be your permanent residence as of January 1, and the appraiser accepts electronic filing.

Seminole County by the numbers

Which offices handle Seminole County property tax?

In Seminole County the paper trail runs through three elected offices. One sets your value, one collects your money, and one files your deed.

Every Florida county elects the same officers, so a buyer from another county will recognize the setup. Knowing which counter to call saves days during a sale.

  • Seminole County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions and portability.
  • Seminole County Tax Collector: bills, installment plans, deferral requests and certificates.
  • Clerk of Court: recording the deed and stamp tax.

How big and how dense is Seminole County?

Seminole County held 491,884 people by the Bureau's mid-2025 estimate, packed onto about 309 square miles. In 2020 that meant 1,521.9 neighbors per square mile.

Census survey years 2020 to 2024 put a typical owned home at $386,900. Two in three households (66.2 percent) own, and midpoint household income was $85,761. Seniors account for 18.3 percent of the population, and Florida starts some tax breaks at 65.

Which Seminole County property tax dates should a seller know?

The appraiser's own date page lays out a yearly rhythm. What you own on January 1 is what gets assessed, and March 1 closes the window for homestead and agricultural filings.

Business owners file personal property returns by April 1. Mid-August brings the proposed-tax (TRIM) notice, with 25 days after mailing to petition the Value Adjustment Board. Those hearings start in November, just as bills go out.

  • Jan. 1: ownership and use fixed for the year.
  • Mar. 1: exemption and classification applications.
  • Apr. 1: business personal property returns.
  • Mid-Aug.: TRIM notice, then 25 days to petition.
  • Nov.: bills mailed, board hearings begin.

How does the early payment discount work in Seminole County?

The earlier a bill is paid, the bigger the cut. The appraiser's page lists 4 percent off for November, then 3, 2 and 1 percent through February.

A fall closing raises a practical question for the title agent: has the bill been paid, and at what discount? When the closing lands in a high-discount month, buyer and seller can agree in writing who keeps the savings. Taxes still open after April 1 are delinquent, and certificates go to auction by June 1. For installments, the state sets a May 1 application date in the assessment year; the Seminole tax collector can explain its own plan.

What happens to Save Our Homes and homestead when a Seminole County house sells?

A closing wipes the slate. Any transfer of title is a change of ownership, so the buyer's assessment jumps to market value the next January 1 and none of your cap carries over.

You, though, can take the savings with you. Portability moves the gap between market and assessed value, to a ceiling of $500,000, onto a new Florida homestead set up within three years. File it with the new homestead application by March 1. The yearly cap itself is the smaller of 3 percent or inflation, and it came to 2.7 percent for 2026.

Homestead lapses if you rent the place or move away. Call the appraiser before turning a Seminole County house into a rental.

What should a Seminole County buyer of an investment or second home expect?

Without homestead, the 10 percent annual limit on assessment growth for non-homestead property is what slows increases, and a change of ownership resets it.

Owners occupy 66.2 percent of homes, and the Census lists a typical rent of $1,783 for 2020 to 2024. A landlord who buys a house to rent never qualifies for homestead, so budget the full market-value tax from the first bill. A seller marketing a rental should expect buyers to ask for the property's tax history.

How can a Seminole County owner contest a value or a denied exemption?

Value disputes go to the Value Adjustment Board by petition inside the 25-day window printed on the proposed-tax notice. Ask the appraiser's office to review the property record first and bring any errors to its attention.

If the appraiser denies an exemption, a classification or a portability claim, the state gives 30 days from the date the denial letter was mailed. Hearings run from November. Skipping the window means waiting for the next cycle, which matters when a sale is pending and the buyer wants a lower carrying cost.

  • Check the notice for the exact deadline.
  • Gather recent sales and photos of defects.
  • Ask the title agent how a pending petition affects the closing.

What paperwork should a Seminole County seller gather before listing?

Pull the latest bill and the notice of proposed taxes so buyers see the exemptions and caps currently on the parcel. Confirm whether the property had homestead on January 1 and whether any deferral or installment plan is active, because each leaves a trail the title company will find.

Gather the deed, the payoff letter from any lender, and any open permits. If the seller plans to port the Save Our Homes difference, copy the TRIM notice that shows it, since the new county's appraiser will want the amount. Taking these steps early shortens the time between contract and closing.

What do the deed and recording cost in Seminole County?

Florida levies seventy cents per hundred dollars of price. Seminole is not Miami-Dade, the lone county with a different schedule. A loan the buyer assumes counts toward the price.

Everyone on the deed is answerable, so the purchase agreement should name who funds it. Recording starts at $5.00 for page one, then $4.00 a page, before technology add-ons. Probated estates get a break: a personal representative's deed is listed as not taxable.

What if the Seminole County tax bill is unpaid when you sell?

An open bill will not stop a closing; the title company deducts it from your proceeds. A certificate that has already sold is bigger, since its investor needs paying too.

Certificates go to the bidder accepting the lowest interest, in quarter-point steps. The investor may not demand payment from the owner for two years after April 1 of the issue year. A homestead with under $250 overdue is protected: the county takes that certificate rather than an auction. Before listing, ask for a payoff.

  • Payoff statement from the collector.
  • Certificate search by the title agent.
  • Confirmation of any lender escrow.

Can Seminole County owners get help with the tax bill?

Yes. Homestead takes up to $50,000 off taxable value: the first $25,000 reaches school taxes, and a second slice, indexed to inflation, applies only to non-school taxes on assessed value over $50,000.

Seniors may get more where a local ordinance allows and income fits the limit; ask the appraiser what Seminole has adopted. A veteran rated 10 percent or more disabled gets $5,000 off assessed value, and a total, permanent disability can erase homestead tax. Deferral requests go to the tax collector by March 31, covering tax above 5 percent of household income.

More questions about Seminole County, FL Property Tax Guide

Does a Seminole County sale trigger a reassessment?

Yes. The next January 1 the house is assessed at market value, and the seller's caps and exemptions stay behind.

When are Seminole County tax bills mailed?

In November, from the tax collector. Proposed-tax notices come first, in mid-August.

Where is Seminole County homestead filed?

At the property appraiser's office, by March 1, using Form DR-501. The home must already be your permanent residence on January 1.

How long is the Seminole County appeal window?

You get 25 days from the August notice. The petition, on a DR-486 form, goes through the clerk to the Value Adjustment Board.

Who pays stamp tax on a Seminole County sale?

The law makes every party to the deed liable, so the sale contract should name who pays. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, handled by the clerk when the deed is recorded.

Marion County by the numbers

Which Marion County offices handle your bill?

One office values, one bills, and one keeps the records: the appraiser, the tax collector and the clerk of court. All three work out of the Ocala area, and each has its own website.

  • Marion County Property Appraiser: parcel and sales search, a property tax estimator, homestead e-filing, TPP return e-filing, a page of important dates and information on the TRIM notice and the Value Adjustment Board. The office lists its address as 501 SE 25th Avenue, Ocala, with walk-ins welcome or appointments available.
  • Marion County Tax Collector: pay taxes online, search the tax roll, apply for a tax deed online, buy county-held certificates, and read about installment plans, deferred taxes and delinquent taxes. The main office is at the McPherson Complex, 503 SE 25th Avenue, Ocala, and the office runs eight locations across the county.
  • Marion County Clerk of Court and Comptroller: the county recorder, the keeper of Official Records, and the office that handles tax deed sales and the Value Adjustment Board.

Pick the right door before you call: value and exemptions belong to the appraiser, and amounts owed belong to the collector.

When are Marion County property taxes due?

The tax collector's payment page lists November 1 as the due date and April 1 as the delinquency date for Marion County taxes and assessments. Florida allows a discount for early payment starting in November.

Early payment discounts on the Marion County Tax Collector's payment page
Month paidDiscount
November4%

MarchGross amount, no discount

On or after April 1 the amount you owe depends on the day the collector receives your payment, not the postmark. The office also notes that taxes are payable even if a bill never arrives, and that a mortgage company paying from escrow may request the bill and the owner then gets an informational copy. The collector's notice for 2026 states that the real estate, tangible personal property and railroad rolls opened for collection.

What can Marion County homeowners do about the bill?

Several options exist before a bill turns delinquent. The collector's property tax menu lists an installment plan and deferred taxes, and the state describes the rules behind both.

  • Installment plan: section 197.222 lets owners prepay and pay in installments, with May 1 as the application deadline.
  • Homestead deferral: Form DR-570 goes to the tax collector by March 31. Deferral covers the portion above 5 percent of last year's household income, and a permanent resident aged 65 or older may defer the part above 3 percent.
  • Partial payments: before the delinquency date these are at the tax collector's discretion under section 197.374.
  • Escrow: a lender holding escrow can request your bill, so check with your servicer before paying twice.

Check with the collector on which of these still fit a parcel headed to sale, since a plan tied to the current owner may not carry to a buyer.

What tools does the Marion County appraiser offer owners?

The appraiser's site lists a property tax estimator, a mortgage estimate letter request, a mailing address change form and a homestead e-file page. It also lists a form for reporting property damage and a confidential form for reporting suspected homestead fraud.

Owners who run a business or rent out a property can file a tangible personal property return electronically and request an extension. The office also posts frequently asked questions, a property taxpayer's bill of rights, reports, digital data requests and a code list. These are the first stops for an owner who wants to understand a bill before a sale.

  • Estimator: a way to model taxes for a parcel before you commit to a price.
  • Mortgage estimate letter: a document lenders and buyers ask about.
  • Address change: keeps the TRIM notice and bill reaching you after you move.

Walk-ins are welcome at the Ocala office, and appointments can be booked ahead through the website.

How does Marion County value homes for tax?

Ownership and condition on January 1 set each year's value. Exemption and classification paperwork goes in by March 1, and business personal property returns follow on April 1.

Homestead removes up to $50,000 from taxable value, with school taxes touched only by the first $25,000. The appraiser's e-file page handles the application, which must show the home was your permanent residence on January 1.

After the first year, a state cap slows increases on a homestead's assessed value, and the state's chart shows 2.7% for 2026. Other property has a separate 10 percent ceiling. A sale or other change of ownership resets the parcel to market-based value the next January, with exceptions for spouses and some transfers at death.

The TRIM notice arrives in August. Petitions to the Value Adjustment Board run through the clerk, and the clerk's office announced in July 2026 that those petitions can be e-filed.

What else is on a Marion County tax bill?

The collector's property tax menu separates ad valorem taxes from non-ad valorem assessments, and its payment page speaks of taxes and assessments together. A bill can therefore carry more than the county's general levy. The menu also offers a tax bill explanation and a page of current tax payment methods.

Questions split into two lists, one for current tax and one for delinquent tax. The office phone is (352) 368-8200, and its website lists eight county locations with lobby cameras so you can check the line before you leave home.

  • Pay online: search the tax roll by owner or parcel and pay from the same page.
  • Deferred taxes: a menu page covers the homestead deferral rules.
  • Tax certificates and deed sales: the collector's page and the clerk's page both cover these.

Read the explanation page before assuming a line item is wrong, then bring any real error to the right office.

What happens to unpaid Marion County taxes?

Delinquency starts April 1, and the state says certificates are sold on all unpaid items by June 1. A certificate buyer pays the bill and earns interest, but cannot press the owner for payment for two years.

The collector's menu points owners to later steps as well: an online tax deed application, online purchase of county-held certificates, and a page on delinquent taxes. The clerk lists tax deed sales and lands available for taxes among its departments. A homestead parcel carries a higher opening bid at a deed sale.

Clear a certificate early, since the amount only grows.

Can a Marion County house with tax owed still sell?

Yes. Begin with the collector's exact balance. The title company can take it out of the money the buyer brings to the table, so a sale does not need a clean tax record first.

The state's deed stamp rate is 70 cents for each $100 of price, and the clerk takes it at recording. The buyer's first bill can also come in higher than yours, because the seller's cap ends with the sale.

For an inherited house, or one behind by several years, a written payoff should come before any offer is accepted. The clerk's Property Alert Service sends a message when paperwork hits the records under your parcel or name.

The Marion County Tax Collector sends and collects the bill. The property appraiser sets the value and mails the TRIM notice in August.

When do Marion County property taxes become delinquent?

April 1. After that date the amount due depends on when the collector receives your payment, and the postmark does not count.

Can I apply for homestead exemption in Marion County after March 1?

Do I need to pay all back taxes before selling in Marion County?

Collier County by the numbers

Which Collier County offices handle my property tax bill?

Billing and payment sit with the tax collector. Values and exemptions belong to the appraiser, while appeals and tax deed auctions run through the clerk's office. A call to the wrong office costs time.

The tax collector's mailing address is 3291 Tamiami Trail East, Naples, FL 34112. Property tax questions go to propertytax@colliertax.com or 239-252-8171. The Property Appraiser can be reached at (239) 252-8141 for value and exemption questions.

What does paying early save in Collier County, and when is a bill late?

Bills are payable in November, and paying early earns a discount that shrinks each month. The tax collector's page starts the discount at 4% in November and drops it a point each month until it ends at 1% in February. The gross amount is due in March, and the bill goes delinquent in April.

Collier County payment months, as printed by the tax collector
Month paidDiscount
November4% off
December3% off
January2% off
February1% off
MarchGross amount due
AprilDelinquent

The collector does not accept post-dated checks. Florida's revenue department notes that certificate sales on unpaid items finish by June 1. All offices close on listed holidays, including Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and the day after, and on one training day in October.

How does the Collier County assessment and notice cycle work?

The appraiser values every parcel as of each New Year's Day. In mid-August the appraiser mails a TRIM notice, the formal proposal of next year's tax.

  • August: TRIM notice arrives, listing proposed values and tax.
  • September and October: local taxing authorities hold budget hearings.
  • November: the tax collector sends bills.

Other property faces a 10 percent yearly ceiling on assessed growth. Read the TRIM notice closely, because it is the notice that starts the appeal clock.

Where do I contest a Collier County property value?

Petitions go to the Value Adjustment Board, whose clerk is the Collier County clerk and comptroller. An assessment appeal is due within 25 days after the appraiser mails the TRIM notice, and the 2026 petition deadline of September 11 has passed.

Other petitions run on different clocks. The clerk's table lists these:

  • Exemption or classification denial: 30 days after the appraiser mails the denial, with all denials mailed by July 1
  • Tax deferral denial: 30 days after the tax collector mails the denial
  • Portability and change of ownership or control: 25 days after the TRIM notice

The filing fee is $50.00 per petition per parcel for most types and $15.00 for a portability petition. The board has two county commissioners, one school board member and two citizen members, and special magistrates hear the cases and recommend decisions. Late filing needs a good cause statement.

How should I read a Collier County tax bill?

The tax collector bills ad valorem tax, which means tax according to worth, on real estate and on a business's tangible personal property. One mill equals a dollar of tax on each thousand dollars of taxable value, and every taxing authority sets its own rate, so the county, school district, city and special districts all appear on one bill.

Three checks help before you pay or sell:

  • Match the parcel number and legal owner on the bill to your deed.
  • Confirm the homestead exemption shows on the bill if you applied by March 1.
  • See whether any non-ad valorem charge appears, because those are assessments rather than value-based tax.

The tax collector's site links to a tax search where you can pull a notice or receipt, and a mortgage lender that pays from escrow should still be checked against that record.

What homestead and exemption rules matter for a Collier County owner?

Homestead applications reach the appraiser by that March date, and the house must be your permanent home on January 1. The exemption reaches $50,000, where the first $25,000 reduces every levy, school tax included, and the next $25,000 reduces only non-school levies on value above $50,000.

Under Save Our Homes, a homestead's assessed value may climb each year by the smaller of 3 percent and the CPI change, and the state's chart prints 2.7% for 2026. After a sale the parcel goes back to full market-based value the next New Year's Day, which can make a buyer's bill very different from the seller's. Portability lets an owner bring accumulated savings along to a replacement Florida home, provided it begins inside a three-year window after the old one ended.

Homestead protection ends if the home is rented or stops being the permanent residence. Senior owners may qualify for added local exemptions, and disabled veterans have separate benefits. The appraiser can say which apply to your Naples or Marco Island address.

Can I delay or spread out Collier County property tax?

Yes, through tax deferral and the installment program, both listed on the tax collector's property tax page. Deferring homestead tax takes Form DR-570, filed with the collector by March 31 after the assessment year, and covers the part above 5 percent of household income.

A permanent resident 65 or older may defer the part above 3 percent. The installment plan under section 197.222 needs an application by the May 1 cutoff in the year of assessment. Confirm current terms with the collector, since deferred tax accrues interest and carries a lien.

Who settles the Collier County tax bill at a sale?

Unpaid current-year tax is settled at closing, normally by the closing agent from the proceeds. Request a payoff figure for your closing date, and confirm earlier years show paid.

If taxes stay unpaid, the county sells a certificate. Once two years have run from the April 1 following issue, the holder can file for a tax deed, and the clerk then runs the auction. A homestead parcel's opening bid adds one-half of the latest assessment. At the clerk's tax deed auction, a winning bidder pays within 24 hours, so a delinquent house can be lost quickly, and a seller with unpaid years should settle them before listing. For recording costs on your own sale, see the Collier County property records guide.

Where do I find Collier County tax deed and foreclosure listings?

The Collier Clerk posts both a tax deeds list and a foreclosure sale list on its records search page. The tax deeds list covers properties where the tax collector sold certificates for delinquent real estate taxes.

State law lets the tax collector award each certificate to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest rate, in quarter-percent steps, and unsold certificates go to the county at the maximum rate. The certificate holder may not contact the owner for payment until two years from the first April 1 after issue. A homeowner with a small delinquency has options before that point, since payment to the tax collector redeems the certificate, so ask the collector's office for a payoff early rather than waiting for a sale notice.

More questions about Collier County, FL Property Tax Guide

What date marks Collier County tax as late?

Lateness begins in April, on the state's April 1 date. The gross amount is due in March, with discounts only from November through February.

What early-payment discounts does Collier County offer?

Savings shrink from 4% in the first month of payment through 1% in the last, which is February. After that the full gross amount applies, starting in March.

How long is the window to contest a Collier County assessment?

Petitions are due within 25 days after the appraiser mails the TRIM notice. The 2026 deadline was September 11, and most petitions carry a $50.00 filing fee.

Does Collier County accept post-dated checks for property tax?

No. The tax collector states that post-dated checks are not accepted for property tax bills.

What is the mailing address for Collier County tax payments?

Mail it to the Collier County Tax Collector, 3291 Tamiami Trail East, Naples, FL 34112. Questions go to 239-252-8171.

Due dates and discounts

  • Real estate taxes delinquent April 1; 3% minimum mandatory charge imposed April 1 and an advertising charge added in May. Tax certificate sale conducted online at lienhub.com (lienhub.com/county/alachua/certsale/); minimum 5% interest unless zero bid; certificate valid seven years; tax deed application after two years; unsold certificates struck to the county carry 18%.

Alachua County by the numbers

Which offices touch an Alachua County tax bill?

Three elected offices share the job. One values property and rules on exemptions, one sends and collects the bill, and one records deeds and takes the documentary stamp tax.

The Alachua County Tax Collector's site explains that the Property Appraiser prepares the real estate and tangible personal property rolls, which fix ownership, mailing address, legal description and value. Taxes equal taxable value, after exemptions, times the millage rate set by each taxing authority. If no bill arrives in November, the Tax Collector's page gives (352) 374-5236 as the number to call.

  • Value, ownership and exemptions: Alachua County Property Appraiser (acpafl.org), which also offers a free Title Alert for ownership changes.
  • Bills, payment plans and deferral: Alachua County Tax Collector.
  • Recorded deeds and doc stamps: the circuit court clerk, who also conducts foreclosure and tax deed sales.

When are Alachua County property taxes due?

Statements usually go out around the start of November, the gross amount is due at the end of March, and April 1 starts delinquency.

Early payment schedule printed by the Alachua County Tax Collector
When the payment is postmarkedReduction in the bill
During NovemberFour percent off
During DecemberThree percent off
During JanuaryTwo percent off
During FebruaryOne percent off
During MarchFull amount, no reduction

Discounts follow the postmark. Once a bill is delinquent, the office says a 3 percent minimum charge is added on April 1 and an advertising charge in May, and the date the payment is received controls the amount.

What are the Alachua County millage rates?

Alachua County's own 2026 TRIM explainer lists a 2025 countywide millage of 7.6000 mills and a proposed 2026 rollback rate of 7.2107 mills, which it describes as the tenth straight year of a lower countywide rate.

Treat the 2026 figure as proposed until the final adopted rate appears on your bill or the Tax Collector's site. The same article notes that a TRIM notice carries several taxing authorities, so the county is only one line on it. Homes inside a city add that city's levy, and the explainer says that for Gainesville certain charges once on monthly utility bills now appear on the notice.

Some owners in unincorporated areas also see a Law Enforcement Municipal Services Taxing Unit line, which the county lists at a proposed 3.5678 mills. Non-ad valorem items such as county fire, solid waste and stormwater are charged by assessment, not millage.

Which exemptions and deadlines should an Alachua County owner know?

Exemption applications go to the Alachua County appraiser's office and are due March 1. Per the Florida Department of Revenue, the home must be your permanent residence by the preceding January 1.

  • Homestead takes up to $50,000 off. The first $25,000 reaches every levy, school included, and the second $25,000 reaches only non-school levies on value over $50,000.
  • Save Our Homes holds annual growth in assessed value to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is less. The state chart prints 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • A sale or foreclosure sends assessed value back up to just value each following January, though spousal transfers are among the exceptions.
  • Portability moves the accumulated benefit to a new homestead, if it is set up inside three years of the old one being given up.
  • Disabled veterans, deployed servicemembers and seniors can qualify for added relief. A city or county ordinance sets the senior exemption.

Renting out a homestead ends the exemption, so a seller who moved out should ask the Property Appraiser how the status stands.

Can Alachua County owners pay in installments or defer tax?

Yes. The Tax Collector offers a quarterly installment plan and a homestead tax deferral, each with its own rules.

Installments require prior year taxes above $100, and the application window closes April 30. Discounts printed on the page are 6 percent on the June 30 payment, 4.5 percent on the September 30 payment, 3 percent on the December 31 payment and none on the March 31 payment.

For deferral, the property must qualify for homestead, the primary mortgage cannot exceed 70 percent of assessed value, and the form is due at the end of March. Interest accrues on deferred tax at no more than 7 percent a year, and the whole balance falls due when homestead eligibility, use or ownership changes. That means a sale triggers payoff at closing.

What should landlords in Alachua County know about tax on rentals?

Rental houses carry two exposures: the real estate bill and tangible personal property tax on furniture, fixtures and equipment inside a rental.

The Tax Collector explains that the Property Appraiser values tangible property as of January 1 and that a return that arrives by April 1 earns an exemption of up to $25,000. Late or missing returns bring penalties and loss of that exemption. Unpaid tangible tax turns delinquent April 1 with a $10 fee and 1.5 percent monthly interest, and a 20 percent collection fee is added May 1.

Landlords selling a rental should note that, per the same page, the tangible tax lien follows the property and survives a sale, and any proration between buyer and seller is handled at closing. Owners with rentals can also ask the county's waste collection office (352-338-3233) about assessment discounts for a vacant residential rental.

What happens when Alachua County taxes go unpaid?

The Tax Collector advertises delinquent parcels, then runs an online certificate sale at lienhub.com by early June, with bidding opening at 18 percent and dropping.

The winning bidder pays the tax and earns interest, and the certificate becomes a first lien on the property. After at least two years from delinquency, the page says, the certificate holder can seek a tax deed, and an unredeemed property goes to public auction. To clear a certificate, the owner pays the Tax Collector the tax, interest, costs and charges.

Florida law bars a certificate holder from demanding payment from the owner for two years after April 1 of the issue year. A seller with a certificate on the house can usually clear it from sale proceeds, and the payoff figure comes from the Tax Collector's office.

How is tax handled when an Alachua County house sells?

The bill goes to whoever is on the roll, and the two sides settle the split at the closing table.

Deeds carry Florida's documentary stamp tax, 70 cents on each $100 of consideration outside Miami-Dade, paid to the clerk when the deed is recorded. Every party to the deed is liable, whatever the contract says about who pays. A buyer whose mortgage pays taxes through escrow gets the bill through the lender, and the Tax Collector notes that lenders must pay inside the 4 percent window.

The county counted 290,028 residents in July 2025, and owners live in 54.1 percent of homes, a low share that points to a large renter base. QuickFacts lists a $288,800 median value. With college-town turnover, ask the title company early for a tax and lien search.

More questions about Alachua County, FL Property Tax Guide

When does Alachua County mail property tax bills?

Around the start of November. If yours does not arrive, call the Tax Collector at (352) 374-5236.

How long can I wait before Alachua County taxes go delinquent?

Pay by the end of March. After that, a 3 percent minimum charge applies from April 1.

Is the 2026 Alachua County millage final?

The county's explainer calls it proposed. It shows 7.2107 mills as the proposed 2026 rollback rate against 7.6000 in 2025. Confirm the adopted rate with the Tax Collector or your bill.

Does selling my Alachua County home end my homestead?

A sale counts as a change of ownership, so assessed value returns to just value the next January. The new owner files a fresh homestead application.

Can an Alachua County owner with unpaid tax still sell?

Yes. The title company can pay delinquent tax and any certificate out of the buyer's funds. Request from the Tax Collector the payoff amount before the closing date.
