Bay County by the numbers

Who is responsible for each part of a Bay County bill?

The Bay County Property Appraiser sets the value and decides exemptions, local governments set millage rates, and the Bay County Tax Collector prints, mails and collects the bill.

The Tax Collector's real estate page lays out the order. The appraiser assesses, the County Commission and other levying bodies set millage, the appraiser builds the roll, and the certified roll then moves to the Tax Collector. Any change to name, mailing address, location or assessed value has to go through the Property Appraiser, not the Tax Collector. Owners who pay through escrow should know the mortgage company requests the original bill and the owner gets a copy.

  • Property Appraiser: value questions and TRIM notice questions, (850) 248-8401, as printed on the Value Adjustment Board page.
  • Tax Collector: payment, delinquent tax and tax deferral.
  • Clerk of Court and Comptroller: official records, plus the clerk work for the Value Adjustment Board.

What is the yearly tax calendar in Bay County?

The yearly cycle tracks the Florida Department of Revenue calendar, and each step belongs to one office.

  • January 1: the date that fixes value and ownership for the tax year.
  • March 1: exemption and classification applications are due.
  • August: the Property Appraiser mails the TRIM notice of proposed taxes. A value challenge goes to the court clerk within 25 days of that notice.
  • September and October: taxing authorities hold tentative budget hearings, with final budget and millage hearings in October and November.
  • November: the Tax Collector sends the bill.
  • April 1: unpaid taxes become delinquent, and certificates are sold by June 1.

For a Bay County house listed in spring, that means the prior year's bill may still be open at closing while the new roll is being built.

Where are the Bay County Tax Collector's offices?

The Tax Collector lists four service offices, and a Bay County bill can only be paid at its own offices.

  • Panama City: 850 W. 11th St., Panama City, FL 32401.
  • Panama City Beach: 10520 Hutchison Blvd., Panama City Beach, FL 32407.
  • Lynn Haven: 700 Florida Ave., Lynn Haven, FL 32444.
  • Callaway: 805 S. Tyndall Pkwy, Callaway, FL 32404.

Bring the property tax notice or the property address. Delinquent balances must be paid in certified funds, which the page lists as cash, a cashier's check, a money order or a credit card. Appointments can be booked through the Tax Collector's site, and online payment is offered too.

What does a Bay County seller do before listing?

Start with the tax notice and the Property Appraiser's record for the parcel, then compare the owner name to the deed. A name that does not match, or a mailing address that is out of date, means the bill may never reach you, and the Tax Collector's page says changes to name or address must be made through the Property Appraiser.

Next, check whether non-ad valorem charges for paving, stormwater or solid waste are on the bill, since those are billed beside the tax and are owed at closing like the rest. A house that sat vacant or was repaired after storm damage can have an assessed value that no longer matches its condition, which is a reason to review the TRIM notice in August rather than wait for the bill.

Finally, ask the title company for a lien and tax search. Panama City, Panama City Beach, Lynn Haven and Callaway all sit in the same county tax system, so the same offices answer for any of them.

When are Bay County taxes due, and what discounts apply?

Bills usually reach mailboxes by the first of November, the deadline is March 31, and April 1 starts delinquency. The discount months run November through February.

  • November: 4 percent off.
  • December: 3 percent off.
  • January: 2 percent off.
  • February: 1 percent off.

Non-ad valorem assessments, mainly paving, stormwater and solid waste collection, follow the same calendar and carry the same early payment discounts. They come from local governments and are certified to the Tax Collector, so a question about one goes to the government that levied it.

How do I file for homestead or other exemptions in Bay County?

Apply through the Bay County Property Appraiser before the March 1 cutoff, having made the home your permanent residence by January 1.

The Tax Collector's page is explicit that exemptions go through the Property Appraiser. State guidance prices the homestead exemption at up to $50,000: school taxes see only the first $25,000, while the second $25,000 reduces non-school levies on value above $50,000.

  • Save Our Homes keeps yearly assessed value growth at 3 percent or CPI, whichever is smaller, and the state chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • After a sale or foreclosure, the property is revalued at just value each following January.
  • A seller who rents the home out loses homestead, with a limited carve-out for servicemembers.

The Value Adjustment Board page adds that a timely filed homestead application that was denied needs no petition fee, while one received after March 1 does.

How do I dispute a Bay County valuation?

Petition the Bay County Value Adjustment Board. The 2026 petition deadline fell on September 8, 2026, and the next filing window follows the TRIM notices mailed the following August.

Bay County Value Adjustment Board filing details as printed on its site
ItemDetail
Filing fee$50.00, non-refundable
Online filingAdds a 3.5% non-refundable card processing fee
Extra contiguous parcels or accounts$5.00 for each after the first
Mail address for checks225 McKenzie Avenue, Panama City, FL 32401

Section 194.014, quoted on that page, requires a petitioner contesting value to pay all non-ad valorem assessments and at least 75 percent of the ad valorem taxes, less the discount, before the taxes go delinquent. If the partial payment is missed, the board must deny the petition by April 20.

What can a Bay County owner do about a bill they cannot pay?

Florida offers a homestead tax deferral through Form DR-570, filed with the Tax Collector by March 31. It covers tax above 5 percent of household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident aged 65 or older.

Section 197.222 of state law also allows an installment plan, with applications due May 1 of the assessment year. Ask the Bay County Tax Collector which plans it runs and what the payoff is.

Unpaid tax turns delinquent April 1, and state law requires certificates to be sold by June 1. Two years after April 1 of the issue year, the holder is allowed to seek a tax deed. A seller in that spot can usually settle the balance out of the price paid at the table.

What happens to Bay County tax when the house sells?

Whoever holds title on the roll receives the bill, and the year is divided between buyer and seller when the deal closes. Have the title company pull the current bill, any non-ad valorem balance and the discount month in effect.

A deed documentary stamp tax applies at 70 cents per $100 of consideration outside Miami-Dade, collected by the clerk at recording. Everyone named on a taxable deed is liable, even if the contract assigns payment to one side.

A buyer starts with no inherited cap once the next January arrives, so the seller's tax history is a poor guide to what the buyer will owe. Selling an inherited or storm-worn house works the same way: clear liens and unpaid balances first, then record the deed in Panama City.

More questions about Bay County, FL Property Tax Guide

What is the Bay County property tax due date?

March 31 is the due date, and April 1 starts delinquency. Notices normally go out by early November.

How much is the Bay County early payment discount?

Four percent in November, shrinking by a point each month through February, with nothing off in March.

Where is the Bay County Tax Collector?

Panama City is the central location, with additional offices in Panama City Beach, Lynn Haven and Callaway. Bring your notice or property address.

Can I still file a 2026 value petition in Bay County?

The 2026 deadline was September 8, 2026, and later petitions are treated as late filed and reviewed. Questions go to the Property Appraiser at (850) 248-8401.

Does a Bay County buyer keep my Save Our Homes cap?

No. Ownership changes reset the property to just value the following January, with narrow exceptions such as some spousal transfers.

Charlotte County by the numbers

What should a Charlotte County property owner know first?

One combined notice arrives each year from the county tax collector, built on values the property appraiser set. Charlotte County collects in arrears, which means a November bill pays for the calendar year that is nearly over.

The collector describes two kinds of charge on the notice. Ad valorem tax follows value. Non-ad valorem assessments follow things like square footage or the number of units, and the office names stormwater, fire and rescue and solid waste as examples. County commissioners, the School Board, city commissioners and other authorities set millage, while the appraiser does not.

About 217,212 people lived in Charlotte County in 2025 by Census estimate, and 40.9% were 65 or older. Of 131,960 housing units, 83.8% have owner occupants, and the county sprawls across 681.12 land square miles. Median home value is $328,900 (2020 to 2024 survey). Permits issued in 2025 totaled 3,015.

Which Charlotte County offices handle which part of the bill?

Each office has a lane: the appraiser sets value and approves exemptions, the collector issues and takes payment on the bill, and the clerk runs tax deed sales.

  • Property appraiser: values, exemptions and homestead applications, phone (941) 743-1593 for exemption questions on a notice and (941) 743-1498 for assessed value questions.
  • Tax collector: bills, discounts, installment plans and delinquent taxes, phone (941) 743-1350.
  • Clerk's office: online tax deed sales, phone (941) 637-2130.

Installment applications are mailed to the collector at 18500 Murdock Circle, Port Charlotte, FL 33948. If you sold the house, send the bill on to the buyer or return it to the collector.

What dates and discounts apply to a Charlotte County bill?

Statements go out by the first of November, and paying early earns a sliding discount that starts at 4% and shrinks one point a month.

Charlotte County billing and collection steps
StepDetail
Statements mailedBy November 1
Early paymentFour points off in the first month, then one fewer each month through February

Where an escrow account pays the tax, the collector's page says the mortgage company should request the bill and the owner receives a copy for information.

How does the installment plan work in Charlotte County?

Send the application to the collector before May 1; the first payment is due by June 30.

Skip the first payment and the plan is cancelled, leaving the whole tax due by March 31. After the first payment you owe participation for the year, and enrollment renews on its own. The office says that to leave, you simply ignore the June bill and wait for the November notice at the gross amount. Anything unpaid on April 1 is treated as a delinquent bill.

Installments one and two are each a quarter of the estimate. Numbers three and four add half of any true-up each, so the last two bills can differ from the first two.

What happens if Charlotte County taxes go unpaid?

Real estate tax left unpaid turns delinquent April 1 and heads to a certificate sale by early June.

Delinquent parcels are advertised in a local paper weekly for three weeks, and advertising and collection fees land on the delinquent account. The sale is a reverse auction on the interest rate starting at 18%, and the lowest bidder gets the certificate, a first lien. A certificate is valid for seven years. Once two years pass from the delinquency date, the holder can seek a tax deed, and the clerk conducts the sale online.

  • Only cashier's checks, money orders or cash are accepted for delinquent taxes.
  • A deed sale opens at a total that includes a $75.00 collector fee, a $150.00 ownership and encumbrance report, a $60.00 clerk fee and a $59.00 web fee, plus taxes, interest and half the assessed value.
  • Paying all taxes, costs and interest before the deed is issued stops the sale.

How does homestead work for Charlotte County owners?

The county appraiser takes homestead applications until March 1 of the year you want the benefit, and you must live there as a permanent resident by New Year's Day.

State law gives up to $50,000 off. School taxes see only the first $25,000, while the added $25,000 applies on value above $50,000, for non-school levies. Later growth in assessed value is capped at 3 percent or CPI, and the state's chart prints a 2.7 percent cap for 2026. Selling resets the figure to full just value the following January 1.

Renting the home out ends homestead, except for the servicemember rule in the statutes. Seniors and veterans may qualify for extra benefits, and the appraiser's office rules on each case.

How do incomes and rents look in Charlotte County?

Median household income is $69,952 in 2024 dollars, and per capita income is $42,592. Renters pay about $1,464, and monthly owner costs run $1,773 with a mortgage and $678 without one.

Just 43.2% of people 16 and older work or look for work, a figure that tracks the county's age profile. QuickFacts also lists 19,280 veterans, 4,601 employer establishments in 2023 and 90,542 households of 2.17 people on average.

For a seller, the ownership numbers matter most. Because 87.3% of residents stayed put over the past year, many carry capped assessments, while a buyer starts from the reset value.

What other charges does the Charlotte County collector handle?

The collector also bills tangible personal property tax, which falls on the furniture and equipment of a business or rental property and on structural additions to mobile homes. These bills go out with the real estate bills and earn the same early discounts.

On April 1 tangible tax goes delinquent and picks up 1.5% interest, a $2.00 late fee and advertising costs. Warrants are issued before April 30 on unpaid accounts, and within 30 days the office applies to the circuit court for an order allowing levy and seizure.

  • Redeeming a certificate on or after June 1 adds a $6.25 redemption fee.
  • Paper bills can be replaced with email bills through the office's Bill Express sign-up, though an undeliverable bill does not extend a discount period.
  • Email addresses given for e-billing become public records.

How is the tax handled when you sell in Charlotte County?

Your closing agent divides the year's tax between the two parties and takes anything owed, delinquent amounts included, out of the proceeds.

Call (941) 743-1350 for a payoff and ask whether a certificate was sold, since a holder has to be repaid with interest before the lien clears. The deed carries the state's 70 cents per $100 stamp tax, paid at recording, with every party to the document liable.

A buyer of a homesteaded house will not inherit the seller's exemption or capped value. Ask both offices for figures on your parcel.

More questions about Charlotte County, FL Property Tax Guide

Which office mails the Charlotte County bill?

The Charlotte County Tax Collector mails it on or before November 1, using the roll certified by the property appraiser. Call (941) 743-1350 with billing questions.

What is the early payment discount in Charlotte County?

Four percent off in November, falling one point each month to 1% in February. March brings none, and delinquency starts April 1.

Can Charlotte County taxes be paid in installments?

Yes, when the estimate exceeds $100 and the application is in before May 1. Four payments follow, ending March 31.

When can a tax certificate turn into a tax deed application?

Two years after the tax went delinquent. A certificate lasts seven years, and redemption is possible until a deed is issued.

Where do I file for homestead in Charlotte County?

Send it to the county appraiser by March 1. That office decides eligibility, and the collector only bills.

Citrus County by the numbers

How big is Citrus County and who lives there?

Citrus County spans 581.92 land square miles, and its 2025 population estimate is 171,666, up 11.6% from 153,843 in 2020.

Seniors make up 38.1% of the population and children 14.2%. Owners occupy 85.2% of the 90,919 housing units, and permits issued in 2025 numbered 2,102.

The survey's median home value is $245,500. Owner costs run $1,354 a month for those with a mortgage and $447 for those without. Households bring in a median $56,546, and 13.5% of people live in poverty. Income per person is $36,732, spread over 71,291 households. Among residents under 65, 15.6% report a disability, which makes a tax bill weigh on fixed incomes.

Which Citrus County office does what?

Valuation and exemption rulings come from the property appraiser here, while the tax collector sends the bill, takes payment and sells certificates.

  • Property appraiser: homestead and other exemption applications, portability, agricultural classification and the August TRIM notice. The office phone is (352) 341-6600.
  • Tax collector: bills, discounts, installment applications and delinquent tax advertising.
  • Clerk: files the deed at closing and collects stamp tax.

The appraiser's site sets March 1 as the filing cutoff for portability, exemptions, classifications and assessment reductions, and April 1 for tangible personal property returns. Both dates repeat every year. Owners who buy a home after January 1 are encouraged to pre-file for the next year.

What are the Citrus County tax discounts and due dates?

The 4% November discount is the best of the year; it falls by one point each month, and March carries the gross amount, due by March 31.

Can I pay Citrus County property tax in installments?

Quarterly payments are allowed, spreading the bill over the year. The application must reach the collector by April 30, and eligibility turns on prior year taxes above $100.

June 30 is the first due date, at 6% off, and a payment taken between July 1 and July 30 gets no discount. September 30 brings the second at 4.5% off and December 31 the third at 3% off. The fourth, due March 31, has no discount. If the first payment is missed, the plan ends and the full tax is due by March 31.

Payments one and two follow last year's bill. Ownership, value or exemption changes show up in payments three and four. Enrollment renews itself each year, per the collector. Buyers taking over an active plan should check with the office, and the contract should say who pays each remaining installment.

What happens to unpaid Citrus County taxes?

The bill is delinquent from April 1, with a 3% penalty on the gross amount.

In May the collector prints the delinquent list in the local newspaper weekly for three weeks, and that cost lands on the bill. Selling of certificates begins by June 1. Unpaid tangible personal property carries a 1.5% penalty after April 1 and is advertised once.

A tax deed application becomes possible two years after the certificate's issue date. Redemption stays open until a deed issues, and the opening bid on a homestead parcel includes half the assessed value. Request a payoff before listing, and keep the written figure with your closing file.

How do homestead and Save Our Homes work for a Citrus County owner?

Homestead exemption can reduce taxable value by up to $50,000 if the county appraiser has your application before the March 1 cutoff.

Per the appraiser's page, $25,000 reduces every tax, and a second $25,000 reduces only non-school taxes on assessed value over $50,000. The same page puts the typical savings at roughly $500 a year. After the first year, the assessment cannot rise by more than the lesser of CPI change or 3 percent. If you moved from one Florida homestead to another within three years, you may be able to take some of your Save Our Homes savings along.

State guidance says homestead ends if the owner rents the unit or stops living there permanently, and a sale resets value to just value the next January 1.

What does the Census show about work and housing in Citrus County?

Labor force participation is low at 40.3%, and 17,659 residents are veterans. Receipts for medical and social assistance reached $1,111,065 thousand in 2022, and retail sales were $2,628,656 thousand, which averages $16,176 a resident. Accommodation and food services took in $258,230 thousand that year.

There were 3,063 employer establishments and 31,162 paid employees in 2023, and workers average a 27.8 minute commute. Renters pay about $1,107, and 88.3% of residents stayed in their home through the past year. The county also lists 13,125 nonemployer businesses. Density is 264.4 people per square mile in 2020, up from 242.8 in 2010, with a computer in 94.5% of households and 91.4% of adults 25 and over holding at least a high school diploma.

Furniture and equipment used in a rental or business is taxed separately as tangible personal property, with a 1.5% penalty on unpaid tangible tax after April 1.

What relief exists for older and veteran owners in Citrus County?

With seniors making up more than a third of the population, relief programs carry weight in Citrus County. An ordinance can add a senior exemption of as much as $50,000 for older owners under an income cap. The appraiser's office can say whether one applies locally.

  • Deferral: send Form DR-570 to the collector by March 31. It postpones the part of the tax above 5 percent of household income, or above 3 percent for permanent residents 65 and older.
  • Disabled veterans: $5,000 off assessed value at a service-connected rating of 10 percent or higher.
  • Veterans past 65 with a permanent service-connected disability can receive a homestead discount matching their VA percentage.

A denied exemption can go to the value adjustment board, but the petition window is 30 days.

What changes for a Citrus County seller at closing?

At the table, the title company apportions the year's tax and pays any back taxes from your proceeds.

The recorded deed carries Florida stamp tax, 70 cents per $100 of price, for which both buyer and seller stay liable. Many Citrus County sellers hold capped assessments, so the first bill a buyer receives often differs from the seller's last. Before closing, ask for three things.

  • A written payoff covering the current year and any earlier balance.
  • Word on whether a certificate was sold against the parcel.
  • The standing of any installment plan, which renews each year.

More questions about Citrus County, FL Property Tax Guide

What is the Citrus County early payment discount?

The discount starts at 4% for November and drops by a point each month through February. Nothing comes off in March, and April 1 begins delinquency.

When is the installment application due in Citrus County?

Applications close April 30. The first payment is due June 30, and a payment in July earns no discount.

When does a Citrus County tax bill turn delinquent?

On April 1, with a 3% penalty on the gross amount. A certificate sale starts by June 1.

What is the homestead filing deadline in Citrus County?

Get the form to the appraiser before March 1 rolls around. The appraiser, rather than the collector, rules on eligibility.

Can I sell a Citrus County house that has delinquent tax?

Yes. Whatever is owed gets deducted from your sale check by the title company, so get a payoff early and find out if the county sold a certificate.

Clay County by the numbers

What do Clay County's size and population mean for sellers?

Clay County has 604.61 land square miles and an estimated 239,593 people in mid-2025. That is 9.8% above the 218,249 counted at the start of 2020.

Households earn a median $87,820 for 2020 to 2024, more than the medians reported for Charlotte County and Citrus County, and the typical owned home is worth $312,500. Owners occupy 75.9% of 94,791 housing units, and rent runs about $1,551. Households average 2.69 people; 22.5% of residents are children and 18.8% are seniors.

The mean commute is 31.3 minutes, and 61.7% of adults work or seek work. The county also counts 27,517 veterans and 83,707 households.

Who sends the bill and who values the property in Clay County?

Billing and valuation sit with different offices. One mails and collects the tax, and the other determines what the parcel is worth and who qualifies for exemptions.

Mailing happens by November 1. When a lender pays the tax, the owner is sent an information-only copy. Taxes are assessed as of January 1 but are normally payable November 1. Citing Florida Statute 197.122, the page puts the burden on owners to learn what they owe and pay before delinquency, even if no bill arrived.

  • Property appraiser: value, homestead, portability and other exemptions, filed by March 1.
  • Tax collector: payment, installment and partial payment plans, certificate sales.
  • Clerk: records the deed and collects stamp tax.

What are the Clay County discounts and due dates?

Discounts start at 4% in November and step down monthly to 1% in February, after which March carries none and April 1 brings delinquency.

Clay County billing calendar
Pay inResult

Every payment method is accepted. A card payment adds a 2.50% fee, while an online e-check adds none.

How do Clay County installment and partial payment plans work?

To use installments you apply by April 30 with estimated taxes above $100, then pay the first quarter by June 30.

The first installment carries a 6% discount, with no discount if paid in July, and failing to make it by July 31 cancels the plan. The second, due September 30, carries 4.5%. The third, due December 31, carries 3%, and the fourth, due March 31, carries none. Last year's notice drives the first two payments, and the final two absorb any change in ownership, value or exemptions.

Partial payments are a separate option under Florida Statute 197.374. The owner submits a Partial Payment Plan application with the first payment or in person, and payments can begin November 1. Online payment is not accepted for this plan. Early payment discounts are forfeited, so the full March amount is due, and any balance left on April 1 is delinquent and goes into the June certificate sale.

What happens when Clay County taxes are not paid?

Expect a 3% penalty on April 1, more fees from May 1, and a certificate sale by June 1.

A certificate left unredeemed can lead to a tax deed application two years on, and the application fee is $75. The clerk runs the auction. An owner can pay the taxes before the deed issues and stop the sale.

Costs climb at each stage, so request a payoff before you put a house with unpaid tax on the market.

What does Clay County's economy look like in the Census data?

The Census counts 4,455 employer establishments and 48,303 paid employees in 2023, with an annual payroll of $2,210,794 thousand and employment up 5.1% from 2022. Medical and social assistance receipts reached $1,626,540 thousand in 2022 and retail sales $2,931,043 thousand.

Among 4,168 employer firms, 354 are veteran-owned, and another 20,041 nonemployer establishments were counted in 2024. A bachelor's degree is held by 28.3% of adults, broadband reaches 94.6% of households, and 9.1% of residents are below the poverty line. Per capita income is $39,563, and 10.0% of people under 65 lack health insurance.

Between the 2010 and 2020 counts, density climbed from 315.8 to 361.0 people per square mile. Computers are in 97.2% of homes. People born abroad are 7.0% of residents, and 10.5% of those under 65 report a disability.

For a seller, 1,522 building permits in 2025 and rising employment point to steady assessment activity, so read the TRIM notice each August. A value petition filed with the clerk is due 25 days after the TRIM notice, and exemption denials carry a 30 day window.

Which Clay County deadlines trip up sellers?

Three dates deserve attention during a listing, whether you sell in winter or in summer. March 1 is the exemption filing deadline for any buyer who wants homestead in the first year. March 31 is the final due date for a full bill or the fourth installment, and April 1 starts the penalty clock.

The installment plan also has a July trap. A first payment that misses June 30 but lands before July 31 earns no discount, and missing July 31 cancels the plan and returns the owner to the regular due dates and discounts. If you close in summer, find out which installments are paid so the contract divides the rest fairly.

  • Application for installments: April 30.
  • Credit card fee: 2.50%, none for online e-check.
  • Partial payment: current year only, November 1 through March 31.

How do homestead and Save Our Homes cap work in Clay County?

Send Form DR-501 to the appraiser by March 1. The home has to be your permanent residence on January 1.

The exemption is up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 covering all taxes and the added $25,000 covering only non-school taxes on value over $50,000. From the second year, assessed value can rise by only the smaller of 3 percent or inflation; the published chart shows caps of 2.9 percent for 2025 and 2.7 percent for 2026. Portability allows a move to a new Florida homestead within three years, with Form DR-501T filed alongside.

Non-homestead property has a separate 10 percent annual limit on assessed value growth. That matters for a rental or second home in Clay County, because its value for tax purposes can still climb every year.

How is the tax settled when you sell a Clay County home?

At closing the agent apportions the year's tax, subtracts any balance from your proceeds and sends the deed to the clerk for recording, which is when stamp tax is collected.

A deed carries a stamp tax of 70 cents on each $100 of consideration everywhere except Miami-Dade, and the state revenue agency says all parties to the document are liable no matter who agrees to pay. Confirm which tax year your payoff covers, because partial payment rules apply to the current year only.

With a lender-held escrow, find out when any refund would arrive, and check with the collector that this year's bill is settled.

Four points off in November, shrinking monthly through February. March pays the full amount, and April 1 starts delinquency with a 3% penalty.

When is the Clay County installment application due?

Apply by the end of April, with an estimate above $100. The June 30 first payment gets the biggest discount.

Cards carry a 2.50% fee. Online e-check payments carry none.

When is the Clay County tax certificate sale?

By June 1, covering the prior year's delinquent real estate taxes, with extra fees from May 1.

Where do I apply for homestead in Clay County?

Use Form DR-501 and send it to the appraiser by the first of March. The tax collector only bills.

Behind on Escambia County property tax?

Escambia County by the numbers

Which Escambia office sends the bill?

Billing and collection belong to the Escambia County Tax Collector, and valuation and the roll belong to the Property Appraiser. The appraiser's roll covers Escambia County, the City of Pensacola and the Town of Century, and its site notes that assessment values and exemptions reflect the 2026 certified tax roll.

The Tax Collector's office collects for the District School Board, the Board of County Commissioners, the City of Pensacola, the Town of Century, the Sheriff, the Downtown Improvement Board and the Northwest Florida Water Management District. It also collects for several state agencies. You can search a bill by name, address or account number on the Tax Collector's site, sign up for paperless e-billing, and read posted reports, including a list of the top 25 taxpayers in the county.

What is the payment schedule for Escambia County bills?

Bills are normally mailed November 1 and can be paid early at a discount that shrinks each month. Escambia's Tax Collector prints the schedule as 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January, 1 percent in February and the gross amount in March.

Escambia County tax collection schedule printed by the Tax Collector
PeriodWhat applies
November 1Notices mailed addressed to whoever owned the parcel on January 1
November4 percent discount
December3 percent discount
January2 percent discount
February1 percent discount
MarchGross amount
April 1Delinquent: 3 percent penalty on real estate, 1.5 percent on tangible property
May 1Advertising costs begin to be added

A missed bill does not excuse late payment. The office reminds owners it is their duty to find out the amount due and pay before April 1, and the same rule applies if a bill went to an old address. Send address changes to the Property Appraiser, who maintains the roll.

What non-ad valorem charges show up on an Escambia County bill?

Some line items are flat assessments that do not depend on your home's value, and the charge depends on whether the house is inside Pensacola or in the unincorporated county. Unpaid non-ad valorem amounts can lead to a tax certificate just like unpaid property tax.

  • Unincorporated Escambia: the Board of County Commissioners assesses fire protection, rescue and advanced life support, street lighting, road paving, retention ponds and solid waste. For amounts, call the County Office of Management and Budget at (850) 595-4960.
  • Inside Pensacola: the City Council assesses stormwater management, based on the square footage of impervious surface on the property. For amounts, call the City of Pensacola at (850) 436-5646.

When you sell, look at the bill's non-ad valorem section as well as the main levy, because a buyer or title agent will ask whether these were paid.

What other accounts does the Escambia Tax Collector manage?

The same office also issues the Escambia County Business Tax Receipt, so a landlord or small business owner who sells a property should check that account too. New business tax accounts are opened through the office's website.

  • Paperless e-billing: owners can sign up so the property tax bill arrives by email.
  • Reports: the site posts tax, real estate and other reports for public viewing.
  • Top 25 taxpayers: a list is published for the county.
  • Late rule for business property: tangible bills carry a 1.5 percent penalty after April 1, compared with 3 percent on real estate.

The office describes itself as a fee officer funded by the fees it earns, with a cash flow of $600 million. For a seller, the practical point is that one office can confirm several balances in a single visit, so ask for every account tied to your name or entity before you close.

How does homestead change things for Escambia owners?

A resident owner applies to the Property Appraiser by March 1, using Form DR-501, for up to $50,000 of exemption. The home must be the permanent residence on January 1.

After that, the capped increase protects the owner, and DOR's chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026. The protection ends at a sale, so the next owner of an Escambia house typically sees a higher bill the following year.

How do I dispute an Escambia County assessment?

Challenge the value after the August notice arrives, and do it quickly. Florida DOR says a petition on one of the DR-486 forms goes to the clerk within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, and the same notice lists the dates when the School Board, the county and the City of Pensacola hold budget hearings.

Exemption problems run on another track. If the Property Appraiser denies an exemption, classification, portability transfer or tax deferral, the Value Adjustment Board petition is due 30 days after the denial letter was mailed. Growth in a taxing body's property tax revenue is also capped by state law at per capita personal income growth plus new construction unless a super-majority, unanimous vote or referendum overrides the cap, which is why hearings in September and October can change your rate even when your value stays flat.

Keep every notice you receive. A buyer's agent may ask for the TRIM notice to see what your neighbors' proposed rates look like in the same district.

What follows nonpayment in Escambia County?

A certificate is sold after April 1, and a tax deed can follow. The Tax Collector warns that nonpayment can cost the property.

  • Certificates go to the lowest bidding interest rate, in quarter-point steps.
  • A deed application waits two years and carries a $75 fee.
  • A homestead's opening bid at the deed sale includes half the latest assessed value.

A seller can still close and redeem from proceeds. Request a payoff statement well ahead of closing.

Are there senior or veteran reductions in Escambia?

Some, but each is a separate request.

  • A veteran with a permanent service-connected disability, 65 or older, may get a homestead discount matching the VA rating.
  • A disabled ex-servicemember gets $5,000 off assessed value.
  • Deferral applications go to the Tax Collector by March 31.

Ask the Property Appraiser which local options Escambia has adopted.

What closing steps involve Escambia taxes and title?

Clear the tax account first, then plan for deed stamps. Deed stamps in Escambia run at the common statewide rate, 70 cents on each $100 of price, due through the clerk at recording, and each party to the deed is liable for it.

If the house is escrowed, the mortgage company pays within the discount period, so ask your servicer what has been paid and when a refund follows payoff. For a property that has passed through probate or has unrecorded heirs, you may need the clerk's records on the estate before the buyer's title agent will insure.

More questions about Escambia County, FL Property Tax Guide

When does Escambia County mail property tax bills?

Normally November 1 each year, addressed to whoever owned the parcel on January 1. If you do not get one, ask the Tax Collector, because the duty to pay before April 1 stays with the owner.

What penalty applies to late Escambia County property tax?

A 3 percent penalty is added to real estate bills on April 1, and 1.5 percent to tangible property bills. Advertising costs start being added May 1, and a certificate can follow.

Whom do I phone about a stormwater or fire line on my Escambia bill?

For unincorporated Escambia, call the County Office of Management and Budget at (850) 595-4960. For the Pensacola stormwater charge, call the City of Pensacola at (850) 436-5646.

Does my Escambia County homestead cap pass to the buyer?

No. A sale is a change of ownership, so the property resets to just value the following January 1. Portability can carry part of your cap to your next Florida home.

Can I sell my Escambia County house with unpaid taxes?

Yes. The balance, and any certificate redemption, comes out of the proceeds. Request a payoff statement from the Tax Collector well ahead of closing.

Hernando County by the numbers

Which offices deal with a Hernando County tax bill?

Three elected offices share the work in Hernando County: the property appraiser values parcels and grants exemptions, the tax collector mails the bills and takes the money, and the clerk files deeds and runs tax deed auctions. A seller will probably contact each one.

The tax collector's mailing address is 20 N. Main Street, Room 112, Brooksville, FL 34601, and questions can go to tc@hernandocounty.us. The tax collector's own site says the appraiser handles homestead exemptions, assessed values and name or address changes for notices. The Hernando County Property Appraiser keeps offices in Brooksville and in Spring Hill, and publishes a tax estimator and a parcel search.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, parcel search, ownership changes on the roll.
  • Tax Collector: tax bills, payments, installment plan, certificate sale.
  • Clerk: recorded deeds and tax deed sales.

When is Hernando County property tax due?

Hernando County bills in November, and payment is accepted through March 31, and any account still open on April 1 is delinquent.

Paying in November saves 4 percent on the bill; each later month trims the savings by a point until February, and March brings none. The office honors the postmark on current-year payments sent during a discount period. Online e-check payments are free for current and delinquent bills, while cards carry a $2.75 minimum or 2.5% processing fee that goes to a third-party vendor.

Tangible personal property tax, which covers furniture, fixtures and equipment in businesses and rental properties, arrives on the same bill and earns the same discounts. A $25,000 exemption is available to owners who file a return by April 1, so landlords selling a rental should ask whether such an account exists for the address.

How does the Hernando County installment plan work?

The plan splits the bill into four quarterly payments, and you can only pay each installment in its own month. Enrollment opens every November 1 and closes April 30, and it is confirmed once the first June payment is made.

Hernando County Tax Collector installment schedule
Due dateDiscount

September 304.5%

March 31Final payment, no discount

A late installment has to be paid with the next one. An unpaid balance on April 1 is delinquent and no discount applies. Withdrawing means giving up the discounts the law provides. The statute behind the plan is section 197.222.

Outside the plan, partial payments on the current year are possible from November 1 through March 31. That route needs a signed application, forfeits all discounts and allows only five partial payments, with the balance due by March 31.

What homestead rules apply in Hernando County?

A Hernando County homestead exemption takes up to $50,000 off the taxable value of the home you live in. You have to own it and make it your permanent Florida residence by January 1 of the year you apply.

The appraiser's page says it is taking applications covering tax year 2027, with a filing deadline of March 1, 2027, and that later applications count for the 2028 tax year. Owners can apply at an appraiser office, through the mail or on a secure online portal. Statewide, the Save Our Homes cap holds yearly assessment growth at 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is smaller, and the Florida Revenue chart prints 2.7 percent for 2026.

On the bill, the tax collector combines all exemptions into one dollar figure under the word Exemption. Once a home is sold, the appraiser removes the owner's exemption and cap starting the next year, so a buyer must apply to start fresh.

What happens to unpaid Hernando County property tax?

Delinquent Hernando County tax earns 3% interest from April 1, gets listed in a local newspaper, and picks up advertising and collection fees. The tax collector auctions tax certificates online through LienHub at the end of May, and the page mentions May 29 as the cutoff for payment before the sale.

  • Bidding starts at 18 percent interest and falls in steps toward 0.25 percent.
  • The winning bidder pays the taxes and holds a first lien on the parcel.
  • A homestead parcel with a taxable amount under $250.00, or one in litigation, is struck off to the county.
  • A certificate lives seven years unless bankruptcy interrupts it.
  • Two years on, the holder may ask for a tax deed sale, which the clerk then conducts.

Delinquent bills can be paid by any method, but a parcel in tax deed status needs certified funds. If no one bids at a deed sale, the land goes on a list of lands available for taxes, and the county has the first 90 days to buy it.

What should a Hernando County seller know before closing?

A seller in Hernando County pays off the tax out of the closing funds, and the recorded deed is what shifts the bill to the buyer. When a finished deed reaches the Hernando clerk's records, the appraiser changes the owner on the roll, and the tax collector's record follows after the next certified tax roll in October.

Florida's documentary stamp tax on a deed runs 70 cents for each $100 of the price in every county but Miami-Dade, and each party to the deed is liable. The closing statement should split the current year's bill between buyer and seller; ask whether any tangible personal property account sits on the same bill.

Millage rates are set by each taxing authority, and the tax collector names the county commission, the City of Brooksville, the school board and the regional water district as examples. The appraiser posts a millage report once rates are updated at final roll certification. For the rate on your parcel, check the TRIM notice mailed in August or ask the tax collector.

How can a Hernando County owner challenge a value?

Petitions are due at the clerk's office within 25 days of the August TRIM mailing from the appraiser. Petitions go to the Value Adjustment Board, using one of the DR-486 forms. A petition filed after the deadline on the notice is out of time, so mark the date when the envelope arrives.

A refused homestead exemption, classification or deferral has its own 30 day limit, measured from the day the denial letter went out. The board deals with value and exemptions, and tax rates are set elsewhere, at the budget hearings of the taxing authorities in September and October. Homeowners with a rental or an agricultural parcel can ask the appraiser's office, which lists agricultural classification, mobile home and tangible property pages on its site, whether a separate filing applies.

More questions about Hernando County, FL Property Tax Guide

When does Hernando County property tax become delinquent?

April 1. Payment is accepted through the end of March, and the tax collector then adds 3% interest to delinquent amounts, along with advertising and collection fees.

What discount does Hernando County give for early payment?

Savings start at 4 percent for November payers and fall one point a month through February. March has no discount, and the postmark decides the date for current-year payments.

Does Hernando County take credit cards for tax payments?

Yes, with a $2.75 minimum or 2.5% processing fee charged by a third-party vendor. E-checks are free online for current and delinquent bills, and tax deed payments need certified funds.

How do I apply for the Hernando County homestead exemption?

Apply with the property appraiser at an office, by mail or through the online portal. The 2027 filing window closes March 1, 2027, and you must live in the home as your permanent residence on January 1.

Who runs the Hernando County tax certificate sale?

The tax collector runs it online through LienHub at the end of May each year. Bidders register with LienHub, and parcels are auctioned one at a time in parcel number order.

Indian River County by the numbers

Which Indian River County offices touch a tax bill?

The work divides three ways: the Property Appraiser sets values and takes exemption filings, the Tax Collector mails and collects the bills, and a county Value Adjustment Board hears appeals. Recorded deeds sit with the Clerk of the Court.

The Property Appraiser keeps two offices: the Vero office at 1800 27th St., Bldg. B, Vero Beach, (772) 226-1469, and a Sebastian office at 1921 U.S. 1, (772) 226-1133, both staffed Monday through Friday from eight to five. The Tax Collector's tax department answers at (772) 226-1343. The Collector says it acts as an agent for local governments and has no say over assessed value or the amount due.

The Tax Collector's site links to the county's municipalities, which include Vero Beach, Sebastian, Indian River Shores, Orchid and Fellsmere. Houses in any of them are billed by the same county Tax Collector.

How large is the Indian River County tax roll?

The Property Appraiser's home page reports a 2026 certified roll with $51,957,635,233 in just value and $33,819,841,085 in taxable value. It counts 96,241 real parcels and 9,853 tangible personal property accounts.

Exemptions, assessment caps and other reductions explain the gap between those two totals. Your own notice carries the three numbers that govern one parcel: market, assessed and taxable value.

What are the Indian River County due dates and discounts?

Bills go out by November 1, and the early-payment discount falls one step each month until March.

  • November postmark: 4% off
  • December postmark: 3% off
  • January postmark: 2% off
  • February postmark: 1% off
  • March: full gross amount

Silence from the mail is no excuse: the Tax Collector says the owner must see that a bill is received, and asks anyone without one by November 9 to call. Send a written address change to the Property Appraiser, and expect a separate bill for each parcel you own.

Two bill messages deserve attention. A "Do Not Pay" notice means a mortgage company has requested your original bill, and "Back Taxes Remain Unpaid" means delinquent tax also sits on the account. Call (772) 226-1343 to learn the amount.

What if an Indian River County bill goes unpaid?

The delinquency date is April 1, when a 3% penalty attaches to the gross tax. By May, an advertising fee is added and the account is listed weekly in a local newspaper for three weeks running. Then a certificate has to be sold by June 1.

The Tax Collector sends interested bidders to a county page on a tax certificate sale website. A certificate ranks as a first lien on the parcel. Two years after the April 1 of issue, its holder may seek a deed, and the Clerk then auctions the property under the state's deposit and payment-within-24-hours rules.

The Tax Collector's office adds that no partial payments are taken on current or delinquent real estate bills. An owner who cannot pay in full has three routes: next year's installment plan, a homestead deferral if eligible, or a sale that clears the tax from proceeds.

Does Indian River County offer a four-payment plan?

Yes, when next year's estimated bill exceeds $100. The application is filed ahead of the plan year: the office takes 2026 tax year applications from November 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027, and closed the 2025 window on May 1, 2026.

Four bills make up the plan: June (6% discount), September (4.5%), December (3%) and March (no discount). June and September are computed from last year's tax, while December and March absorb the true-up to the new roll. A late first payment may be made in July, minus the 6%. Skip it altogether and the account reverts to a normal November bill.

The office cannot accept an installment outside its month, and a payment that misses its month forfeits the discount. If the house sells mid-plan, the account stays on the plan for that year, so the closing agent needs the list of paid installments. A buyer who prefers an annual bill next year can ask the Tax Collector to drop the account.

What deferral and exemptions are available in Indian River County?

A homestead owner whose age and income qualify can postpone part or all of the bill by applying to the Tax Collector by March 31. Interest accrues on the deferred amount as a lien, and everything becomes payable at death, on a sale of the home, or when homestead status changes.

Homestead filings go to the Property Appraiser by March 1, with permanent Florida residency required on January 1. The appraiser's home page says that applications submitted after September 6 are for the 2027 tax year. The state exemption comes in two tiers, and the school-tax-exempt tier is the first $25,000 only.

On a homestead, the Save Our Homes cap (2.7 percent for 2026) restrains growth. When the home sells, value resets to market the next January 1, so the buyer's bill may look nothing like yours.

Where do I send a petition against an Indian River County value?

File a petition with the Value Adjustment Board by the date printed on your Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, which Florida sets at 25 days after the notices are mailed.

The Property Appraiser's home page links to the county's Value Adjustment Board site. If the appraiser denied an exemption, the state allows a petition 30 days after the denial letter is mailed. Bring comparable sales, photographs and repair estimates with you.

What if the bill arrives after the house has sold?

Bills follow the certified tax roll, so a November notice can land on someone who has already sold. The Tax Collector gives clear directions for that case.

  • A real estate bill for property you no longer own should be forwarded to the new owner or returned to the Tax Collector's office.
  • A business equipment bill is different: if you owned the equipment on January 1, you still owe the tax. If you did not, call the Property Appraiser at (772) 226-1370.
  • Each parcel gets its own bill, so check that the legal description on yours matches everything you own.
  • Address changes go to the Property Appraiser, not the Tax Collector, and the appraiser offers an online change-of-address form.

Those steps keep a missing or misdirected notice from turning into a delinquent account that a buyer's lender will notice.

What belongs on an Indian River County seller's closing checklist?

Order a payoff and confirm which bill is open. The Tax Collector says the new owner answers for the entire November bill, yet closing agents ordinarily prorate it, giving the buyer a credit for the seller's months. The seller does not send the Tax Collector a partial payment.

  • Look for a back-taxes message on the account.
  • List any installment payments already made.
  • Ask if a deferral lien is attached to the homestead.
  • Check the recorded deeds at the Clerk's office.

The state deed stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and every party on the document can be liable. Where back tax, a deferral lien or a damaged roof complicates a sale, a cash buyer taking the house as-is can have the title company pay the balance.

Use the county tax payment portal the Tax Collector links from its site. Discounts follow the postmark date, and the tax department at (772) 226-1343 can tell you about other payment options.

April 1, when the 3% penalty is added. In May unpaid accounts are advertised, ahead of a certificate sale due by June 1.

When can I apply for the 2026 tax year installment plan?

Applications for the 2026 tax year run November 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027, and the first payment falls in June.

Can I pay part of an Indian River County bill?

No. The Tax Collector says partial payments on current or delinquent real estate bills are not accepted.

The bill goes to the owner, but closing agents normally prorate, so the buyer repays the seller for the months after closing. Check the split on the closing statement.

Lake County by the numbers

Who sends the property tax bill in Lake County, Florida?

One office sends and collects the bill; a different one decides what the house is worth for tax purposes. Keep that split in mind when something looks wrong, because each office can only fix its own part.

The tax collector's property tax page says any change to a name, mailing address, location or assessed value on the roll must go through the property appraiser, whose number it prints as (352) 253-2150. The page adds that collection starts November 1, and that a missing notice does not excuse the owner from paying. For escrowed loans the notice carries a code at the top and a banner at the bottom.

  • Property Appraiser: values every parcel, handles homestead and other exemption filings, mails the August notice of proposed taxes.
  • Tax Collector: prints and mails the bill, takes payment, runs the June tax certificate sale on unpaid accounts.
  • Clerk of the Circuit Court: files the deed, takes the deed stamps, and supports the value adjustment board.

What are the Lake County early payment discounts and deadlines?

Lake County lets owners save up to 4 percent by paying in November, and the discount shrinks by one point each month through February. The window closes at the end of March.

Lake County tax collector payment schedule, as printed on the collector's property tax page
Paid in full byDiscount
November 304 percent

A payment sent by mail earns the discount according to its postmark. On April 1 the page says a 3 percent statutory interest charge is added to the total due. The state lists the same ladder statewide and adds that tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1.

Ask the tax collector's office about installment plans and the tax certificate sale schedule before you rely on either, since the collector's office sets those details each year.

What millage rates apply to a Lake County home?

It depends on where the house sits. The Lake County Property Appraiser's 2026 final millage rate sheet lists a separate total for every taxing district code, and the totals run from the low 13s for unincorporated land to the high 19s in some cities.

For the unincorporated codes at the top of the sheet, the totals printed are 13.0632, 13.0670 and 13.4678 depending on the code. The county general fund line is 5.0254 in every row, the school board state line is 3.0560, and the school board local line is 2.9980. Those lines repeat across the sheet, so the gap between districts comes from the extra lines: the city levy, a fire or ambulance district, a hospital district and community development districts.

  • Clermont: 16.2875 total, with a city line of 4.2000.
  • Leesburg: 15.8704 total, with a city line of 3.3783.
  • Mount Dora: 18.7921 total, with a city line of 6.3000.
  • Eustis: 19.8819 total, with a city line of 7.3898.
  • Montverde: 15.3975 total, with a city line of 2.8300.

Read the sheet for your own code before you assume any figure. The code is on your tax notice and on the appraiser's parcel record. Lake County's municipalities on the sheet include Astatula, Clermont, Eustis, Fruitland Park, Groveland, Howey-in-the-Hills, Lady Lake, Leesburg, Mascotte, Minneola, Montverde, Mount Dora, Tavares and Umatilla.

How do homestead exemption and Save Our Homes work for Lake County owners?

Living in the house on January 1 and filing by March 1 gets a Lake County owner a homestead exemption worth up to $50,000 in value, per the state. School levies take only the first slice of that exemption. In Lake County the school board lines on the millage sheet are 3.0560 and 2.9980, so the school share of a bill gets the smaller break.

The form is DR-501, filed with the property appraiser. Renting the home or moving out ends the exemption. The Lake County Property Appraiser's home page links a list of exemptions and how to qualify, which is the place to check senior, veteran and disability benefits that local rules may add.

Save Our Homes holds a homestead's yearly assessed growth under a ceiling tied to inflation. The state's chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024. The buyer's first full bill can look very different from the seller's, because a sale returns the parcel to market value. A seller moving within Florida may be able to take the accumulated cushion along to the next homestead through portability, which has its own form and a three-year clock.

What happens to Lake County property tax when you sell the house?

Seller and buyer divide the current year's tax at closing, and any back tax has to be gone before title passes. The title company normally pays the collector from the seller's share.

A house sold in spring or summer usually has no current bill yet, since statements arrive in the fall. The title agent estimates it. Get the exact amount and any older balance from the collector while the contract is still being negotiated.

  • Pull the parcel record from the appraiser and confirm the owner and mailing address.
  • Ask the collector whether any year is delinquent or holds a certificate.
  • Tell the title company if you have a homestead exemption so the proration uses the right figure.
  • Plan for the buyer's value reset after closing, since the next bill can be higher.

Deed stamps are set by statute at 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and each party stays liable even if the contract assigns the cost to one side.

What if Lake County property tax goes unpaid?

Delinquency starts April 1, and the property can eventually reach a tax deed sale. An unpaid parcel sits under a certificate for a while first; the investor who holds it cannot ask for a deed until two years of waiting have run.

The certificate sale opens on or before June 1. Bidders compete by accepting the lowest interest rate, and certificates with no taker go to the county. A homestead parcel with less than $250 delinquent is issued to the county instead of auctioned. The clerk then conducts a public auction, and the winning bidder must put down a nonrefundable deposit.

Owners who cannot pay can look at the homestead tax deferral. Homestead owners with low income can ask the collector to defer part of the bill using Form DR-570, filed by the end of March. A separate installment prepayment request has a May 1 date.

How do you challenge a Lake County value?

If the August notice shows a value that looks off, a petition to the board must come within 25 days of that notice. The state revenue department's taxpayer page prints that 25-day window.

A denied exemption or deferral runs on its own 30-day clock, counted from the mailing date of the denial letter. The board is staffed through the Lake County clerk's office, which publishes its own forms page. Talk to the appraiser first, since many questions about square footage or exemption status resolve before any petition.

Taxing authorities hold public hearings on their budgets in September and October and adopt final millage after that. Those hearings are where you can speak about rates, as opposed to the value of your own house.

More questions about Lake County, FL Property Tax Guide

When are Lake County property taxes due?

The collector's ladder runs from 4 percent down to 1 percent across four months, and the gross bill is due by the end of March. After that, a 3 percent charge attaches.

Who do I call to change my Lake County mailing address on a tax bill?

Call the Lake County Property Appraiser, not the tax collector. The collector's page says name, address, location and assessed value changes are made by the appraiser, and it lists (352) 253-2150 for that office.

What is the total millage in unincorporated Lake County?

The 2026 final millage sheet prints 13.0632, 13.0670 or 13.4678 for unincorporated codes, depending on the district. Your notice shows your code, and the sheet shows the full line breakdown.

Does selling my Lake County house reset my tax value?

Yes for the buyer. Yes for the buyer. A sale counts as a change of ownership, so the seller's capped value does not follow the house.

Can I sell a Lake County house with unpaid property tax?

Yes. The balance, plus any certificate redemption, comes out of the seller's proceeds. Collect the payoff number from the collector's office and hand it to the closing agent early.

Leon County by the numbers

Who runs property tax in Leon County?

In Leon County one office values parcels and approves exemptions, another prints bills and collects, and elected boards set the millage between them.

The collector's website lays out the order: value, then rates, then a certified roll, then mailed notices. Because the collector has no power over the roll, a corrected name or address has to come through the appraiser.

  • Appraiser: values, exemption files, parcel data, owner records.
  • Collector: notices, payments, quarterly plans, delinquency, certificates.
  • Clerk: deed recording and the stamp tax paid with it.

When is Leon County property tax billed, and when does it go delinquent?

Collection opens each November 1 for the calendar year, and the collector's site holds owners responsible for knowing what they owe before April 1. The appraiser's page reports the 2026 bills went out in November.

Once April 1 passes, a delinquency fee, an advertising fee, interest of 1.5 percent a month and collection costs under s. 197.332(1) get stacked onto the balance. A newspaper list of delinquent names must run within 45 days. The plan page adds that balances left on April 1 face a tax certificate on June 1.

The statewide discount ladder (4, 3, 2 and 1 percent, November to February) applies. Where a lender escrows the tax, the collector says the lender should request the original notice so the owner gets a duplicate.

Does Leon County offer an installment plan for property tax?

Yes, for estimated tax above $100, with the application in hand at the collector's office ahead of May 1. Enrollment then renews itself every year.

Earning the discount means paying the first quarter by June 30. A late payment through July 31 is taken at full price; missing it cancels enrollment and the whole bill falls due March 31. Meeting June 30 commits the owner to the plan all year.

  • Quarter one, June 30: 6 percent off.
  • Quarter two, September 30: 4.5 percent off.
  • Quarter three, December 31: 3 percent off, plus half of any true-up.
  • Quarter four, March 31: full price, plus the remaining true-up.

Quarters one and two track last year's notice, and changes in owner, value or exemptions reach quarters three and four. A seller closing mid-year should give the title company a list of what is paid.

What exemptions does the Leon County Property Appraiser list?

The appraiser's site sets March 1 as the yearly filing cutoff and describes homestead along with several veteran and service benefits. Homestead is the base for the other benefits listed, so owners should file for it first.

Florida stacks homestead in two layers. The first $25,000 of assessed value is shielded from every levy, school included, and a second layer protects value above $50,000 from non-school levies only. Permanent residence must exist by January 1, and renting the home or moving out ends the benefit.

The veteran and military exemptions the office describes each require homestead first:

  • A $5,000 reduction for service-connected disability of 10 percent or higher (surviving spouses may qualify).
  • A percentage discount for combat-related disability at age 65 or older, tied to the VA rating.
  • A full exemption where the disability is total and permanent.
  • A deployment exemption: Form DR-501M plus deployment orders.

Paperwork is accepted four ways, including fax. Counties and cities may add income-limited senior exemptions, so ask the appraiser which of those cover your address.

What caps and rules apply to Leon County assessments?

The appraiser's FAQ says non-homestead assessments cannot rise more than 10 percent a year, for non-school taxes. Homestead rises are limited by Save Our Homes to the smaller of 3 percent or inflation.

The state chart shows caps of 2.7 percent (2026), 2.9 percent (2025) and 3.0 percent (2024). After a sale the parcel returns to full just value the next January 1, so a buyer inheriting a long-held home's low assessment will not keep it. Mention this when pricing a listing.

Amendment 3 starts January 1, 2027, the appraiser writes, and leaves 2026 bills untouched. The office is awaiting state guidance, so watch its site for the next roll.

What happens to unpaid business personal property tax in Leon County?

Leon County treats a business's tangible personal property separately from real estate, and the collector enforces it differently. Unpaid tangible tax leads to a petition for tax warrants rather than a tax certificate on the land.

Per the collector's page, within 30 days after the warrants are prepared the office applies to the Clerk of the Circuit Court for an order that directs levy and seizure of the property or garnishment of the delinquent taxpayer's bank account for the tax and costs. Landlords who furnish rentals or run a business out of a house should know the same collector handles real estate tax and this separate tangible tax, since the Tax Collector's page says both are collected there each year beginning November 1. A seller clearing a payoff should ask the office whether any tangible account is tied to the address, and a buyer purchasing a rental from an investor should do the same before closing.

How should Leon County sellers handle tax at closing?

Request a proration and a payoff figure for anything delinquent, and report any installments already paid. The closing agent divides the live year between the parties; late balances come out of your funds.

Document stamp tax on a Leon County deed is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, the rate for every Florida county except Miami-Dade. Payment goes to the clerk at the time of recording, and each party named in the document is liable however the parties split the cost.

Homestead stays behind. A buyer files on their own by the first of March, and a seller moving within Florida can carry the Save Our Homes benefit by filing Form DR-501T, with a three-year window counted from the January 1 of the year the old homestead ended.

How does Leon County compare on housing?

Leon County, home to Tallahassee, counted about 299,048 people in mid-2025, across 668 square miles, and it is a renter-heavy market compared with most of Florida.

Leon County snapshot, Census Bureau QuickFacts (2020 to 2024 unless noted)
MeasureLeon County
People, mid-2025 estimate299,048
Housing units, 2025 estimate143,256
Owner-occupied housing rate52.6%
Typical home value where owners live$301,800
Median gross rent$1,291
Adults 25+ holding a bachelor's degree48.9%

The Census Bureau reports 122,597 households averaging 2.27 people, a median gross rent of $1,291 and a poverty rate of 21.3 percent, with only 17.0 percent of residents aged 65 or older. Median household income for 2020 to 2024 is $66,287, and 2,047 building permits were issued in 2025.

Because owners occupy only about half the homes, a sizeable share of sellers are landlords with tenants in place. A rented home loses homestead, and lease terms shape any closing date.

More questions about Leon County, FL Property Tax Guide

When does Leon County property tax become delinquent?

The April 1 after the assessment year. From that date the collector tacks on a delinquency fee, an advertising fee, monthly interest and statutory collection costs.

Can I pay Leon County property tax in installments?

Yes, when estimated tax tops $100 and the form is in before May 1. Four payments fall on June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, discounted 6, 4.5 and 3 percent for the first three.

By when must Leon County homestead be filed?

The first of March. The appraiser accepts applications by email, mail, fax or in person. Contact the office for the homestead amount.

Does Amendment 3 change my 2026 Leon County bill?

No. The appraiser's message says the amendment begins January 1, 2027 and leaves 2026 bills as issued.

Who changes the name or address on a Leon County tax bill?

The appraiser. Roll changes run through that office, so contact it before bills are next mailed.

Martin County by the numbers

Who sends and who values in Martin County?

The Martin County Property Appraiser values property, and the Martin County Tax Collector sends bills and collects them. Both offices are county constitutional offices, and the clerk's Official Records hold recorded deeds and liens.

  • Martin County Property Appraiser: real property parcel search by parcel ID, account number, subdivision, address or owner last name, plus published millage and census-based county statistics.
  • Martin County Tax Collector: tax statements, alternative payment plans, delinquent taxes and certificates, an important-dates page, a tangible personal property page and a glossary. Offices operate in Stuart, Hobe Sound, Indiantown and Palm City, and the phone line is 772-288-5600.
  • Martin County Clerk Official Records: the search for recorded instruments.

Amounts owed go to the collector. Value, exemptions and parcel records go to the appraiser.

What does the Martin County Property Appraiser report about the county?

The appraiser's home page says ten taxing authorities levy property taxes against Martin County parcels, and each proposes its own millage rate before public hearings adopt the budgets. Commercial and industrial parcels are 3.6% of real property parcels, per the appraiser.

The same page lists the headings it tracks: total market value, land area in square miles, single family homes, condo units, parks and natural areas, golf courses, restaurants, population, median household income, owner-occupied housing, population per square mile, housing units and veterans, with the data sourced from census.gov. Open the page to see the current values, since they change with each year's roll.

The page also notes that a proposed constitutional amendment on Florida property taxes was on the November 2026 general election ballot, and that approval by at least 60% of voters would put changes into effect January 1, 2027. Check the appraiser's site for what followed.

Where do Martin County residents pay and find help?

The tax collector runs four offices: Stuart, Hobe Sound, Indiantown and Palm City. The home page shows estimated wait times and people waiting at each office, and the office says e-checks are free. Its online payment pages and the county-taxes portal let owners look up accounts without a visit.

The same website carries a glossary of tax terms, a page on tangible personal property taxes, a frequently asked questions page on tax certificate sales and a page on alternative payment plans. Because the collector warns that site information is not guaranteed for legal purposes and may change daily, confirm any amount by phone before you rely on it for a closing.

Owners who want to understand the value side go to the property appraiser's parcel search and can compare their TRIM notice against the published roll data. A buyer's lender or title company will often ask for both the appraiser record and the collector's account history.

When are Martin County property taxes due?

Martin County tax statements are normally mailed on or about November 1, and the gross amount is due by March 31. Discounts run from 4% in November down to 1% in February.

Martin County Tax Collector calendar, as printed on its Important Tax Dates page
MonthWhat the collector lists
NovemberCollection begins, 4% discount through November 30
December3% discount; third installment due by December 31 with 3% discount
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchGross amount due by March 31; fourth installment due
AprilUnpaid real property taxes delinquent on April 1; applications for the next installment year due by April 30
JuneCertificate sale starts by June 1; first installment due by June 30 with 6% discount
SeptemberSecond installment due by September 30 with 4.5% discount

What does delinquency cost in Martin County?

On April 1 the collector adds 3% interest to unpaid real property taxes. Unpaid business personal property accrues 1.5% per month plus a $2.00 delinquent fee, and those accounts are advertised in a local newspaper within 45 days.

For real estate, the collector's calendar describes a newspaper ad run weekly over three weeks before the certificate sale, with the ad cost charged to the delinquent parcel. A certificate holder must wait two years before contacting the owner for payment, and a tax deed application can follow after that.

What does the Martin County calendar say about business and vehicle taxes?

The collector's calendar covers more than real estate. Tangible personal property gets the same early-payment discounts as real property, and the same April 1 delinquency date. Warrants on delinquent personal property accounts are prepared before April 30, two years after the year of assessment.

  • Local business tax receipts: renewals are due September 30 and become delinquent October 1, when a late fee applies.
  • Heavy trucks over 5,000 pounds, truck-trailers, semi-trailers and certain vehicles for hire: registration and renewal due December 31.
  • Mobile home decals: they also expire December 31.

A seller who owns a rental or runs a business from the property should check these items with the collector, since a house sale does not end a business account tied to the address.

Is there an installment plan in Martin County?

Yes. The collector offers an alternative payment plan with four payments. State law gives the program as section 197.222, with the application due by April 30 per the Martin collector's calendar for the next year.

  • June 30: first payment with a 6% discount.
  • July: a late first payment may be accepted with a 5% penalty, otherwise participation is canceled.
  • September 30: second payment with a 4.5% discount.
  • December 31: third payment with a 3% discount.
  • March 31: fourth and final payment.

Enrolled taxpayers do not need to reapply to continue the program. A seller who is partway through the plan should ask the collector what is left, since the remaining portion is settled when the sale closes.

Which exemptions can lower a Martin County bill?

Martin County owners file with the property appraiser, and the first deadline falls in early March.

  • Homestead takes up to $50,000 off value. School taxes see only the first $25,000 of it.
  • A state cap limits yearly growth on a homestead. The state's chart prints 2.7% for 2026.
  • Other property has a 10 percent annual ceiling.
  • Portability carries cap savings to a new homestead, for up to $500,000 of difference. The statute page notes that chapter 2026-239 changes first apply to the 2027 roll.
  • A service-connected disability of 10 percent or more earns a $5,000 reduction in assessed value for an honorably discharged Florida resident.

A sale resets the parcel to market-based value the following January. The TRIM notice arrives in August and petitions go to the clerk.

How does Martin County tax get settled at a sale?

The collector's payoff number lets the title company clear the tax when the sale funds. The collector's offices in Stuart, Hobe Sound, Indiantown and Palm City can all be reached at 772-288-5600 about whether a certificate exists.

Florida charges deed stamp tax at 70 cents per $100 of consideration. A contract-for-deed buyer on record is among those notified before a tax deed sale, so a land contract does not hide a parcel from the process.

More questions about Martin County, FL Property Tax Guide

When are Martin County property tax statements mailed?

On or about November 1 each year, according to the Martin County Tax Collector. The gross amount is due by March 31.

What interest does Martin County add after April 1?

The collector's calendar lists a 3% interest charge on unpaid real property taxes. Tangible personal property accrues 1.5% per month plus a $2.00 fee.

Does Martin County have an installment plan for property tax?

Yes. It has four payments due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, with discounts of 6%, 4.5% and 3% on the first three. Applications are due by April 30.

Who do I call in Martin County about my tax account?

Call the Martin County Tax Collector at 772-288-5600. For parcel values and exemptions, contact the Martin County Property Appraiser.

Can I sell a Martin County house if taxes are overdue?

Yes. The balance can be cleared through closing. Get the payoff and any certificate details from the collector beforehand.
