Okaloosa County by the numbers

What does Okaloosa County's housing market look like?

Okaloosa County holds 221,810 residents by the 2025 QuickFacts estimate, a gain of 4.8 percent since 2020, over 930.19 square miles of land. For 2022, QuickFacts lists retail sales near $5.17 billion and health care receipts near $1.47 billion.

Owned homes have a median value of $351,200, 68.4 percent of units are owner-occupied, and rent runs $1,612 at the median. The county counted 108,608 housing units and 85,411 households. Seniors are 18.2 percent of the population and veterans number 31,494, so military and age relief comes up often.

  • The county issued 1,057 building permits in 2025.
  • Workers travel 26.3 minutes on average to reach a job.
  • Median household income: $81,998 (2024 dollars).

What dates and penalties apply to Okaloosa County tax bills?

Collection for the calendar year starts November 1, with notices out by then. Gross payment is accepted through March 31 and the discount ladder is below.

  • November payers keep 4 percent.
  • December payers keep 3 percent.
  • January and February drop to 2 and 1 percent.
  • March has no discount; April 1 is delinquency.

The collector's calendar adds that a 3 percent penalty hits real property taxes in April and reminder notices of unpaid taxes are mailed by April 10. Current taxes can be paid by mail, in person, online or by phone, and card payments add a bank card user fee. After delinquency the office takes cash, cashier's check or money order, and postmarks no longer count.

Who lives in Okaloosa County, and what drives its economy?

Okaloosa is a younger, more mobile county than its coastal neighbors. Residents under 18 are 22.2 percent of the population, and 81.6 percent of people lived at the same address a year before the survey. Median household income is $81,998 and per capita income is $44,070, with 10.6 percent of people in poverty.

The 2023 business count shows 6,011 employer establishments and total employment of 64,766, with annual payroll of $3,224,319 thousand. Veteran-owned employer firms numbered 575 for the 2023 reference year, and nonemployer establishments reached 21,815 in 2024.

  • College graduates make up 34.8 percent of adults.
  • Broadband reaches 93.2 percent of households.

Higher turnover means a deep buyer pool, and also more sellers who bought recently and carry a fresh assessment.

How does the Okaloosa County installment plan work?

The county offers a four-payment plan for owners whose estimated taxes exceed $100 and who do not pay through escrow. Paper or online applications are accepted until May 1.

Okaloosa installment plan schedule (source: okaloosatax.com real estate taxes page)
InstallmentDueShare and discount printed
FirstJuly 31One quarter of estimated taxes, 6 percent discount if postmarked by June 30
SecondSeptember 30One quarter, 4.5 percent discount
ThirdDecember 31One quarter plus half of any adjustment, 3 percent discount
FourthMarch 31One quarter plus the other half of the adjustment, no discount

Missing the first payment cancels the plan, and the full amount is due by March 31 of the following year. Participants are re-enrolled automatically, and discounts do not apply to delinquent payments. A sale in mid-plan leaves a remaining balance that the closing agent has to settle.

How are values and challenges handled in Okaloosa County?

Values are fixed as of January 1. Rentals and other non-homestead parcels can rise at most 10 percent a year, a cap that helps an Okaloosa investor until a sale resets it.

The proposed-tax notice arrives in August, and a petition about value must reach the clerk within 25 days. After that, taxing bodies hold budget hearings in September and October and adopt final millage in October and November.

  • January 1: value date.
  • March 1: exemption deadline.
  • April 1: tangible personal property return deadline, for owners of furnishings in a rental.

A landlord's furniture, fixtures and equipment fall under tangible personal property tax, and the collector bills it on the same discount ladder as real estate, with a 1.5 percent monthly fee added after April 1 delinquency. Compare your parcel with similar properties nearby before deciding whether to file.

What other items does the Okaloosa County Tax Collector handle?

The collector's calendar shows a year-round schedule that goes beyond the real estate bill, and some of it affects sellers with rentals or business property.

  • Tangible personal property returns go to the property appraiser by April 1, and the same discount ladder applies to the bill.
  • A 1.5 percent monthly fee is added to unpaid tangible personal property tax after April 1, and the list of delinquent taxpayers is advertised once in a local newspaper.
  • Tax warrants are issued before April 30 of the next year on unpaid tangible bills, and the collector may ask the circuit court for an order to levy and seize the property.
  • Mobile homes and recreational vehicles that are permanently affixed to the owner's land and declared real property receive a permanent RP decal, which transfers to the buyer when land and home sell together.

For an RP decal, the owner first obtains Form DR-402 from the property appraiser to show that the land and the mobile home title are in the same name. A seller with a mobile home on owned land should settle that paperwork before listing.

What exemptions matter in Okaloosa County?

With about 31,494 veterans in the county, the military-related reductions deserve a look. Relief includes a $5,000 reduction for disabled ex-servicemembers and a possible full exemption for total and permanent disability. A servicemember on orders can rent out a homestead without losing the exemption, and deployed members can claim a share through Form DR-501M.

The property appraiser also handles address changes, and the tax collector's page lists (850) 651-7240 for that office. Ask whether the optional senior exemption is in force and what income limit applies.

What happens if Okaloosa County taxes go unpaid?

Delinquent parcels are advertised weekly for three weeks at the owner's expense. The certificate sale follows on LienHub by June 1, with bids falling from 18 percent.

The certificate is a seven-year first lien, and redeeming it means paying tax, interest, penalties and advertising fees. A deed application becomes possible after two years, with the clerk of court running the auction. The collector also sells county-held certificates that earn 18 percent.

State statute adds that the opening bid on homestead land includes half of the assessed value, and the winning bidder pays a 5 percent deposit with the balance due within 24 hours. A seller with any unpaid year should clear it before listing.

What should an Okaloosa County seller do about taxes at closing?

Closing agents prorate the current year and check for any earlier balance. The year of sale is billed the next November, so the settlement figure is an estimate.

The deed is taxed at 70 cents per $100 of price. A long-time owner's capped value, which the state chart limits to 2.7 percent growth for 2026, does not pass to the buyer.

More questions about Okaloosa County, FL Property Tax Guide

What does an Okaloosa County owner pay if taxes are late?

The collector's calendar says 3 percent is added to real property taxes in April. Advertising and collection fees follow, and the total depends on the day payment arrives.

How do I join the Okaloosa County installment plan?

Apply before May 1 at the collector's office or online. Your estimated taxes must exceed $100 and cannot be paid through escrow.

When is the first Okaloosa installment due?

July 31, with a 6 percent discount if postmarked by June 30. Skip it and the plan is canceled, with the whole bill due the next March 31.

Who changes my mailing address for Okaloosa tax bills?

The property appraiser. The tax collector's page says address changes are processed there and gives (850) 651-7240 and www.okaloosapa.com.

Who conducts Okaloosa tax deed sales?

The clerk of court holds the public auction after a deed application. The tax collector handles the earlier certificate sale online.

Osceola County by the numbers

Which Osceola County office answers my tax question?

Osceola County splits the job across the Property Appraiser, the Tax Collector and the clerk and comptroller. Each has a separate phone line and a separate part of the process, so match your question to the right door.

The Property Appraiser sets assessed value and handles exemptions, tangible property returns and the tax roll. Its main number is (407) 742-5000, and its site has a tax estimator and a homestead filing page. The Tax Collector prints and mails tax notices, takes payment and runs the tax certificate process. The clerk, who doubles as county recorder, keeps the Official Records where deeds and mortgages are filed.

The Tax Collector lists four offices at 407-742-4000, all open weekdays until 4:00 pm: the main office at 2501 E. Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy in Kissimmee, one at 2595 Simpson Road in Kissimmee, a St. Cloud office at 1300 9th Street, Suite 101B, and a Campbell City office at 4730 South Orange Blossom Trail. Appointments can be booked online.

  • Osceola County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, millage page, tax estimator.
  • Osceola County Tax Collector: notices, payment, installment plan, certificates.
  • Osceola Clerk of Court and Comptroller: Official Records search, which includes a property fraud alert signup.

What dates matter on an Osceola County tax bill?

The Tax Collector's calendar runs November through March for payment, with April 1 as the delinquency date. Collection starts November 1 for the January through December assessment year, and notices normally go out by that date to the last address on the tax roll.

If a mortgage escrow pays your tax, the lender is supposed to request the bill and you get a copy. The collector reminds taxpayers that it is the owner's responsibility to make sure the tax is paid and a bill is received.

The Property Appraiser's important dates page lists January 1 as the assessment and valuation date, March 1 as the exemption filing deadline and April 1 for tangible personal property returns. The office also posts its closure days, including Veterans Day, the Thanksgiving days, Christmas Eve and Day and New Year's Day.

Osceola County tax calendar as printed by the Tax Collector and Property Appraiser
MonthEvent
January 1Assessment and valuation date
March 1Deadline to file for exemptions
March 31Gross amount due on real estate tax
April 1Unpaid real estate tax delinquent, 3 percent charge added
April 30Installment plan applications for next year due
By June 1Online sale of tax certificates
NovemberCollection opens, top discount through November 30

What early payment discounts and installment options does Osceola County offer?

Paying early cuts the bill by a set percentage that declines each month. The break starts at 4 percent for November payments and loses a point each month, reaching 1 percent in February, and March payers owe the full gross amount.

The installment plan splits the bill into four payments. Applications for the next year are due April 30. The first payment is owed by June 30. Paying it in July forfeits the discount and adds a 5 percent late charge, and missing July 31 cancels participation. Two more payments follow, on September 30 and December 31.

A separate tangible personal property bill covers furniture, fixtures and equipment in businesses and rentals, plus structural additions to mobile homes. Estimated tax over $100.00 may be paid quarterly. A landlord selling a furnished rental should ask the appraiser about the April 1 return.

  • Discounts apply to both real estate and tangible personal property bills.
  • Changes to name, address or assessed value go through the Property Appraiser, not the Tax Collector.

How does homestead work for an Osceola County seller or buyer?

The Property Appraiser's FAQ and dates page set March 1 as the filing deadline, and the benefit starts for the year you file in. State materials describe the homestead benefit as a ceiling of $50,000 in two tiers, only the first of which reaches school taxes.

The appraiser's site has a File Homestead page and a form for reporting exemption fraud, and the clerk offers a property fraud alert. If you sell, tell the appraiser; a sale or deed ends the capped assessment, and value is reset at the following January 1 valuation. A buyer who intends to live there files fresh by the March deadline.

Farmland carries its own classification, and Osceola's appraiser says it does not pass to a new owner. A buyer of pasture or grove land applies again during the January to March window, and classified parcels are re-inspected at least every three years.

What follows once Osceola County tax is delinquent?

On April 1 the unpaid tax gets a 3 percent charge, then the parcel is advertised, then a lien is sold, and after two years the certificate holder may apply for a tax deed. The Tax Collector's pages lay out the sequence.

Before the sale, the delinquent list is advertised in parcel order in a local paper for three straight weeks. By the first of June the collector runs a public online auction on LienHub. Bidding opens at 18 percent and the certificate goes to the investor who accepts the lowest rate. The certificate is a lien, not a deed, and it gives the buyer no right to enter the property.

To clear it, you pay the certificate amount plus interest at the rate it sold for, and a $6.25 redemption fee on or after June 1. County held certificates, those no investor bought, are sold later through LienHub. A certificate still open on the second April 1 after the sale lets the holder ask for a tax deed, after paying off other certificates on the parcel and the current year's tax.

  • An investor holding a certificate is barred from pressing you for payment during the first two years.
  • You can sell with a lien in place; closing pays it off.

What do the deed and tax look like at an Osceola closing?

The tax lien gets paid off at the closing table, then the deed goes into Osceola's Official Records. The deed carries Florida's stamp tax, set by statute at 70 cents for each $100 of the price, with Miami-Dade the one exception, and every signer of the deed answers for it.

State law sets a per-page recording charge, with a modernization trust fund charge and a technology charge added. The clerk collects the stamp tax at recording. Osceola's clerk has also opened a Poinciana branch office, which the clerk's site describes as expanding access.

Tax cycles matter at the table. Bills mail in November, and a closing before then leaves the new year's bill unissued. Find out from your closing agent how the year gets prorated, and keep the Tax Collector's payoff letter in your closing file. If the 10 percent non-homestead cap applied to your rental, expect the buyer's value to reset after the sale.

More questions about Osceola County, FL Property Tax Guide

What is the delinquency date for Osceola County tax?

On April 1. The Tax Collector adds a 3 percent charge to the gross amount that day, advertises the delinquent list, and runs an online lien auction by June 1.

What discounts does the Osceola County Tax Collector give?

Four percent off for November, then a point less each month through February. March brings no discount, and March 31 is the gross due date.

Where is the Osceola County Tax Collector?

Its main office is at 2501 E. Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy in Kissimmee. Others sit on Simpson Road in Kissimmee, in St. Cloud and in Campbell City, all on the 407-742-4000 line.

How do I redeem an Osceola County tax certificate?

Pay the certificate amount plus interest at the rate it sold for, and a $6.25 fee when redeeming on or after June 1. Contact the Tax Collector for the exact payoff.

Does back tax stop me from selling in Osceola County?

Yes, because the lien rides with the parcel and the payoff is deducted at closing. Before you sign, phone 407-742-4000 and ask the Tax Collector for the number.

Santa Rosa County by the numbers

Which Santa Rosa County offices deal with property tax?

Santa Rosa County divides the job three ways. The Property Appraiser (SRCPA, at srcpa.gov) sets values and exemptions, the Tax Collector (srctc.com) mails and collects the bill, and a Value Adjustment Board hears appeals.

The collector's pages explain the chain. The appraiser sets assessed value and exemption eligibility, the county commission, school board and other levying bodies set millage, and the finished roll goes to the collector, who prints and mails the notices. Bills go to the owner's last address on the roll, and a mortgage company that pays through escrow should request the bill. Its offices are in Milton, Midway, Pace and Jay.

The appraiser's home page reports county statistics that show the scale of the roll: about 99.4 thousand residential properties, 8 thousand commercial, 5.4 thousand agricultural, and a taxable county value of 20.29 billion dollars.

  • Value, exemptions, name and address: Property Appraiser.
  • Bill, payment, delinquency, certificates: Tax Collector.
  • Appeals of assessments, denied exemptions and deferrals: Value Adjustment Board, made up of three county commissioners and two school board members or a special master.

Because the office split is clean, a seller can settle most questions with two calls: the appraiser for what the parcel is valued at and which exemptions it carries, and the collector for what is owed and by when.

What is the Santa Rosa County payment schedule?

Statements are normally in the mail by November 1 for the calendar tax year, and the gross amount is due March 31. Early payment earns a discount that drops each month.

Santa Rosa County Tax Collector discount schedule for real estate
Month paidDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchNone
April 1 onwardDelinquent, 3% penalty; advertising fees added May 1

The collector adds that a discount window closing on a weekend or legal holiday stays open until the next business day. The collector puts the burden on the owner to make sure a bill arrives, so call the office if none shows up.

What happens if Santa Rosa County taxes go delinquent?

A 3 percent penalty is added on April 1, and after that only cashier's check, money order, cash or credit card are accepted. The date the office receives the payment determines the amount due.

Delinquent parcels must be advertised for three weeks in a local paper, and the county commission gives that job to the lowest bidder. The cost lands on the delinquent bill. By June 1 the collector holds the certificate sale online through LienHub.com, as a reverse auction that opens at 18 percent interest and goes to the lowest bidder.

  • A certificate is a lien, and the office states that buying one gives no ownership rights.
  • Unpaid amounts rise right away if the county holds the certificate and it is purchased, or if a tax deed application is made.
  • The office warns that losing the property is possible when taxes stay unpaid.

Under the state statute summary, a certificate holder may file for a tax deed only after two years have passed since April 1 of the issue year, and the holder may not contact the owner to demand payment during those two years. Homestead parcels also carry an opening bid that includes half of the latest assessed value.

A seller in this position needs a fresh payoff statement, because the total grows as costs are added.

How do Santa Rosa County homestead filing dates work?

The appraiser's Dates to Remember box lists a homestead filing period from January 1, 2027 to March 1, 2027. The same box gives January 1 to June 1, 2027 for the Persons 65 or Over exemption and for the Deployed Service Member exemption.

Filing is online. Search for your parcel on the appraiser's site, then click Apply for Exemptions, after updating your Florida ID and vehicle registration to the home address. The state revenue agency sets the base rules: the owner must make the property the permanent residence by January 1 and file with the county property appraiser by March 1. The first $25,000 of the exemption applies to all levies, and the additional amount applies only to non-school levies on value above $50,000.

State law lets a county or city add a senior exemption worth up to $50,000 by ordinance, within an income limit, plus a 25-year version for homes valued under $250,000. Ask the appraiser which of those Santa Rosa taxing authorities have adopted. Veterans rated 10 percent or more for a service-connected disability can qualify for a $5,000 reduction (ss. 196.081 and 196.091).

What changes at a Santa Rosa County sale?

For the next owner the parcel starts over at just value, and the seller's exemptions leave with the seller. Florida defines change of ownership broadly: a sale, foreclosure or transfer of legal or beneficial title, except where the same person stays entitled or a spouse transfers.

Santa Rosa's appraiser sends a Property Owner Protection Alert about letters that offer a copy of your deed for a fee. The businesses mailing them have no official capacity, and the offices of the Property Appraiser and the Clerk of Courts did not approve or take part in those mailings. A seller who receives one can skip the fee offer and request the deed from the Clerk.

Documentary stamps on a deed run $0.70 per $100 of price, and price includes any mortgage the buyer takes over. The Clerk collects at recording. If a tax certificate or tax deed matter exists, s. 197.542 has the winning bidder at a deed sale post a deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater.

How can a Santa Rosa County seller handle tax due at closing?

Have the closing agent order a tax payoff and apply it at closing. The collector's online parcel search shows the balance, and the Milton, Midway, Pace and Jay branches answer questions in person. If a lender escrows your taxes, the servicer requests the bill, and the payoff still needs confirming before closing.

Another thing worth knowing is that Santa Rosa's collector is explicit about who answers what. Questions on legal description, value, exemptions and name or address changes belong with the appraiser at srcpa.gov, while rates belong to the taxing authorities that hold advertised public hearings. Non-ad valorem charges, which the collector says typically cover fire departments, street lighting, paving and special local projects, come from local levying agencies, so ask the agency named on the bill.

For a deeper bill review, ask the appraiser how your parcel's assessed value compares with its just value, since the gap is the Save Our Homes benefit the buyer will lose. The state revenue agency lists a 3.4% CPI for 2024 with a 3.0% cap, 2.9% for 2025 and 2.7% for 2026.

More questions about Santa Rosa County, FL Property Tax Guide

What is the Santa Rosa County payment schedule?

The gross amount is due by March 31, with bills mailed on or before November 1. Payments in November earn 4%, December 3%, January 2% and February 1%.

What is the late penalty in Santa Rosa County?

A 3 percent penalty is added on April 1 for unpaid real estate accounts. Advertising fees are added on May 1, and a tax certificate sale follows by June 1.

Where do I file Santa Rosa County homestead?

Use the Apply for Exemptions button on your parcel page at the appraiser's site. The posted homestead period for 2027 runs January 1 to March 1.

Who hears a Santa Rosa County assessment appeal?

The Value Adjustment Board. It hears denied exemptions, assessment petitions and tax deferral appeals. the state revenue agency sets a 25 day window after the TRIM notice for a value petition.

Does the county sell my house when I miss a payment?

Not directly. The county sells a tax certificate, which is a lien starting at 18 percent interest, and only a later tax deed application can lead to a sale of the property.

St Johns County by the numbers

How fast is St. Johns County growing?

St. Johns County is one of the faster-growing counties in Florida, up 26.7 percent between the April 2020 base of 273,426 and the July 2025 estimate of 346,328. For a seller, growth means a lot of recent construction nearby: the Census Bureau counted 4,735 building permits in 2025.

St. Johns spans about 600.6 square miles of land, with 455.2 residents per square mile in 2020. Owners live in 82.2 percent of the homes, so most competing listings are single-family homes. The table gives the main numbers.

Which office does what on a St. Johns County property tax bill?

The Saint Johns County Property Appraiser values the property and handles exemptions, while the county tax collector mails the bill in November. The appraiser's website also hosts a property tax estimator, a new-owner guide and a property damage guide, all useful when a house changes hands.

The Value Adjustment Board hears disputes about value or exemption denials, and the clerk of court records the deed. Taxing bodies, including the school board and municipalities, set the millage rates after public hearings advertised on the TRIM notice.

What are the key property tax dates in St. Johns County?

The appraiser's date page gives the cycle: January 1 sets the status and condition of the property, and March 1 is the filing deadline for homestead and other personal exemptions, agricultural classification and organizational exemptions. Tangible personal property returns for businesses are filed between January 1 and April 1.

Notices of proposed taxes arrive in August or September, and they list public hearing dates on millage. Tax bills follow in November. The 2026 deadline was moved to March 2 because March 1 fell on a weekend, which the office explains as the rule when the date lands on a weekend.

  • January 1: condition and ownership fix eligibility.
  • March 1 (or next business day): exemption filing.
  • April 1: business personal property returns.
  • August to September: TRIM notices.
  • November: bills mailed.

What is the St. Johns County homestead exemption worth?

For tax year 2026 the appraiser prints a total homestead exemption of $51,411. The first $25,000 reaches all taxes including school taxes, and the remaining $26,411 applies to assessed value between $50,000 and $75,000, excluding school taxes.

You must own the home and live there as your permanent residence on January 1. The office asks for a Florida driver license or ID showing the homestead address and Social Security numbers for the applicant and spouse. A trust owner who is not a trustee may need to supply the trust. Placing the home in an LLC ends the exemption and removes caps, because the office treats that as a change of ownership.

Late filers with just cause can apply until the end of the TRIM period, typically late August.

What happens to the Save Our Homes cap when a St. Johns County house sells?

The buyer starts over, and the seller may take the benefit along. A homesteaded property's assessed value cannot rise more than 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is less, but a sale resets the property to market value on the next January 1.

The seller can move up to $500,000 of accumulated difference to a new Florida home through portability. St. Johns County's appraiser says the transfer must occur within three tax years, counted January through December from the sale, and a December sale counts as one tax year. If you downsize, the benefit is scaled by the ratio of the new just value to the old one. All owners of the old home who also own the new one must apply together. Portability does not cross state lines. Non-homestead property has a separate 10 percent cap that cannot be ported.

What do deed taxes and recording cost on a St. Johns County sale?

Seventy cents for each $100 of price is the stamp rate, and no surtax follows it here because the Miami-Dade schedule is the only exception. The department of revenue says every party named on the deed shares liability, so settle the question in writing.

Statute puts the clerk's first page at $5.00 and later pages at $4.00, with trust fund and technology additions. A mortgage that stays on the house counts toward the price. A spouse-to-spouse deed whose only consideration is the mortgage on the marital homestead is listed as exempt.

How can a St. Johns County owner dispute an assessment?

File a petition with the Value Adjustment Board within 25 days of the TRIM notice, using one of the DR-486 forms, which the state says go to the clerk. The notice itself prints the exact deadline, so check it the day it arrives.

The appraiser's site has a Value Adjustment Board page and a Property Owner Bill of Rights for owners who want to understand the process first. If the dispute is a denied exemption, classification or portability claim, the state allows a petition in the 30 days after a denial letter goes out. A seller who thinks the value is too high should raise it before listing, since a lower assessed value changes the buyer's carrying cost estimate.

Which other exemptions apply to St. Johns County sellers and buyers?

The appraiser lists other exemptions and an agricultural classification on separate pages, and the state adds age and veteran benefits. Some 22.5 percent of residents are 65 and over, so the senior options are worth a look.

  • Age 65 or older: local ordinances may allow an added homestead exemption of up to $50,000 when household income is within the limit.
  • Disabled former servicemembers with a rating of 10 percent or more: a $5,000 reduction in assessed value.
  • Veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability: a discount equal to the disability percentage on homestead.
  • Deployed servicemembers: an exemption matching the share of the prior year deployed.

A buyer who closes after January 1 cannot claim homestead for that year, so ask the appraiser how the first partial year will be billed.

What if taxes go unpaid on a St. Johns County property?

The unpaid balance becomes delinquent April 1, and certificates must be sold on unpaid items by June 1. A title company will want the balance cleared out of the seller's proceeds.

A certificate holder may apply for a tax deed once two years pass from April 1 of the issue year, paying a $75 application fee. Where the land is homestead, the starting bid adds half of the latest assessed value. Homestead owners can ask the tax collector about deferral by March 31.

  • Obtain a payoff statement early.
  • Ask whether any certificate exists on the parcel.
  • Check the escrow account when a lender pays.

More questions about St. Johns County, FL Property Tax Guide

What is the 2026 homestead exemption total in St. Johns County?

$51,411, as printed by the St. Johns County Property Appraiser: $25,000 on all taxes and $26,411 on non-school taxes over $50,000 of assessed value.

When is the exemption deadline in St. Johns County?

March 1, or the next business day when it falls on a weekend, which made it March 2 in 2026. Late filers with just cause can apply until the TRIM period ends.

Does a St. Johns County buyer inherit the seller's capped value?

No. The sale resets the property to market value the next January 1, and the seller's cap and exemptions end with the sale.

Can I rent out my St. Johns County homestead?

Renting the whole home for more than 30 days in two consecutive tax years can cost you the exemption, according to the appraiser. Renting a garage apartment removes only that part.

Is there a deed tax on St. Johns County sales?

Yes. Documentary stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, paid to the clerk at the recording counter.

St Lucie County by the numbers

What kind of county is St. Lucie County for a seller?

St. Lucie County grew from 329,226 people in April 2020 to an estimated 402,449 in July 2025, a 22.2 percent gain. Its land area is 571.66 square miles, with 575.9 residents per square mile counted in 2020.

Owners' homes were typically worth $347,300 in the 2020 to 2024 data and rent ran $1,585. Owners occupy 78.6 percent of homes, and one resident in four, 24.9 percent, is 65 or over, which makes the senior and deferral options below worth a close read.

Who handles property tax in St. Lucie County?

Three county offices matter. The Saint Lucie County Property Appraiser values property and processes exemptions; the St. Lucie County Tax Collector sends bills and takes payments; and the Clerk of the Circuit Court runs the Value Adjustment Board process and records deeds.

The property appraiser's office lists a phone line of 772-462-1000 on its TRIM notice page for questions about value or exemptions. Exemption questions belong with the appraiser, not the collector.

When does the St. Lucie County TRIM notice arrive, and what can an owner do with it?

The property appraiser mails the notice in mid-August to the owner of record of every parcel. It is an estimate rather than a bill, built from proposed millage rates, the January 1 value and any exemptions.

The notice shows three columns: last year's figures, what taxes would be if each taxing authority kept its revenue flat, and what they would be at the proposed rate. It also lists budget hearing dates and the deadline for a Value Adjustment Board petition over value, classification or an exemption. For 2026 that deadline was September 8, which has passed. Future deadlines are printed on each year's notice.

A buyer should note that the notice explains why a bill jumps after a purchase: reassessment on January 1 and removal of the prior owner's exemptions and caps.

What are the St. Lucie County tax discounts and deadlines?

The tax collector publishes a month-by-month list. The early-payment discount shrinks from 4 percent in November to 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February, which the state revenue department prints the same way.

The collector's calendar also gives January 31 as its deadline for homestead tax deferral, while the state's general guidance names March 31 following the assessment year, so ask the St. Lucie office which date governs your application. March 1 is the deadline to file new homestead exemptions with the property appraiser.

  • November: 4 percent discount, bills issued.
  • December: 3 percent.
  • January: 2 percent.
  • February: 1 percent.
  • April 1: unpaid taxes turn delinquent.

How does Save Our Homes affect a St. Lucie County sale?

The appraiser's TRIM guide explains it plainly: a property bought in a given year is reassessed and the prior owner's exemptions and caps are removed, which can lift the tax bill. For sellers, that is the reason a listing's current tax figure understates what a buyer will pay.

The Save Our Homes cap limits assessment growth on a homestead to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is lower, and starts accruing after the first year of homestead. The 2026 cap on the state's chart was 2.7 percent. Sellers who buy another Florida home can transfer up to $500,000 of the accumulated difference through portability, using Form DR-501T by March 1, provided the new homestead is set up within three years.

What does a St. Lucie County deed cost at closing?

Stamp tax runs seventy cents per $100 of price under the statute and the revenue department's page. The Miami-Dade surtax does not reach St. Lucie.

Each signer is liable, so the sale contract should pick who funds it. The fee statute sets clerk charges at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 per added page plus add-ons. Deeds in lieu of foreclosure and trustee's deeds are taxable. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is not.

Which tax breaks can a St. Lucie County homeowner claim?

The standard homestead exemption is up to $50,000 under state law, split into a first $25,000 that covers school taxes and an added slice for non-school taxes on assessed value above $50,000. The added slice is indexed to inflation each January 1.

Beyond that, the state lists several options an owner may qualify for:

  • An added exemption for owners 65 or older where a local ordinance allows it and household income is within the limit.
  • A $5,000 reduction for disabled former servicemembers rated 10 percent or more.
  • A homestead discount equal to the VA disability percentage for veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability.
  • Homestead tax deferral, with the tax collector, for taxes above a share of household income.

Ask the property appraiser which of these apply to your parcel before the March 1 deadline. An owner who missed it should still call, since the notice window in August also lets the office hear exemption disputes through the Value Adjustment Board.

What should an heir or seller who lived elsewhere check in St. Lucie County?

Start with whether homestead is still in place. State rules say homestead ends if the house is rented, stops being the permanent home or the owner leaves Florida as a permanent resident. Renting the home is the usual way owners lose it without noticing.

Then look at the title. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed as not taxable for documentary stamps, but a deed with no probate has no estate planning exception. Confirm the parcel number on the property appraiser's record card, which the appraiser's site offers through its real estate search. Finally ask the tax collector for a payoff, since taxes unpaid after April 1 can reach the certificate stage and a certificate holder may later apply for a tax deed.

These steps cost little and keep a sale of a St. Lucie County house from stalling at the closing table.

What if a St. Lucie County owner is behind on taxes?

Delinquency starts April 1. By June 1 the collector sells certificates, and the lowest interest bid wins; unsold ones go to the county at the top rate.

Two years after April 1 of the issue year, a holder may ask for a tax deed. On a homestead the opening bid includes half the latest assessed value. A sale cannot close cleanly with a certificate outstanding, so ask the collector for a payoff.

  • Order a certificate search through the title company.
  • Ask whether a homestead deferral lien exists.
  • Settle any delinquent balance out of the seller's payout.

More questions about St. Lucie County, FL Property Tax Guide

When is the St. Lucie County homestead filing deadline?

March 1 of the tax year, filed with the property appraiser. You must have owned and lived in the home as your permanent residence on January 1.

Does St. Lucie County mail the tax bill in November?

Yes, the tax collector issues bills in November, the month the 4 percent early-payment discount applies. A buyer or seller closing that month should ask the title agent whether the bill is paid and at what discount.

Why did my St. Lucie County taxes jump after buying?

The property is reassessed to market value and the prior owner's exemptions and caps are removed, which the property appraiser's TRIM guide describes.

Who do I call in St. Lucie County about my property value?

The Property Appraiser's office, which lists 772-462-1000 on its TRIM notice page.

Does St. Lucie County have a deed transfer tax?

Yes, Florida's documentary stamp tax at 70 cents per $100 of consideration, owed through the clerk at recording.

Sumter County by the numbers

Why is Sumter County unusual for a seller?

Seniors dominate Sumter County. The Census Bureau counts 57.6 percent of residents at 65 or above, and just 7.6 percent under 18. Headcount reached an estimated 157,772 by mid-2025, a rise of 21.6 percent over the 2020 base of 129,752.

A household averages 1.93 people, and owners live in 87.6 percent of homes. Only 25.8 percent of adults 16 and up are in the civilian labor force. Buyers in such a market tend to ask hard questions about yearly carrying costs, so a seller does well to know the tax picture.

How much is Sumter County building?

Land area comes to 557.13 square miles. Crowding is still light, though it climbed from 170.8 people per square mile in 2010 to 232.9 in 2020. The mid-2025 count of homes was 95,691, and 3,516 permits were issued in 2025.

With that much permitting, a resale can sit next to new homes. Census data for 2020 to 2024 give a typical owned home at $385,400, and owners paid a median $1,686 monthly with a mortgage against $602 without.

Which Sumter County offices handle property tax?

In Sumter the appraiser values land and decides exemptions, while a separate collector sends the bills. The county's clerk of court also keeps the file for the Value Adjustment Board.

The county's board page lists five seats: two commissioners, one school board member, and two citizens, one named by each body. It hears appeals about value, classification and exemptions, leaves rates to the taxing authorities, and may not lower a value or give an exemption because of hardship. Qualified appraisers or attorneys serve as special magistrates, hear each petition and recommend a ruling.

What dates drive the Sumter County tax year?

Sumter follows the statewide calendar. January 1 fixes the assessment, March 1 closes homestead and classification filing, and April 1 is for personal property returns.

August brings the proposed-tax notice and a 25-day clock to petition. A denied exemption or portability claim has its own 30-day clock from the date the letter was mailed. Bills show up in November with a sliding discount of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent through February, and April 1 marks delinquency.

  • Mar. 1: file for homestead.
  • Aug.: proposed-tax notice arrives.
  • 25 days on: value petition closes.
  • Nov.: bills, top discount.
  • Apr. 1: unpaid taxes delinquent.

How do homestead and portability work for Sumter County sellers?

Homestead reduces taxable value by as much as $50,000; the first $25,000 touches school taxes, the rest does not. Be living there on January 1, then apply on Form DR-501 at the appraiser's office.

After a sale the house is reassessed at market value, so the buyer's first full bill may far exceed the seller's. A seller staying in Florida can carry up to $500,000 of capped difference to the next homestead if it is set up within three years; Form DR-501T goes in with the application. Leaving the state forfeits it, because portability only links Florida homes.

Can a Sumter County owner dispute a value without a lawyer?

Yes. The petition goes through the clerk, who also acts as clerk to the Value Adjustment Board, and a special magistrate hears the case. The magistrate is independent of the property appraiser, so you present evidence of value, such as recent comparable sales, repair estimates or errors in the property record.

The panel looks only at whether value, classification or exemption is right. A tight household budget does not move the outcome. Sellers with a contract pending should tell the title agent about any open petition so that the closing statement handles the tax correctly.

Which exemptions matter most in a county this old?

Many Sumter County sales will touch age or veteran benefits. Counties and cities may adopt an added homestead exemption of up to $50,000 for owners over 65 with limited income, and a larger one equal to assessed value for 25-year residents whose home is worth under $250,000.

  • Older veterans with a lasting service-connected disability: discount matching the VA rating.
  • Former servicemembers rated 10 percent or more disabled: $5,000 off assessed value.
  • Total, permanent service-connected disability: possibly full relief on homestead.

Ask the Sumter County Property Appraiser which local ordinances add to this list and how a surviving spouse is treated.

How does a Sumter County buyer's first tax bill differ from the seller's?

Expect a jump. The seller may have been living under the Save Our Homes limit, which holds yearly increases to the lower of 3 percent or the inflation change (2.7 percent for 2026 on the state's chart). Once the deed records, the house is valued at market on the following January 1 and the limit starts over for the buyer.

A buyer who gets homestead in the first year also needs to apply by March 1, since the exemption is not automatic. Both sides gain from knowing this before closing, because the old bill on the listing sheet is a poor guide to the new one.

  • Seller's capped value does not transfer.
  • Buyer applies for homestead after taking title and living there on January 1.
  • Seller who moves within Florida may port the savings.

What can cancel a Sumter County homestead before a sale?

Three events end it: renting the home out, ceasing to use it as the permanent residence, or no longer being a Florida permanent resident.

Owners who move away before listing should speak with the appraiser about their status. One exception: a servicemember may rent out the homestead without abandoning the exemption. Seller and listing agent should confirm the status before preparing the tax proration, and buyers should ask what exemptions the parcel carried last year.

What does a Sumter County deed cost at closing?

Stamp tax is seventy cents for each hundred dollars of price. A mortgage the buyer takes over is added to the price.

Everyone on the deed is liable, so let the contract say who funds it. The clerk bills $5.00 on page one and $4.00 afterward, plus add-ons. A probated estate gets relief because a personal representative's deed is listed as not taxable; a family deed made only for estate planning gets none.

What happens to a Sumter County house with unpaid tax?

Overdue taxes become certificates sold by June 1, and a holder can seek a deed after two years. At the clerk's tax deed auction the winner leaves 5 percent or $200, whichever is larger, and pays the balance in 24 hours, weekends and holidays excluded.

Paying at closing avoids all of it, and a title company will normally insist on that anyway. A homestead parcel is further protected, since its opening bid in a tax deed sale includes half of the latest assessed value. Request a payoff and a certificate search before you sign a contract.

More questions about Sumter County, FL Property Tax Guide

What share of Sumter County is 65 or older?

Over half: the Census Bureau reports 57.6 percent.

When is the Sumter County homestead deadline?

March 1, filed with the Sumter County Property Appraiser.

Who hears assessment appeals in Sumter County?

The Value Adjustment Board, an independent five-member panel, with hearings run by special magistrates. The clerk serves as its clerk.

Can the board cut a Sumter County value for hardship?

No. The county's page says it cannot change an assessed value or grant an exemption or classification based on personal hardship.

Does a Sumter County seller pay a deed tax?

Yes: seventy cents per $100 of price, owed at the clerk's counter. The contract decides which party actually pays, and every signer stays liable to the state regardless.

Monroe County by the numbers

Who bills and collects property tax in Monroe County, Florida?

In the Keys, valuation and collection sit in separate buildings. One elected office decides what a parcel is worth and who gets an exemption; another prints the notices and takes the payments. A seller in Key West and a seller in Key Largo deal with the same two offices, just at different counters.

The collector's page walks through the chain: the appraiser's January value, plus millage from the commission and other taxing bodies, becomes the roll that is certified for collection. Notices go to the address of record on that roll. Escrow lenders request the bill themselves, so the owner may only receive a copy.

Statute 197.122, quoted on that page, makes it the owner's job to learn what is due and pay it before delinquency, bill or no bill. A separate bill goes out for each parcel, matched to the way the deed is recorded, so an owner of two lots should expect two notices.

What does the Census say about housing in the Keys?

Monroe County has few people for its size. QuickFacts shows 80,406 residents for mid-2025, a 3.0 percent dip against 2020, and 983.04 square miles of land, which worked out to 84.3 people per square mile in 2020.

Price and tax planning start with the housing numbers. The five-year survey data gives $780,600 as the median value of an owner-occupied home, with 65.8 percent of units lived in by their owners and 56,009 units counted in 2025. Rent at the median is $1,999 a month. Older residents are 27.2 percent of the county, so the senior and homestead programs below see heavy use.

  • Veterans counted for 2020 to 2024: 5,674, so the veteran exemptions listed further down apply to a real share of owners.
  • Mean commute: 19.5 minutes.
  • Permits for new construction counted in 2025: 279, a small number for a county of this size.

Where can I deal with the Monroe County Tax Collector in person?

The tax collector runs five offices along the Keys, and every one of them handles property tax. The table below is taken from the office locations page and shows the property tax counters in each town.

Monroe County Tax Collector offices that take property tax (source: monroetaxcollector.com office locations page)

The page warns that services and hours vary by location. Mailed payments go to the post office box on that page, and overnight or priority mail goes to the Key West street address. For a missing bill, the office number printed on the property tax page is (305) 295-5044.

Who lives in Monroe County, and what do they do for work?

The Census profile shows an older, higher-income and international county. Median household income for 2020 to 2024 is $87,738 in 2024 dollars and per capita income is $59,543, with 10.9 percent of people in poverty. About one resident in five was born abroad (19.8 percent), and 22.2 percent of those over age 5 use another language at home.

Visitor spending shows in the 2022 business numbers: accommodation and food services sales totaled $2,245,213 thousand, and retail sales were $2,157,198 thousand, or $26,430 per resident. In 2023 the county had 4,154 employer establishments and total employment of 37,134, up 5.4 percent from 2022.

  • College graduates: 38.6 percent of adults.
  • Broadband at home: 89.9 percent of households.

For a seller, this means a buyer pool that often includes second-home buyers and remote workers, who may pay a different amount in tax than the current owner does.

How should a Keys owner prepare an appeal or a correction?

Begin with the August proposed-tax notice. A value challenge uses a DR-486 petition that the clerk must receive within 25 days, so write the deadline on the notice the day it arrives.

A denied exemption has its own 30 day petition clock. Owners of furnished rentals or business equipment also file Form DR-405 by April 1.

  • Gather recent sales of similar properties on your island or key before you file.
  • Photograph any damage that existed on January 1, since value is set on that date.
  • Keep the notice and your filing receipt together.

Ask the appraiser for the comparable sales behind your value.

What is the Monroe County tax calendar for bills and discounts?

The collector's page says statements normally mail by November 1 and that March is the last month at full price.

  • November: 4 percent off.
  • December brings 3 percent.
  • January brings 2 percent, and February brings 1 percent.
  • March is the gross amount with no discount.

On April 1 an unpaid account turns delinquent, and tax certificates are sold by June 1. The collector's page lists three alternatives to a lump sum: a quarterly installment plan, a statutory partial payment plan and a homestead tax deferral program.

How do homestead and Save Our Homes affect a Keys sale?

A capped assessment is a benefit tied to the owner, and it ends when the house sells. In a county where the typical owned home is valued at $780,600, the distance between a long-held capped value and a fresh assessment can be wide.

The exemption takes up to $50,000 off taxable value if filed by March 1. Yearly growth in assessed value is held below the lesser of 3 percent or CPI, which the state chart pegs at 2.7 percent for 2026. After a sale, the next January 1 assessment starts from just value for the new owner. If you are buying again in Florida, ask the appraiser about portability, which has a three year window.

What other exemptions might a Monroe County owner have?

With 5,674 veterans and a 27.2 percent senior share, Monroe County owners often ask about relief tied to service and age. The state lists a $5,000 assessed value reduction for a disabled ex-servicemember, a homestead discount for qualifying veterans 65 and older, and a possible total exemption for permanent and total disability.

Seniors may also benefit from an optional local ordinance. Ask the property appraiser whether Monroe County or a city in it has adopted one, and what income limit applies.

How are taxes and deed costs handled when a Keys house closes?

The title company usually divides the sale year's tax between the parties on the settlement statement. A spring or summer closing happens before that year's bill exists, so the figure is an estimate.

Keys deeds carry state stamp tax at 70 cents per $100 of price (section 201.02), unlike Miami-Dade. Payment goes to the clerk. The clerk's page charges under section 28.24 start at $5.00 for the first page.

Unpaid taxes lead to a certificate sale and, years later, a clerk-run deed auction. Pay off any open year before closing.

More questions about Monroe County, FL Property Tax Guide

When does the Monroe County bill stop being penalty free?

Pay by March 31. That is when the gross amount falls due, and April 1 starts delinquency. Earlier payment, November through February, shrinks the bill by 4, 3, 2 or 1 percent.

Who answers questions about a lost Monroe County bill?

The tax collector. Its property tax page lists (305) 295-5044 for missing statements, and each parcel gets its own bill according to how the deed is recorded.

Does a Keys homeowner's capped value go to the buyer?

No. The buyer's first assessment starts at just value. You may be able to carry part of the savings to your next Florida homestead through portability.

Can I pay Monroe County taxes in installments?

Yes, through the tax collector's quarterly installment plan, a statutory partial payment option or a homestead deferral. State guidance sets May 1 as the application date.

Who runs a tax deed auction in Monroe County?

The county clerk holds the auction, as the collector's public records page says, so overbid or surplus questions go to the clerk.

Nassau County by the numbers

Why does Nassau County's growth matter for a home sale?

QuickFacts reports 106,879 residents in 2025 against 90,352 counted in the 2020 census, a rise of 18.3 percent on the revised base, inside 648.68 square miles of land.

Survey data puts the typical owned home at $382,800, with 82.7 percent of homes owner-occupied and carrying costs of $1,849 a month for those with a mortgage. The county counted 49,001 housing units in 2025 and 1,060 building permits that year.

  • Households: 39,307, averaging 2.47 people.
  • Residents 65 and older: 26.7 percent.
  • Mean commute: 30.1 minutes.

Ask the property appraiser how your parcel's assessed value compares with its just value, since that gap is what a sale erases.

What does the Nassau County Tax Collector say about estimating a tax bill?

The tax collector tells buyers never to treat a seller's past or current tax amount as a forecast. A new owner does not inherit the prior owner's assessed value, Save Our Homes cap or exemptions.

The same page explains that the property appraiser can help estimate upcoming taxes, but that office does not see non-ad valorem assessments such as community development district fees. Those fees are added to the bill separately, and the estimate must come from the district itself. If your Nassau neighborhood sits inside a district, tell your buyer so that the closing numbers include it.

Sellers can use this to set expectations early. A buyer reading your old bill may expect a lower figure than reality, and a clear note about reassessment avoids a surprise at the table.

Who lives in Nassau County, and where do they work?

Nassau County skews toward families who own their homes and commute. QuickFacts lists median household income of $89,804 for 2020 to 2024 and per capita income of $47,685, with 8.7 percent of residents below the poverty line. Broadband subscriptions reach 94.6 percent of households, and 87.4 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

Employer establishments numbered 2,261 in 2023, with total employment of 21,651. Accommodation and food services brought in $613,642 thousand in 2022, and retail sales were $1,305,109 thousand, or $13,341 per resident.

  • Residents under 18: 18.8 percent.
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or higher: 35.6 percent.
  • Foreign-born share: 3.9 percent.

Long commutes and fast growth mean that buyers often arrive from other parts of Florida or other states, so expect questions about new construction, district fees and taxes.

What is the Nassau County bill-and-discount schedule?

Payment runs on a sliding monthly discount that ends March 31. Anything left unpaid becomes delinquent April 1.

  • November payment: 4 percent off.
  • December: 3 percent.
  • January: 2 percent.
  • February: 1 percent.

Florida's revenue department places the property appraiser's notice of proposed taxes in August, public budget hearings in September and October, and tax bills in November. A value challenge goes to the clerk's value adjustment board petition process within 25 days of the notice of proposed property taxes.

For questions about a bill, call the tax collector's tax department at 904-491-7420, the number printed on its partial payment page.

What should a Nassau County seller tell a buyer about the tax bill?

Give the buyer the parcel's real situation, not a rule of thumb. The tax collector's own advice is that a buyer should never rely on a seller's current or past tax amount, and a clear explanation protects both sides before a contract is signed.

  • Say whether a homestead exemption and a capped value are on the roll today, and that neither carries over.
  • Name any community development district or other non-ad valorem assessment, and give the buyer the district's contact so the buyer can ask for the amount.
  • Explain whether taxes are escrowed. If a lender pays, partial payments are discouraged and the lender sets the timing.
  • Mention any unpaid prior year, since the lien follows the land.

A buyer who learns these things at the start is less likely to ask for a credit late in the deal. Sellers who offer a plain written summary, along with a printout from the property appraiser's estimate tool, make closing day smoother. A tax bill estimate from the appraiser will leave out district fees, so ask the title company to add them.

How do exemptions and capped values work for Nassau owners?

Exemptions come from the property appraiser, who takes applications each year. With 26.7 percent of residents age 65 or older and 8,635 veterans, the senior and military programs see steady use in Nassau.

A county or city may adopt an extra senior exemption within an income limit, and another ordinance may help long-term residents with lower-value homes. Ask the property appraiser which of these apply in Nassau County or its towns.

  • A $5,000 reduction in assessed value for a disabled ex-servicemember.
  • A homestead discount for veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability.
  • A possible full homestead exemption for total and permanent disability.

A rented unit cannot keep homestead, so a landlord selling a former residence should confirm what is on the roll.

Is a partial payment allowed in Nassau County?

It is allowed, with costs spelled out by the collector. Section 197.374 allows partial payment on a current-year bill, and the office accepts them from November 1 through March 31 with the postmark counting.

  • The account loses the early-payment discount, even if the balance is later cleared in a discount month.
  • Escrowed accounts paid by a lender should not make partial payments.
  • Accounts on an installment plan should skip partial payments.
  • Whatever is unpaid on April 1 enters the delinquent process of advertising and a certificate sale.

To set one up, contact the tax department at 904-491-7420 or taxes@nassautaxes.com. Payments can be made in person, by mail or online once the account is set up.

What happens to unpaid Nassau County taxes?

The tax collector must hold a tax certificate sale on or before June 1, and it is conducted online on the LienHub platform. The table lays out the terms as the office prints them.

Nassau tax certificate terms (source: nassautaxes.com delinquent real estate taxes page)
ItemAs printed
Sale deadlineOn or before June 1 each year
BiddingDownward on interest, starting at 18 percent; lowest bidder wins
Minimum earned5 percent until accrued interest exceeds it; zero-interest bids earn zero
Lien statusEnforceable first lien on the real estate
ValiditySeven years from issuance
Tax deed applicationWhen two or more years have passed since delinquency

To remove the lien, the owner pays the collector all delinquent tax plus interest, costs and other charges. State law also bars a certificate holder from demanding payment from the owner for two years after April 1 of the issuance year, and a deed application carries a $75 fee. Homestead land with a small delinquency goes to the county rather than to a bidder.

How do homestead rules and deed taxes affect a Nassau County sale?

The standard exemption takes up to $50,000 off taxable value, filed by March 1, and the capped assessment growth was 2.7 percent for 2026 per the state chart. A buyer's value starts over after a sale.

Deed stamps in Nassau follow section 201.02 at 70 cents on every $100 of price. Liability sits with all parties to the deed, and payment goes to the clerk at recording.

More questions about Nassau County, FL Property Tax Guide

Does a new Nassau County owner get the seller's tax amount?

No. The tax collector says the buyer does not benefit from the prior owner's assessed value, Save Our Homes cap or exemptions, so past bills are not a safe estimate.

Do community development district fees show on the appraiser's estimate?

No. The appraiser has no access to non-ad valorem assessments, so ask the district for its amount, which is then added to the tax bill.

Do I lose the discount if I make a partial payment in Nassau County?

Yes. Per the tax collector, the account is no longer eligible for discount even if the rest is paid during a discount month. Partial payments run November 1 through March 31.

When does Nassau County sell tax certificates?

The sale is held by June 1 each year on the LienHub site. Bids start at 18 percent and fall, and the lowest rate takes the certificate.

How long before a tax deed can be sought on a Nassau County parcel?

The certificate holder may apply when two or more years have passed since delinquency. Until then, the owner can redeem by paying taxes, interest, costs and charges.

Due dates and discounts

  • Installment plan: applications due April 30; prior year taxes must exceed $100.00 and not be escrowed. 1st installment due June 30 with 6% discount; 2nd due September 30 with 4.5% discount; 3rd due December 31 with 3% discount; 4th due March 31 no discount. 1st and 2nd installments are 1/4 of previous year's taxes. Missing the first payment ends eligibility for the year.
  • Tax certificate sale held on or before June 1, conducted as an online auction at lienhub.com/county/walton, bidding downward from 18% in 1/4% increments; minimum 5% interest except zero bids. Certificate valid seven years; holder may apply for tax deed two years after April 1 delinquency date.

Walton County by the numbers

Where do Walton County owners deal with property taxes?

Walton County owners work with the tax collector, who bills and collects, and the property appraiser, who sets values and exemptions. The tax collector's office runs three branches: the DeFuniak Springs courthouse for north Walton, the Santa Rosa Beach courthouse annex for south Walton, and a Freeport office. The mailing address is a post office box in DeFuniak Springs.

The collector's site shows the branches open on weekdays into late afternoon, with a slightly later Wednesday start. Property tax questions about the estimated tax on a TRIM notice go to the property appraiser, while payment and delinquency questions go to the collector's office.

Because the county stretches from the Gulf coast to the inland towns, a seller may live a long way from the office that holds the file. Online payment and the parcel search save the trip.

What is the Walton County property tax calendar?

The tax collector publishes a month by month list, and it is more detailed than most Florida counties. Here are the entries that matter to a home seller.

Walton County Tax Collector calendar for real estate taxes
MonthEntry on the collector's page
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchExemptions due to the Property Appraiser by March 1; full amount due by March 31; fourth installment due March 31
AprilUnpaid real estate tax delinquent April 1 with a 3% charge; installment plan applications for next year due April 30
MayDelinquent real estate taxes advertised once a week for three weeks; certificate sale on or before June 1
June to SeptemberFirst installment due June 30, second due September 30
NovemberBills mailed; 4% discount through November 30
December3% discount; third installment due December 31

Source: Walton County Tax Collector, important tax dates. The page also notes the property appraiser mails the TRIM notice in August.

How does the Walton County installment plan work?

The plan splits the year into four payments, with a discount on the first three. The tax collector's installment page and calendar describe it this way.

  • Applications for the following year are due April 30.
  • The prior year's tax must exceed $100.00 and not be paid through escrow.
  • June 30 brings the first installment, carrying a 6% discount, September 30 the second at 4.5%, the third December 31 with 3%, and the fourth March 31 with no discount.
  • The first two payments are each one quarter of the previous year's taxes.
  • If the first payment is missed, the owner is out of the plan for the year. The calendar says the first installment must be received by July 31 or participation ends.

Enrolled taxpayers do not need to reapply each year. A seller on the plan should ask the collector for the balance left after each payment, since the later installments are adjusted after the roll is set.

What happens when Walton County taxes become delinquent?

On April 1 unpaid real estate tax is delinquent and a 3% charge is added to the gross amount. Tangible personal property tax is different: it picks up 1.5% interest per month.

The collector then runs the delinquent list in the DeFuniak Herald for three straight weeks, and the advertising and auction fee is added to the bill. The certificate sale follows, scheduled by June 1 as an online auction at lienhub.com/county/walton. Bidding starts at 18% and drops in quarter-percent steps, with a 5% minimum interest unless the bid is zero. A certificate is good for seven years.

Once the holder has waited two years from the April 1 delinquency date, an application for a tax deed is possible. The collector states that tax deed sales are set by the Clerk of Court and run online at walton.realforeclose.com, and that the owner may redeem until the clerk signs the tax deed. Delinquent taxes can be paid by cash, cashier's check, money order or card, with a convenience fee on card payments.

How do exemptions and the March 1 date affect a Walton County seller?

Exemptions follow the owner, so a sale ends the seller's homestead and the buyer must file their own. The tax collector's calendar sets the filing date at March 1 with the property appraiser, the same date the state taxpayer guide gives (link).

The state homestead exemption is up to $50,000, the first $25,000 for all taxes and an additional amount for non-school taxes on value above $50,000, according to the state homestead guide. Owners lose homestead if they rent the property or stop living there.

The tax collector also has a page on military property taxes. Servicemembers who rent a homestead out are covered by a separate state provision, so ask the collector if that applies.

Who pays the taxes when a Walton County home sells?

The contract decides, and closings in Florida normally prorate taxes to the day of closing. The title agent asks the collector for the current balance, including any certificate, and pays it from the seller's side of the statement.

The clerk collects deed stamps at filing, at 70 cents on each $100 of price, and every party to the document is liable whoever agrees to pay, per the stamp tax page. Clerk filing charges come from s. 28.24, which starts at $5.00 for a first page and adds $4.00 per further page, with extra per-page charges.

For a house with a tax certificate, the redemption has to be paid before or at closing. A buyer who sees a certificate issued more than two years ago should ask the Clerk of Court whether a tax deed application is pending.

How should a Walton County owner with unpaid taxes plan a sale?

Contact the tax collector first, because each month moves the cost. A sale before April avoids the 3% charge and the advertising fee, while one after the certificate sale carries interest and fees.

  • Search the parcel on the tax collector's payment portal for the current balance.
  • Ask whether a certificate exists and what rate it sold at.
  • Check homestead status with the property appraiser before March 1.
  • Tell the title company so the payoff is ordered ahead of the closing date.

How are Walton County tangible personal property taxes treated?

Tax on business equipment follows a harsher track than real estate. The tax collector's calendar says unpaid tangible personal property tax is delinquent April 1 and picks up 1.5% interest for each month.

Within 45 days after the March 31 deadline, those delinquent accounts are advertised in a local newspaper at the owner's cost. A list is published once in May, and warrant processing begins June 1. A landlord or small business owner selling a rental with equipment inside should ask the collector whether a personal property account sits under the same owner name.

  • Discounts match real estate: 4% in November, 3% in December, 2% in January, 1% in February.
  • Delinquent real estate carries a flat 3% charge, not monthly interest.
  • Different advertising rules apply to each, so ask which list a parcel is on.

What does a Walton County tax certificate holder have to wait for?

The holder cannot move fast. A certificate on a Walton County parcel is valid for seven years, and the holder may apply for a tax deed only two years after the April 1 delinquency date. Under state law the holder also may not contact the owner to demand payment during the first two years, per the statute on certificate sales.

For the seller, that window is time to arrange a sale. Many owners use it to list the house, find a buyer, and let the closing agent redeem the certificate from proceeds. Ask the collector for the redemption total on the planned closing date, because interest runs by the month.

More questions about Walton County, FL Property Tax Guide

When do Walton County property taxes become delinquent?

April 1. The Walton County Tax Collector says unpaid real estate tax is delinquent on that date and a 3% charge is added to the gross amount.

What is the Walton County installment plan discount?

6% on the first installment, 4.5% on the second, 3% on the third and none on the fourth. Applications are due April 30.

Where does Walton County hold its tax certificate sale?

Online, at lienhub.com/county/walton, on or before June 1. Bidding starts at 18% and goes down in quarter-percent steps.

Can I still keep my house after a Walton County tax certificate is sold?

Yes. The owner may redeem until the Clerk of Court signs the tax deed. A tax deed application cannot be filed until two years after the April 1 delinquency date.

When is the Walton County exemption deadline?

March 1. The tax collector's calendar says exemptions are due to the Property Appraiser's Office by that date.
