Putnam County by the numbers

Which Putnam County offices send the bill and value the house?

In Putnam County the appraiser sets the value and decides exemptions, while the Tax Collector bills, collects and distributes the money. Changes to name, address or assessed value on the roll go through the appraiser, not the collector.

The appraiser's main office is at 312 Oak Street in Palatka, with a mailing box at PO Box 1920, Palatka, FL 32178. Crescent City and Interlachen have satellite offices that open on set days: Crescent City on Mondays and Wednesdays, Interlachen on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The exemption department's number is (386) 329-0286. The Tax Collector keeps its property tax pages at putnamtax.com and runs tax certificate sales through an online bidding site.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, tangible personal property, roll corrections.
  • Tax Collector: bills, discounts, installments, delinquent taxes and certificates.
  • Clerk of the Court: tax deed sales and recorded deeds.

Which taxing authorities appear on a Putnam County bill?

A Putnam bill can carry lines from the county, a fire district, the school board, two water management districts and one of five municipalities. The Tax Collector's property tax page lists each one with a phone number so you can ask the right office about its rate.

That list names the county, the Fire MSTU District, the Putnam County School Board, the St. Johns River Water Management District, the Suwannee Water Management District, and the City of Palatka, City of Crescent City, Town of Interlachen, Town of Pomona Park and Town of Welaka. A parcel inside a city pays that city's levy in addition to the county's.

Non-ad valorem charges sit beside the tax lines. The county enacted a solid waste special assessment for residential units, split between landfill improvements, garbage collection and recycling. The commissioners have also authorized 28 separate MSBU projects for road maintenance or paving, which charge only the properties that benefit. The Hastings Drainage District levies its own assessment. A buyer or seller can see these on the bill, and homestead exemption does not reduce them.

What is the Putnam County payment schedule?

Value is fixed on January 1 and bills usually open for collection on November 1. The gross amount is due by March 31, and any unpaid real estate taxes go delinquent April 1.

Putnam County Tax Collector discount schedule for current real estate taxes
Payment monthDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchNone, gross amount due

The collector also offers a quarterly installment plan for owners whose estimated bill is more than $100. The application must reach the office by April 30 of the year you want to start. Payments fall due June 30 (6% discount), September 30 (4.5%), December 31 (3%) and March 31 (no discount). Missing the June payment removes the account from the plan, and under s. 197.222 the owner cannot rejoin until the next year with a new application. The first two payments use the prior year's taxes and the last two use the new roll.

What happens to an unpaid Putnam County bill?

Delinquent parcels are run in a local newspaper in three weekly ads in a row, then a tax certificate sale is held online by June 1. The certificate is a lien and does not convey ownership.

Bidding starts at 18% and drops in quarter percent steps until the lowest bidder takes the certificate. After the sale, the Tax Collector's FAQ says the owner could pay interest up to 18% a year, depending on the bid rate. After delinquency the office takes cashier's check, certified check, cash or money order, and the day it receives the payment sets the amount due.

  • In most cases, if taxes stay unpaid two years from April 1, the certificate holder can file a tax deed application.
  • Applications go through RealTDA, and the county posts a Lands Available for Taxes list for parcels that did not sell.
  • Paying the taxes cancels the lien, but all payments after delinquency must be in certified funds.

Anyone selling a house with a certificate on it needs a redemption quote from the collector, passed to the closing agent early, because interest accrues until the lien is cleared.

What homestead and senior exemptions does the Putnam County appraiser offer?

The county appraiser's exemption page says the homestead exemption removes the first $25,000 of value from every ad valorem levy, and that special assessments are untouched by it. The Palatka office takes applications year-round, and the satellite offices join in during the first two months of the year.

Every exemption has a March 1 deadline, counted from the year after you buy. After that date you must also complete an Extenuating Circumstances form. The applicant must hold title, be a Florida permanent resident and treat the home as a primary residence on the assessment date. Proof of residency includes a Florida driver license or ID showing the home address and a Florida vehicle registration. Trust-owned homes face stricter review.

  • Low income senior exemption: a county ordinance adds $25,000 against the county general millage for homeowners aged 65 and over who meet the income limit; the office tells applicants to ask for the current limit.
  • Super Senior exemption: for 25-year residents with a just value under $250,000, which exempts the whole assessed value where a taxing authority has enacted it. The page names Putnam County, Palatka, Crescent City, Interlachen, Pomona Park and Welaka.
  • Deployed service member, total and permanent disability and first responder exemptions, each with their own proof requirements.

Once approved, an exemption renews automatically, but the owner must report changes in use or status right away under ss. 196.131 and 196.161.

How does a sale change the next bill in Putnam County?

The buyer's next roll starts at just value, and any exemption you held stays behind. State rules treat a sale, foreclosure or transfer of title as a transfer of ownership, with exceptions for spouses and certain transfers at death.

A house held by one family for years can carry a bill that looks small next to what its new owner sees on the first full roll. The assessment cap, which the state's 2026 chart sets at 2.7%, applies only while the same owner keeps the homestead. If you are moving within Florida, the portability form can carry up to $500,000 of your accrued benefit to the new homestead, filed with the exemption application by March 1.

The deed also carries documentary stamps at $0.70 per $100 of price, paid through the Clerk at recording. Anyone named on the deed is liable, even when the contract assigns payment to one side.

What should a Putnam County seller check before listing?

Check three things before listing: the current bill is paid or will be settled at closing, no tax certificate exists, and the exemption record matches how the house is used. Homestead ends if the unit is rented or stops being the permanent home.

The Tax Collector and the appraiser are both in Palatka, and the roll is public. Print the parcel record and the bill, and hand both to the closing agent. Putnam parcels can carry MSBU road assessments and a solid waste charge, so ask whether any are unpaid, since they ride on the same bill as the taxes.

More questions about Putnam County, FL Property Tax Guide

How much can I save by paying a Putnam County bill early?

The discount starts at 4% for November, then steps down by a point each month through February. March carries none. Bills open for collection November 1.

What is the Putnam County delinquency date?

April 1. Anything unpaid after March 31 is delinquent the next day and heads for a certificate sale by June 1.

Does Putnam County offer a payment plan?

Yes. The quarterly plan needs an application in by April 30 and an estimated bill over $100, and its first three payments carry 6%, 4.5% and 3% discounts.

Where do I file for homestead in Putnam County?

File with the Property Appraiser in Palatka, or at the Crescent City or Interlachen satellite during the winter filing season. The cutoff is March 1 after you buy.

Can I lose my Putnam County house over unpaid taxes?

Eventually, yes. Once two years pass a certificate holder may seek a tax deed and the house can go to auction, though paying the full amount before the sale keeps it yours.

Due dates and discounts

  • Real estate taxes due November 1 and delinquent if not paid by April 1; reminder notices mailed by April 30; delinquent list advertised in May. Tax certificate face amount includes delinquent tax, interest at 1.5% per month for April and May, 5% Tax Collector commission, advertising charge and tax sale cost.
  • Tax certificate auction conducted online (levyfl.realtaxlien.com via West Florida Business Systems), normally on or before May 31; auction process must start on or before June 1. Bids 0 to 18% in 0.25% increments; minimum 5% interest if redeemed on or after June 1 (not for zero bids). Unbid certificates issued to the county at 18%. Certificate life 7 years.
  • Tax deed application available after two years from April 1 of issuance year; applicant pays $150 title search fee and $75 application fee (fees can change). Clerk of Circuit Court sets sale date; public sale to highest bidder. Homestead property opening bid includes half of assessed value.

What we could not confirm

Levy County by the numbers

Where do Levy County owners pay and question property tax?

Levy owners pay at the Tax Collector's Bronson headquarters, 310 School Street, Suite 102 (352-486-5172), or at one of two branches. Valuation sits with a different office, the Property Appraiser, on the same street in Bronson at (352) 486-5222.

  • Bronson main office: 310 School Street, Suite 102, Bronson, FL 32621, Monday to Friday, opening 8:30 and closing 4:30
  • Williston branch: 551 SW 1st Avenue, Williston, FL 32696, (352) 528-6091.
  • Chiefland branch: 226 North Main Street, Chiefland, FL 32626, (352) 493-4646.

Address changes cannot be made at the collector's counter, for real property or tangible accounts alike; they go through the appraiser. A seller should update the mailing address there so a stray bill finds the right person after closing.

What are the Levy County property tax dates?

Bills fall due on November 1, and a balance still open after the following March 31 is delinquent from April 1. The state discount shrinks from 4 percent in November by one point per month to 1 percent in February.

Reminder letters on unpaid accounts go out by April 30. A delinquent list is prepared in May for the newspaper and the web, and the certificate auction usually runs by May 31, with Chapter 197 requiring a start no later than June 1.

Upstream of the bill, the state calendar is just as fixed: value as of January 1, exemption filings by March 1, a proposed-tax notice in August, and 25 days from that notice to petition on value.

How can you pay Levy County property tax online, and what does it cost?

Cards cost extra online and e-check does not. The collector's site lists 2.3 percent on credit cards, a flat $1.75 for charges below $76, and nothing for an online e-check (ACH); processor fees do not reach the county.

At the counter, every payment draws 2.3 percent and e-checks are unavailable. Anything processed after 11:59 p.m. counts as the next calendar day, a trap near a deadline. A seller wanting a clean payoff can use an online e-check before midnight to dodge both the fee and the next-day rule.

Cards accepted are Visa, Master Card, American Express and Discover. Call 352-486-5172 on a weekday if the system gives trouble.

What happens when Levy County property tax goes unpaid?

Delinquent tax is sold off as a certificate, a lien instead of a transfer of the house. Its face amount stacks the unpaid tax, 1.5 percent a month for April and May, a 5 percent collector commission, the advertising charge and the cost of the sale.

Levy County tax certificate terms, from the Tax Collector's tax sale page
ItemAs the office prints it
Sale methodOnline auction through West Florida Business Systems, on or before May 31
Bid range0 to 18 percent in 0.25 percent steps, lowest rate wins
Minimum interest if redeemed on or after June 15 percent (not for zero bids)
Unbid certificatesIssued to the county at 18 percent
Certificate life7 years
Holder may seek a tax deedAfter two years from April 1 of the issuance year

The delinquent list runs weekly for three weeks ahead of the auction. Certificate buyers must wait two years, counting from April 1 of the issuance year, before contacting the owner.

What does a Levy County tax deed application involve?

An applicant must complete these steps, and the office says the fee amounts can change without notice:

  • File a signed tax deed application.
  • Redeem any other outstanding certificates and pay current tax if owed.
  • Pay a $150 title search fee and a $75 application fee.

The county clerk then schedules the sale and charges advertising, mailing and sheriff costs.

Where homestead is on the current roll, the opening bid adds half the assessed value to taxes and costs. A parcel nobody bids on can join the list of lands available for taxes, and land left unsold there for 3 years reverts to Levy County. Unpaid government liens survive a tax deed under s. 197.552.

Timing is the practical point for an owner planning to sell. Get a payoff figure from the collector for any certificate before listing, since a title company will want each lien cleared at closing.

What should Levy County sellers know about agricultural classification?

Farm classification stays with the seller, not the land. The appraiser's page calls it non-transferable, so a buyer files a fresh application after any sale or transfer.

Filing runs January 1 through March 1. Per the statute the office cites, only land used mainly for bona fide agriculture, meaning good-faith commercial use, qualifies. Zoning alone earns nothing, and the use should exist on the January 1 assessment date, or a reasonable effort to start it must have been made.

Selling acreage? Tell the buyer which parcels carry the classification now, because a buyer who fails to qualify may face a higher assessment. Denials are mailed to the applicant, who can ask the appraiser to talk it through.

How does the Levy County tax certificate auction treat bidders?

The sale runs online through West Florida Business Systems, and the Tax Collector says no deposits are required for the current format. Every bidder must submit a Participating Bidder Agreement after registering or logging in, plus an electronic W-9 each year.

The office also runs a test system so new bidders can practice, and bids made there do not carry over to the live sale. A certificate can be sold to another buyer if the endorsement form and a transfer fee of $2.25 per certificate reach the Tax Collector. The office warns that a certificate is not a guaranteed investment, and if no action is taken within the seven-year life while the tax stays unpaid, the certificate is cancelled. For an owner, this means the lien is held by a private investor who is barred from contacting you for the first two years but who may then apply for a deed.

Who lives in Levy County, and what do homes cost?

Levy County is rural: about 48,520 people live across 1,118 square miles, roughly 38 per square mile in the 2020 count, and the population has risen 13.1 percent since then.

Census data for 2020 to 2024 give an owner-occupied home a median value of $190,600, with 81.4 percent of 22,192 housing units lived in by owners, rent at $850 and household income at $56,750. Households number 18,562 at 2.43 people each, the median selected monthly owner cost with a mortgage is $1,297 and without one is $375, and only 16.5 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree. Broadband subscriptions reach 80.8 percent of households, workers average a 30.4 minute commute, and builders pulled 244 permits in 2025. People 65 and over are 26.7 percent of the county, and 91.1 percent of residents stayed put in the previous year. Long tenure usually means a Save Our Homes assessment below market, which resets after a sale.

A Levy County deed carries Florida's 70 cents per $100 stamp tax, paid to the clerk at recording by whichever party the deal assigns, with every party liable.

More questions about Levy County, FL Property Tax Guide

Where is the Levy County Tax Collector?

Headquarters: 310 School Street, Suite 102, Bronson. Branches: 551 SW 1st Avenue, Williston, and 226 North Main Street, Chiefland. All keep weekday hours.

Is there a fee to pay Levy County property tax online?

Cards add 2.3 percent, or $1.75 flat under $76, payable to the processor. Online e-checks cost nothing; office payments add 2.3 percent.

When does Levy County property tax become delinquent?

From April 1 following the bill. Reminders mail by April 30 and the certificate auction normally closes out by May 31.

Can a buyer keep my Levy County agricultural classification?

No, the appraiser calls it non-transferable. A buyer needs a new application by March 1 and must pass the bona fide agriculture test.

How soon can a tax deed be sought on unpaid Levy County tax?

Two years after the April 1 of the issuance year, a certificate holder may apply. If one exists on your parcel, request a payoff figure from the collector.

Flagler County by the numbers

Which offices run property tax in Flagler?

In Flagler the Property Appraiser sets value. The Tax Collector sends notices and takes payment. Millage is set by the levying bodies: county commissioners, the school board, city commissions and others.

The Tax Collector's website, flaglertax.gov, has pages for property taxes, tangible personal property tax, tourist development tax, business tax receipts and veteran benefits. For questions about a value, an exemption or a classification, contact the Flagler County Property Appraiser directly and ask for the current forms and filing dates. Deeds are recorded, and foreclosure and tax deed auctions are run, by the circuit court clerk.

How are Flagler County property taxes billed?

Flagler bills after the year ends, and notices land around the start of November. The Tax Collector explains that the tax year runs January 1 to December 31 and payment begins November 1 of that year, and its homepage notes that real estate and tangible personal property bills are mailed October 31.

The process runs in a set order:

  • The Property Appraiser establishes values and applies exemptions to complete the tax roll.
  • The certified roll goes to the Tax Collector.
  • The Tax Collector merges in non-ad valorem assessments, which are set amounts that do not depend on value and appear on the same notice.
  • The notice is mailed to the owner's last address on the roll.

If a mortgage servicer pays from escrow, the servicer can request the bill under criteria set by the Tax Collector, and the owner gets a copy for information.

What else does the Flagler Tax Collector handle for property owners?

Beyond the real estate bill, the office runs several accounts that matter to landlords and sellers who own rental or business property. Its website lists these as separate service pages.

  • Tangible personal property tax, which applies to furnishings and equipment used in a rental or business.
  • Tourist development tax, owed on short stays in a rental.
  • Business tax receipts for operating a business in the county.
  • Veteran benefits information.
  • Online payments for tax bills.

An owner closing out a rental should ask the office to confirm that each of these accounts is current and closed, because a balance on one can surface long after the deed records. The same counter also handles driver license and vehicle registration work. Plates on passenger cars and similar vehicles expire at midnight on the owner's birthday, which is a useful reminder when you update your address after a move.

If you cannot visit in person, use the online payment page rather than a link from a text or email. The office has warned that fraudulent texts are circulating in the state agency's name.

What if a Flagler tax bill never arrives?

Nonreceipt is no defense. The Tax Collector cites section 197.122, which tells owners to learn the amount due and pay before delinquency, mailed bill or not.

This catches sellers who moved out, landlords whose tenants get the mail and heirs at a house with an outdated address. The Tax Collector's lobbies may close at 4 p.m. when crowded, and the office warns about text messages that falsely claim to come from the state motor vehicle agency, so check the account yourself on the official site.

What dates drive the Flagler tax year?

Florida's statewide calendar runs here, and Flagler's offices carry out each step.

Calendar steps from the Florida Department of Revenue taxpayer page
DateStep
January 1Assessment date
March 1Exemption filings due
April 1Tangible personal property returns
AugustProposed-tax notice mailed
25 days after the noticeValue petition window
September and OctoberMillage hearings
NovemberBills and early-payment discount
April 1 followingDelinquent

The early-payment discount falls month by month, from 4 percent for a November payment down to 1 percent in February.

Can Flagler owners pay in installments or defer?

Both options exist, and the Tax Collector takes the requests. Installment requests are due on May 1 during the assessment year, and a deferral request on Form DR-570 is due March 31 after it.

Deferral lets a homestead owner postpone the part of the bill that exceeds a share of household income. The share is 5 percent for most owners and 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older. Partial payments before delinquency are accepted only if the Tax Collector chooses to take them. Ask how Flagler handles an installment plan before you plan around it, since the May deadline falls well before bills are mailed.

Does my Flagler assessment cap follow the house to a buyer?

The new owner starts at full just value. The seller's capped assessment does not transfer, because a change of title resets the parcel the next January, with exceptions such as spousal transfers.

While a homestead is held, the yearly assessed increase stops at the lower of 3 percent or inflation. DOR's chart prints 2.7 percent for 2026. Sellers moving inside Florida can port part of that benefit to a new home if they claim it within three years. Both forms reach the Property Appraiser by that same March 1 deadline.

Which veteran breaks can Flagler County owners ask about?

The Tax Collector's site has a veteran benefits page, and the Property Appraiser handles the exemptions themselves. Florida's list is short.

  • A $5,000 cut in assessed value for a disabled ex-servicemember rated 10 percent or more.
  • A homestead discount tied to the VA rating for a veteran 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability.
  • A deployment-based exemption on Form DR-501M.

Ask the Property Appraiser what proof each one needs, and bring discharge or VA rating papers to that conversation.

What if a Flagler County parcel reaches a tax deed auction?

After a certificate has aged two years, its holder may ask for a deed, and the clerk then auctions the parcel publicly. The tax collector assembles the notice list: titleholder, mortgagees, lienholders, the assessed party and any recorded contract buyer.

  • The top bidder leaves a nonrefundable deposit, set at the larger of 5 percent of the bid or $200.
  • The balance, stamps and recording costs are due inside 24 hours, excluding weekends and holidays.
  • An unsold parcel joins the county's lands-available list.

An owner who sells ahead of the auction can redeem from proceeds. Ask the Flagler Tax Collector for a redemption figure, since interest makes it move.

What happens to a Flagler tax bill at closing?

Closing agents confirm the account and pay what is owed from the seller's proceeds. Get the parcel balance from the Tax Collector's office. The clerk collects deed stamps at recording, at a statewide rate of 70 cents on each $100 of price.

A parcel with a certificate attached can still be sold. Settle the certificate at the table so the buyer gets a clean title.

More questions about Flagler County, FL Property Tax Guide

When does Flagler County mail property tax bills?

Around the start of November. The Tax Collector's site says real estate and tangible personal property bills are mailed October 31, and payment begins November 1.

What if I never receive my Flagler County tax bill?

You still owe the tax. Section 197.122 puts the duty on the owner to find out the amount and pay before the delinquency date, so contact the Tax Collector and the Property Appraiser.

Can I defer Flagler County property tax?

A homestead owner can apply on Form DR-570 by March 31 after the assessment year. Deferral covers tax above 5 percent of household income, or 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older.

Does my homestead cap transfer to the buyer of my Flagler County house?

No. A sale resets the property to just value the next January 1. You may be able to port part of your cap to a new Florida homestead.

Who sets Flagler County millage rates?

The levying bodies do: county commissioners, the school board, city commissions and other authorities. The Property Appraiser sets value, not the rate.

Highlands County by the numbers

What makes Highlands County property tax different?

Highlands County is a large, mostly rural county, and that shapes how its tax roll works. The property appraiser says the county covers about 1,029 square miles of land, roughly 658,000 acres, with around 113,000 parcels, 60,000 buildings, 6,000 business accounts and 10,000 tangible personal property accounts on mobile homes.

Farmland is a big piece of that roll: about 75,000 acres of citrus, 275,000 acres of pasture and thousands of acres of cropland. The office also administers over 24,000 homestead exemptions. The tax collector serves the county from locations in Sebring and Avon Park, and the Highlands County Tax Collector posts the payment and deadline pages used below.

When is Highlands County property tax due?

Bills are mailed by October 31, collection begins in November, and the full amount is due by March 31. Anything unpaid or not postmarked by March 31 is delinquent on April 1, when interest and fees begin.

The appraiser's FAQ lists the early payment discounts as a four, three, two and one percent sequence running November through February. It adds that Highlands taxes are paid in arrears for the calendar year, January through December, which matters at a closing because the seller owes part of a year that the buyer will be billed for.

  • Installment plan: apply by April 30 for the next tax year; payments fall in June (6% discount), September (4.5%), December (3%) and March (final, no discount).
  • Missed first payment: an account without the first installment by July 31 is removed from the plan and gets a full bill in October.
  • Homestead deferral: the county tax collector lists January 31 as its filing deadline for the deferral program.

What dates should a Highlands County owner mark?

The county's calendar runs from the January 1 valuation through the April 1 delinquency, with a handful of deadlines that catch sellers off guard.

Highlands County property tax calendar from the tax collector and appraiser pages
MonthEventSource
January 31Homestead tax deferral filing deadlineTax Collector
March 1New homestead exemptions and agricultural classification applicationsAppraiser
April 1Unpaid taxes delinquentTax Collector

On or before June 1Tax certificate saleTax Collector
AugustTRIM notices mailedTax Collector
October 31Bills mailedTax Collector

In May, delinquent real estate accounts are advertised three times in a local newspaper, and delinquent tangible personal property accounts once.

How do homestead and agricultural classification work in Highlands County?

New homestead exemptions must be filed with the Highlands County Property Appraiser by March 1. The appraiser says the exemption is free to anyone who qualifies, and that it can be handled in minutes at the office or at visits to municipal sites around the county.

The office warns that new owners sometimes receive mailings offering a reduction in taxable value for a fee. It says such offers amount to the savings the homestead exemption already gives, and that the paid service is generally just information on how to apply.

Agricultural land follows a different rule. An application must be filed with the appraiser before March 1 of the tax year, and only land used in good faith for commercial agriculture qualifies. Once granted, the classification renews each year. A dwelling on the parcel does not disqualify the land, though the home site is assessed at just value. Citrus is valued by variety, and the office adjusts assessments when disease or freeze damage affects production, and it avoids entering groves because of disease concerns.

How can a Highlands County owner challenge a value or exemption?

Petition the Value Adjustment Board before the deadline printed on the TRIM notice, with a notarized petition and a $50 filing fee per parcel. The board has three county commissioners and two school board members, and it usually appoints special masters who are independent of the appraiser's office to hear cases.

  • For a value dispute, bring sales of comparable properties from the prior year, before January 1, or an appraisal.
  • For an exemption denial, show you qualified as of January 1.
  • The board cannot reduce a bill for hardship or because the value rose from last year.
  • A losing petitioner may sue in circuit court under section 194.171.

The board's clerk mails a record of decision within 20 days of the ruling. The appraiser notes that millage is set by the county, cities, school board and water management districts, so neither the board nor the appraiser can change a rate. A household that cannot meet an increase may qualify for a deferral or the installment plan through the tax collector.

What happens if Highlands County property tax goes unpaid?

An unpaid Highlands County account goes to a tax certificate sale by June 1, once the newspaper notices have run. A tax deed application can be filed by the certificate holder once two years have passed since delinquency, and no later than seven years after the certificate was first issued.

Interest to the applicant runs 1.5 percent monthly, per the tax collector, from the month after the application until the account is redeemed or sold, and that the applicant is not guaranteed the property. The Highlands County Clerk of Courts schedules and runs the sale. Under state rules, a homestead parcel owing under $250 has its certificate issued to the county and not auctioned, and a homestead opening bid at a deed sale includes half of the last assessed value.

A seller facing a certificate can still close. Payoff from proceeds redeems the lien before a deed application is filed.

How should you handle Highlands County property tax when selling?

Order a payoff figure before listing, and decide whether the bill has been issued for the year. Bills go to the owner of record, and a recorded deed is what puts the new owner on the appraiser's roll.

The appraiser's database does not hold items such as special assessments for solid waste collection or fire and road improvement districts, though they appear on the tax bill. The complete bill, non-ad valorem charges included, comes from the tax collector rather than the property record. For a split lot or merged parcels, the appraiser says a survey is needed to split, all taxes on the parcels must be paid, and a mortgage holder must approve in writing.

The state's documentary stamp tax on a deed is a rate of 70 cents for each $100 paid, and a change of ownership returns the capped assessment to just value on the next January 1. For a current millage figure, check the TRIM notice or ask the appraiser.

More questions about Highlands County, FL Property Tax Guide

When is Highlands County property tax due?

The whole bill is owed by March 31, and April 1 marks delinquency. Bills are mailed October 31, and the discount starts at 4 percent in November, slipping a point a month to 1 percent in February.

How do I join the Highlands County installment plan?

Applications go to the tax collector by April 30 for the coming tax year. Payments are due in June, September, December and March, with discounts of 6%, 4.5% and 3% on the first three, and nothing on the last.

What is the filing deadline for a Highlands County homestead exemption?

March 1, filed with the Highlands County Property Appraiser. The exemption is free to qualified owners, and the office advises ignoring paid mailers that offer to reduce taxable value for a fee.

Can I petition the Value Adjustment Board in Highlands County?

Yes, before the deadline on your TRIM notice. The petition is notarized and costs $50 per parcel, and hardship or a rise in value from last year does not alone support a reduction.

Who runs the Highlands County tax deed sale?

The Clerk of Courts schedules and conducts the sale. A certificate holder applies through the tax collector's vendor after two years from the date of delinquency, and the holder is not guaranteed to obtain the property.

Columbia County by the numbers

Who does what on a Columbia County, FL tax bill?

Values and exemptions come from the appraiser. Local taxing bodies adopt budgets and millage, and the tax collector, based in Lake City, mails bills and takes payment.

The tax collector's main line is 386-758-1077 and the Tax Department answers at 386-758-1080. For value or exemption questions, dial the appraiser at (386) 758-1083. The Clerk of Court, at 386-719-7580 for tax deed questions, runs the deed sales that follow long delinquency.

What deadline governs a Columbia County tax bill?

The regular annual bill is due by March 31, and unpaid taxes generally become delinquent April 1. The bill arrives in November, and the early-payment discount starts at 4% that month and falls one point each month through February.

A TRIM notice in August is a proposal, not the payment bill. The tax collector says a proposed-tax notice differs from the annual bill, so check it for values, exemptions and hearing dates. Qualifying payments get next-working-day treatment under Florida law when the due date lands on a weekend or holiday, though a close call deserves a phone call.

How can I pay a Columbia County tax bill?

Payment is possible online, by phone, at the counter, through the mail, or at the Lake City drive-through and drop box. The office lists a 2.5% card fee with a $2 minimum and a $1.50 e-check fee for online or phone payments, and says it receives no part of the card fee.

  • Search by owner name, address or account number in the property tax portal.
  • Mortgage escrow customers should confirm the lender paid the right year, to avoid a duplicate payment.
  • E-billing is available, registered one property account at a time.
  • A duplicate notice can go to a second recipient, but the owner remains responsible.

How does the Columbia County calendar run from month to month?

The tax collector publishes a year-at-a-glance calendar, and its main points are easy to plan around. Columbia County sellers and buyers can use it to see which weeks are likely to bring a bill, a discount change or interest on a late balance, and which dates matter most before a closing.

  • April 1: unpaid taxes generally become delinquent, and tangible personal property returns are due to the appraiser.
  • April 30: installment applications are due.
  • May: delinquent-tax advertising and certificate sale preparation begin.
  • June 30 and September 30: the first two installments fall due.
  • November: annual collection starts at the 4% discount.

The office stresses that the calendar is a planning guide, and that late-mailed bills, weekends and holidays can move a deadline. Follow the dates on your own notice and call about late-mailed bills.

How do the quarterly installments work in Columbia County?

The installment plan lets an owner prepay the current year in four payments if estimated tax is over $100 per notice. Submit Form DR-534 to the tax collector by April 30. The first payment confirms participation.

The first two installments use prior-year tax as the estimate, and later ones adjust to actual tax. A late first installment is accepted through July 31 without the June discount. The plan does not cover delinquent taxes.

Can I make partial payments on Columbia County property tax?

Yes, on current taxes from November 1 through March 31, by signing a partial-payment agreement with the office. No early-payment discounts apply to partial payments, and the full balance must be paid by March 31.

Tracking is the owner's job, and the published local plan mails no balance reminder before April 1. Any unpaid balance becomes delinquent with interest and costs, and partial payments do not stop a certificate sale if real estate tax remains unpaid. State law leaves partial payments to the tax collector's discretion before delinquency.

What homestead and tax relief programs apply in Columbia County?

The Property Appraiser decides homestead, disability, widow or widower, veteran, senior and agricultural benefits. March 1 is the usual filing deadline. The homestead exemption reaches $50,000, and its first $25,000 also lowers school tax.

Save Our Homes ties a homestead's yearly assessment growth to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is lower, and the next January 1 after a sale brings the parcel back to just value. A disabled ex-servicemember may take a $5,000 cut in assessed value. Veterans aged 65 or over with a lasting service-connected disability may receive a discount matching the VA disability rating. A deferral request for homestead tax is filed with the collector by March 31 after the assessment year.

The tax collector's page also mentions income-based help and certain vacancy reductions for service assessments. Call to confirm which one fits.

How is unpaid Columbia County tax handled at a house closing?

Closing agents usually pay the current year out of the seller's proceeds, and the collector can confirm what posted. Ask for an exact payoff for your closing date, since interest and costs change the amount.

A tax certificate is a lien and does not transfer ownership. Section 197.502 lets a certificate holder seek a tax deed once two years have passed since April 1 of the issue year, and the clerk's office holds the sale. Redemption is available until a tax deed is issued, unless the buyer has paid the clerk in full, so call the Tax Department at 386-758-1080 with your parcel number before any sale date. The office accepts cash, money order, cashier's check or card for certificate redemption and cautions against assuming a personal check works.

What else can appear on a Columbia County tax bill?

Besides value-based tax, the bill can carry non-ad valorem assessments for services such as fire, solid waste, paving or lighting, according to the parcel's location. The county, city or district that creates an assessment sets it, and the tax collector only bills what the tax roll certifies.

Business equipment is a different account. Business equipment returns generally reach the appraiser by April 1, and unpaid accounts can lead to tax warrants rather than a certificate sale. Anyone selling a house that hosted a business should ask both offices whether an equipment account is open under the same name.

Mailing address changes are another trap. The tax roll address comes from the Property Appraiser, so a new owner who wants the November bill sent elsewhere should ask that office to update the record. The collector also takes a forwarding request.

What if my Columbia County value looks wrong?

Contact the Property Appraiser first, then use the Value Adjustment Board if needed. A value petition reaches the clerk within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, and an exemption denial can be appealed in the 30 days after a denial letter goes out.

Payment questions and value disputes go to separate offices, and a petition does not replace paying the bill the tax collector sends in November.

More questions about Columbia County, FL Property Tax Guide

The ordinary annual bill must be paid by March 31, and April 1 usually starts delinquency. Discounts run from 4% in November to 1% in February.

How do I join the Columbia County installment plan?

File Form DR-534 with the collector by April 30. Estimated tax must top $100 per notice. Your first payment confirms participation.

What card fee does the Columbia County tax collector charge?

The office lists a 2.5% card fee with a $2 minimum, plus a $1.50 e-check fee, for online or phone payments.

Which number covers a Columbia County homestead exemption?

Call the Property Appraiser at (386) 758-1083. March 1 is the usual filing deadline.

The Clerk of Court conducts them and issues deeds to winning bidders. Tax deed questions go to 386-719-7580.

What does the Jackson County calendar say about delinquent accounts?

Real property tax left unpaid on April 1 picks up a 3% penalty. The calendar says the delinquent list goes into a local newspaper inside 45 days, at the owner's expense, then repeats weekly for three weeks in May before the certificate sale. Since the sale date is chosen in March, a seller can learn it before delinquency even begins.

An investor who buys a certificate holds a lien, not the house. After two years pass without redemption, the investor may apply for a deed and the clerk holds an auction. For a homestead parcel, statute 197.502 puts half of the latest assessed value into the opening bid, on top of what is owed.

Can Jackson County owners spread payments over the year?

  • First payment: due on or before June 1, with cancellation if nothing arrives by June 30.
  • Second payment: before September 30.

  • Final payment: by March 31.

The first item gives two different dates, so call the office and confirm which applies to your account. If you sell while on the plan, give the closing agent a list of paid installments so the proration is right.

Which homestead and assessment limits matter to a Jackson County seller?

Homestead in Jackson County works as it does statewide: live in the house on January 1, file DR-501 by March 1, and up to $50,000 comes off assessed value. Only the first $25,000 lowers school tax.

Growth in a homestead's assessed value is held to the lesser of 3 percent or inflation, and the state's chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026. Non-homestead parcels face a 10 percent cap. Selling ends both, so a buyer's first bill often exceeds the seller's last.

  • Seniors: a county or city ordinance may add an exemption for owners 65 or older within an income limit.
  • Veterans: a service-connected disability of 10 percent or more can bring a $5,000 reduction in assessed value.
  • Leasing the house or leaving it removes homestead status.

Ask the Property Appraiser whether a local ordinance applies to your address.

What is the route for contesting a Jackson County value?

TRIM notices are mailed in August, and a Value Adjustment Board petition must follow within 25 days. For a denied exemption, 30 days run from the denial letter.

Talk to the appraiser's staff first. A wrong square footage figure or exemption status may be fixed without a hearing, and a deed, survey or builder's records help if the record itself is wrong.

Does the November 2026 property tax amendment affect a Jackson County bill?

The county announced a town hall on October 13, 2026 about Amendment 3, a property tax proposal on the November 2026 ballot. The notice said the discussion would cover the possible effect on local funding for public safety, fire and emergency services and special districts. It describes the amendment as proposed, so no figures appear.

The October 13 meeting started at 6:00 p.m. Central Time at the Endeavor Convention Center, was free to attend, and invited local governments, law enforcement, fire and emergency medical services and special taxing districts to take part. That guest list shows who relies on property tax revenue in the county, and who may adjust budgets if the rules change.

What changes depends on the ballot result and any law that follows. Check the Florida Department of Revenue and county budget pages for the effective year before relying on a number in a sale. Until new rules are posted, use the dates and amounts on your own bill.

Do mobile homes and business equipment follow the same dates in Jackson County?

Partly. The collector's calendar treats tangible personal property, such as business furniture and equipment, on the same discount schedule as real estate, but with the harsher 1.5% monthly interest charge once it turns delinquent.

Mobile homes have their own line. A mobile home that is not assessed as real property needs its decal renewed by December 31, and the calendar puts registration of mobile homes, trucks over 8,000 pounds and truck-trailers in the same December window. If you own a mobile home on land you are selling, ask the tax collector whether it is billed as real property or carries a decal, since that decides which deadline you face.

Both points are worth raising with the closing agent early. Tell them whether the property includes a mobile home or business equipment, so that every account tied to it is identified and paid before the settlement date.

What should a Jackson County seller line up before closing?

Get the payoff in writing, with the tax year it covers. The title agent then divides the current year between buyer and seller at the closing table.

  • Use the portal's tax-year search to check whether earlier years remain open.
  • If April 1 has passed, ask about the penalty and advertising costs.
  • Look for recorded liens in the Clerk's records.
  • Hand the closing agent your installment history.

A seller racing a delinquency or certificate sale date can set a quick cash closing, with the tax paid out of proceeds by the title agent.

More questions about Jackson County, FL Property Tax Guide

What is the final day to pay Jackson County property tax without a penalty?

March 31 is the cutoff for the gross amount. Paying early earns 4% in November, then 3%, 2% and 1% in the following three months.

What penalty hits an unpaid Jackson County bill on April 1?

Real property takes a 3% penalty. Business equipment is charged 1.5% interest a month instead.

When does Jackson County hold its tax certificate sale?

The collector fixes the date in March, ahead of the April 1 delinquency date. The collector's announcements give the exact day.

Does Jackson County allow installment payments?

Yes. File by April 30 for next year's plan and pay in June, September, December and March. Ask the office for the exact June date.

Will selling raise the next owner's Jackson County bill?

Usually, yes. The Save Our Homes cap and the 10 percent limit both end at a sale, and the next January 1 resets the property to just value.

Hendry County by the numbers

Where is Hendry County and who bills its property tax?

Hendry County's own website highlights Lake Okeechobee and the Caloosahatchee River, and its historic courthouse is in LaBelle. The tax collector's main office is at 25 E. Hickpochee in LaBelle.

Billing and collection sit with the tax collector, while value and exemptions sit with the property appraiser. The county, school board and cities act as levying authorities and choose the rates. The collector's office offers to help you find whom to call at each.

  • Tax collector: 863-675-5280, mail to P.O. Box 1780, LaBelle, FL 33975-1780. Payments do not require an appointment.
  • Property appraiser: 863-675-5270, the contact for homestead filings, assessed value questions, mailing address changes and parcel description errors.
  • Clerk of court: records the deed at closing and handles tax deed sales.

How does Hendry County define what gets taxed?

The tax collector's page separates three kinds of charge. Real estate tax falls on land, buildings and improvements, scales with the appraiser's value, and attaches to a parcel number. Tangible personal property tax applies to furniture and equipment in businesses and rental properties.

The third is non-ad valorem assessments, set amounts that the taxing authorities collect for things like storm water, street lighting, fire and rescue, and solid waste. They do not depend on what your house is worth. Landlords: furnishings and equipment left in a rental can create a separate personal property bill. Ask the property appraiser whether a rental you are selling has such an account. Read every section of a Hendry bill before listing, since a title company will want the flat assessments settled too.

When are Hendry County property taxes due?

Hendry's tax year is the calendar year, and the bill shows up in November. The collector reminds owners that paying is their duty even if no notice arrives, and asks them to call if November passes with no bill.

Taxes become delinquent on April 1. Real estate then carries 3 percent minimum interest plus ad costs, with a certificate sale to follow by June 1. Unpaid tangible personal property carries 18 percent interest annually, and warrants are expected on or about June 1. Delinquent payments must be in certified U.S. funds drawn on a U.S. bank, and the amount due depends on the date payment is received.

Earlier in the year, state deadlines apply: March 1 for exemptions, April 1 for business property returns, a TRIM notice in August, and 25 days after that notice to petition the value adjustment board, all listed by the Department of Revenue.

How does Hendry County treat late business and rental equipment tax?

Equipment tax runs on a harsher clock than the house. The tax collector says unpaid tangible personal property takes 18 percent interest a year plus advertising and fees, and warrants are expected on or about June 1. The office describes this tax as covering furniture and equipment in businesses and rental properties.

A landlord selling a rental should call the property appraiser at 863-675-5270 and ask whether the address has an equipment account. Any balance there should be settled before closing, since it is a separate bill from the real estate tax and the buyer's title company can find it.

Whatever the tax type, delinquent payments must come in certified U.S. funds drawn on a U.S. bank. The tax collector adds that the total depends on the day payment is received, so a quote given weeks before closing may be stale. Ask for a fresh figure in the last days before you sign, and ask the closing agent to confirm the amount that was wired.

How does the Hendry County installment plan work?

Hendry's collector offers quarterly prepayment under s. 197.222 to accounts above $100 in tax. Sign-up opens each November 1 and closes April 30 of the year you want to join.

Hendry County quarterly plan, four payments
InstallmentAmount basisDueDiscount
1stOne quarter of prior year's taxesJune 306%
2ndOne quarter of prior year's taxesSeptember 304.5%
3rdCurrent liability less 1st and 2nd, divided by 2December 313%
4thRemaining current liabilityMarch 31None

The first installment must be in by July 31 or the account drops out and the full tax is due by March 31, though the 6 percent discount ends after June 30. The first notice is mailed by June 1. If June 15 passes without one, call the office. Enrolled owners are re-enrolled automatically in later years. The office says the plan usually gives a discount close to the 4 percent November rate, though the match can shift with exemptions and values. Any change in ownership, value or exemption shows up in the last two bills, so a house sold mid-year needs a payoff check before closing. Source: the tax collector's installment page.

What other payment help does Hendry County give?

The tax collector's office tells owners to contact it about partial payments, installment payments and homestead tax deferral plans. The office posts a partial payment plan agreement on its website, and the state page says the collector decides whether to accept partial payments before delinquency under s. 197.374.

  • Homestead deferral uses Form DR-570, filed by March 31 following the assessment year.
  • It postpones the share of tax above 5 percent of household income, or 3 percent for permanent residents 65 and up.
  • Several checks for one bill must travel in one envelope, and the bill is payable in a lump unless an installment or partial plan applies.

Anyone may pay the bill. A buyer, relative or closing agent can pay on your behalf. The collector's portal takes online payments. Put your account and phone numbers on a mailed check's memo line, and make sure the words and numerals agree.

What changes for a Hendry County seller with homestead?

An owner who claimed homestead enjoyed a cap on assessed value growth, and that cushion does not travel to the buyer. The state's cap chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 for 2025 and 3.0 for 2024, and the next owner starts at just value on January 1 after the sale. If you plan to buy again in Florida, ask the appraiser there about portability, which moves part of the saved amount to a new homestead set up within three years.

The exemption itself is filed with the Hendry County Property Appraiser by March 1. The property appraiser's number is 863-675-5270.

What should a Hendry County seller do about unpaid tax?

Ask the tax collector for a payoff, then pass it to the closing agent. The flat assessments, the tax and any April 1 charges come out of proceeds, using the figure quoted for the day payment arrives.

If a certificate was sold on your parcel, redemption has to be in certified funds, and the holder must wait before seeking a deed. A financed buyer might take longer than a cash buyer, which counts when time is short.

More questions about Hendry County, FL Property Tax Guide

Who do I call about Hendry County property taxes?

Bills and payments go to 863-675-5280 (tax collector). Value and exemption questions go to 863-675-5270 (property appraiser).

What is the installment deadline in Hendry County?

Sign-up ends April 30, and the 6 percent discount needs the first payment by June 30. Payment after June 30 and before July 31 receives no discount.

When do Hendry County taxes go delinquent?

April 1. Real estate then adds a 3 percent minimum interest charge and advertising costs, and a certificate sale follows by June 1.

What if I do not get a tax bill in November?

The tax is still yours to pay. The collector suggests calling 863-675-5280 or searching online.

Can someone else pay my Hendry County taxes?

Yes. The collector's page says anyone may pay. Options include online, mail to P.O. Box 1780 in LaBelle, or an office visit.

Suwannee County by the numbers

Which Suwannee County offices touch a property tax bill?

Value, billing and recording each sit with a different elected office in Live Oak. The appraiser sets what a parcel is worth, the collector sends and takes in payment, and the clerk keeps the deed records. Millage rates come from the local governments that levy tax, and they multiply against the appraiser's figure.

Suwannee became Florida's thirty-seventh county on December 21, 1858, carved out of western Columbia County. It borrows its name from the river that begins in Georgia's Okefenokee Swamp and travels some 240 miles to the Gulf; more than 70 springs along the way pull in divers. Many Suwannee parcels are river frontage, spring-country lots and rural acreage, so legal descriptions deserve a careful look.

  • Property appraiser: 215 Pine Ave SW, Suite B, Live Oak. Phone 386-362-1385. Weekday hours 8:30 to 5:00, closed on county holidays.
  • Tax collector: 215 Pine Ave SW, Suite A, Live Oak. Phone 386-362-2816. The collector serves county residents, with exceptions for property owners.
  • Clerk of the circuit court: records deeds and mortgages and conducts tax deed sales.

The appraiser's calendar shows the offices closed for Good Friday, Veterans Day (observed) and the Thursday and Friday of Thanksgiving, among other holidays, so plan filings around those days.

Which dates control a Suwannee County tax year?

Four dates do most of the work: January 1, March 1, November and March 31. Value and residency are fixed on January 1. Exemption forms go to the appraiser by March 1, and that deadline also covers agricultural classification (DR-482), conservation classification (DR-482C) and the conservation exemption (DR-418C). Business owners file tangible personal property returns (DR-405) by April 1.

Bills then cover one calendar year and carry early-pay savings, listed below as the collector prints them.

Savings for early payment printed by the Suwannee collector
Month paidSavings
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%

The collector says the postmark controls for mail sent before April 1, and the gross amount is due March 31. Payments after April 30 must be in certified funds, and personal checks mailed or left in the drop box are sent back. The same page says the March 31 date is also the deadline to apply for indigent relief or adjust non-ad valorem assessments.

What if a Suwannee County tax bill is left unpaid?

Taxes turn delinquent April 1, and the collector says real estate picks up a 3% penalty that day. Tax sale certificates are then sold on unpaid accounts on or before June 1, which brings extra charges. Anyone holding a certificate waits two years from the April 1 after issuance before asking for a tax deed, and cannot demand payment from the owner during that stretch.

A sale never wipes out the debt. Ask the Suwannee County Tax Collector for a written payoff covering every open year before you sign a contract, and give a copy to the title company.

  • A buyer under a recorded contract for deed is on the list of people notified before a tax deed sale.
  • On homestead land, the opening bid at a tax deed sale includes half of the latest assessed value.
  • Land that draws no bidder goes on a county list, and the county can buy it for the opening bid.

Does Suwannee County offer installments or deferral?

Both exist. The installment plan requires an estimated bill above $100 and an application on file before May 1. Quarter payments land June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, discounted 6%, 4.5% and 3% on the first three and not discounted on the last. A missed first payment drops the parcel from the plan, and owners who stay in are enrolled again every year without reapplying.

Deferral is for homesteads with a low income against the tax. The collector says an owner can postpone the portion above 5% of household income, or above 3% from age 65, and can postpone all of it under $10,000 of income ($12,000 from age 70). The mortgage cannot exceed 70% of assessed value, liens and deferred tax together are capped at 85%, and insurance must name the collector as payee. Applications are due January 31 after bills are mailed. Deferred tax earns interest and sits as a lien on the house.

How do homestead and Save Our Homes change a Suwannee County sale?

Homestead trims taxable value only while you live in the house, and the benefit does not travel with the title. The appraiser's list shows a $25,000 homestead exemption, $5,000 for disabled veterans, and $5,000 each for widows and widowers. Title must be in your name with the house as your permanent home on January 1. Ask the appraiser about the second homestead layer that applies to value above $50,000 for non-school taxes.

Under Save Our Homes, assessed value on a homestead can rise each year by no more than the lower of 3% or inflation. Selling resets the parcel to full just value the next January 1, which means a buyer can face a larger bill than you paid. If you move to another Florida homestead, portability can carry part of the saved value to it, provided the move happens inside three years counted from January 1 of the year you gave up the old home. File DR-501T alongside the new application by March 1.

  • Renting the house out can end the homestead.
  • Forms DR-501DV, DR-501M and DR-501SC cover veterans, deployed service members and low-income seniors.
  • Seniors send income information by June 1.

What should a Suwannee County seller expect at closing?

Your closing agent divides this year's tax with the buyer, which makes the closing date set your share. Older unpaid years are cleared from the proceeds. The collector also asks sellers to send the tax notice on to the new owner or bring it back to the office.

Recording of the deed falls to the clerk, who also collects the state deed tax at the time of filing.

  • Ask for a payoff before listing when a year was skipped.
  • Have the appraiser update ownership and remove your exemption after the sale.
  • Keep the signed closing statement.

When does a direct cash sale make sense in Suwannee County?

A direct purchase suits an inherited house, a vacant one or a parcel that has fallen behind on tax. The buyer takes it as is, so you skip repairs and showings, and the tax balance comes out of the price at the closing table.

Weigh any offer against what listing would leave after commission, repairs and the carrying months. Verify that the legal description and parcel number on the deed match the appraiser's file before you sign.

More questions about Suwannee County, FL Property Tax Guide

What is the last day to pay Suwannee County property tax?

March 31 is the last day for the gross amount. The collector reports 4% off for November payments, 3% for December, 2% for January and 1% for February, judged by postmark before April 1.

When must I apply for homestead in Suwannee County?

March 1 is the cutoff at the property appraiser's office on Pine Avenue in Live Oak, 386-362-1385. The home must be titled to you and be your permanent residence on January 1.

Can I spread Suwannee County property tax over the year?

Yes, when the estimated bill tops $100 and your signed form reaches the collector before May 1. Four payments fall on June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31.

What happens on April 1 to an unpaid Suwannee County bill?

It turns delinquent and a 3% penalty applies to real estate, according to the collector. Certificates on unpaid accounts are sold on or before June 1. Call 386-362-2816 for a payoff.

Who covers the deed stamp tax on a Suwannee County sale?

Florida holds every signer of the deed answerable, whichever side the contract assigns it to. The charge is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, collected by the clerk when the deed is recorded.

What we could not confirm

  • Clerk fee URL
  • Bill mailing date

Which offices deal with a Jefferson County tax bill?

Three offices share the work in Jefferson County: the property appraiser values parcels, the tax collector sends bills and takes payment, and the clerk keeps the deed records and runs tax deed auctions. The county's own property and taxes page sends residents to jeffersonpa.net to search parcels and file for exemptions.

The county page also explains the August cycle. The appraiser mails a TRIM notice showing the property's value and the proposed rates from the county, the school board, the water management districts and other taxing bodies, and the public hearings listed on it come before rates are adopted in September. The city of Monticello levies its own rate, which appears as a separate line in the tax collector's millage list, so a bill inside city limits has more lines than one outside them.

  • Property Appraiser: values land and buildings, takes exemption filings, mails the notice of proposed taxes.
  • Tax Collector: mails statements on or before November 1, takes payment, advertises delinquent accounts, sells certificates.
  • Clerk and Comptroller: official records, and the public auction if a tax deed application is filed.

What is the Jefferson County billing calendar?

The collector mails statements by the first of November. An early payer saves the most, and the savings fade before the April deadline.

Jefferson County tax collector calendar for real estate tax
WhenWhat the collector's page says
On or before November 1Tax statements mailed
November4 percent discount
December3 percent discount
January2 percent discount
February1 percent discount
April 1Delinquent, 3 percent penalty on unpaid real estate tax
Early MayUnpaid accounts advertised in the local paper
On or before June 1Online tax certificate sale

The glossary on the same page notes that the lien for a year's tax attaches at the start of that year. Tangible personal property, such as business equipment and mobile home attachments, draws a steeper monthly penalty, 1.5 percent, once delinquent.

What is the Jefferson County millage rate for 2026?

The collector's millage page lists six lines for 2026, and a house inside Monticello would see all of them. The numbers print as decimals, so the county line reads .00736730, which is 7.3673 mills.

  • Jefferson County: .00736730
  • School, required local effort: .00316000
  • School, discretionary: .00224800
  • City of Monticello: .00685010
  • Northwest Florida Water Management District: .00002010
  • Suwannee River Water Management District: .00026950

Each line belongs to a different body: commissioners, the school board, the city council and the two water districts each vote on their own. The collector's glossary defines a mill as one-tenth of one cent, or one dollar per thousand dollars of taxable value, which is how to read the decimals above. These figures are the published list for the county, and your own parcel may differ. Ask the tax collector which lines apply to your address, since a rural parcel outside the city would not carry the Monticello line, and non-ad valorem charges for services appear separately on the bill.

What homestead and other exemptions can a Jefferson County owner claim?

The county's property page says the appraiser administers exemptions, homestead included. Homestead is worth up to $50,000 off taxable value. The owner has to occupy the house as a permanent home on January 1, a status test that looks back to the start of the year and file on Form DR-501 before the March 1 cutoff.

The first $25,000 applies to every tax, school tax included. The extra layer of up to $25,000 skips school taxes and starts above $50,000 of value. Renting the home or ceasing to live there ends homestead. For an older owner, a county or city ordinance may add an extra exemption of up to $50,000 within an income limit, and the state lists benefits for disabled veterans and for deployed servicemembers on its exemption pages.

Ask the Jefferson County Property Appraiser which of those local options the county has adopted, because the state pages only describe what a local government may choose. A homestead's assessed value cannot climb faster than a state cap each year, but a sale wipes that cushion out for the next owner.

How does the tax bill affect a Jefferson County sale?

A seller carries the tax up to the closing date. Older unpaid years must be cleared before the buyer can hold clean title. The closing agent usually asks the collector for a payoff and pays it from the seller's side of the settlement.

Jefferson County's collector warns that the tax roll is a working roll and figures can change during the year, so a quoted amount is a snapshot. That matters for a fall sale, just before new statements print. Ask for a written payoff dated close to closing. If a lender escrows the tax, ask the servicer how long a leftover balance takes to come back after payoff.

  • Search the parcel on the collector's site and note every year with a balance.
  • Ask whether a certificate was sold on any year, since a certificate needs to be redeemed with certified funds.
  • Confirm exemptions with the appraiser so the title company prorates correctly.
  • Record the deed with the clerk, who takes the stamp tax at the counter.

State law prices deed stamps by the hundred dollars of price, and no party escapes liability by pointing at the contract.

What happens to unpaid Jefferson County property tax?

The debt gets sold to an investor as a certificate, and the owner has a limited stretch to pay it off before the parcel is at risk. The collector says a certificate is a lien created by paying the delinquent tax, not a purchase of the property.

The Jefferson County page describes the sale as a reverse auction on interest, starting at 18 percent and awarded to the lowest bidder. Certificates last seven years, and the face amount includes the 3 percent penalty, the 5 percent collector's commission and advertising costs. A homestead parcel whose face value is under $250 is issued to the county at 18 percent a year instead of being sold. Redeeming takes certified funds. The page warns that missing the 22-month period can end with the parcel going to a tax deed sale.

An investor holding the certificate can ask for a tax deed once two years have passed. The clerk conducts the auction. Statute adds one-half of the latest assessed value to the opening bid when the land is a homestead. An owner at risk should contact the collector's office right away and ask about the deferral program, which has a March 31 application date.

More questions about Jefferson County, FL Property Tax Guide

When do Jefferson County property taxes become delinquent?

Unpaid real estate tax turns delinquent on April 1, and the collector adds a 3 percent penalty to it. In May the unpaid accounts run in the local newspaper, weekly for three weeks, and the cost of the advertisement lands on the owner's bill, so a small balance grows before the certificate sale, and a seller should clear it well ahead of any listing date.

What is the Jefferson County discount for paying early?

The discount starts at 4 percent for a November payment and drops a point each month through February. The collector mails statements by November 1.

Where do I file for homestead in Jefferson County?

File with the Jefferson County Property Appraiser by March 1. The county's property page directs residents to jeffersonpa.net, and the state form is DR-501.

Does a certificate stop me from selling in Jefferson County?

No, but the certificate gets redeemed out of the proceeds, and the collector wants certified funds. Ask the collector's office for an exact payoff before closing day.

Does the Jefferson County millage include the city of Monticello?

Only for parcels inside the city. The collector's 2026 list shows a separate Monticello line of .00685010 beside the county, school and water district lines.

What is Hamilton County, Florida like for a property owner?

Hamilton County is a rural county in north central Florida with Georgia along its northern edge. Its county website calls it a peninsula within a peninsula, bounded by the Withlacoochee River on the west and the Suwannee River on the east and south, with the Alapaha River, known as the "River of Sand", running through the middle.

The county seat is Jasper, and the tax collector's millage table also lists the municipalities of Jennings and White Springs. The county's page puts the estimated population at 14,799 and notes that Hamilton County sits at the crossroads of I-75 and I-10, within reach of Jacksonville, Gainesville and Tallahassee. For a seller, that mix of farmland, small towns and highway access shapes who buys, and the tax bill depends on whether the parcel sits inside a town.

The county also reports a moratorium on single-site RV and camper living, with no electric permits issued for RVs. If the property you plan to sell has an RV hookup, ask the county before listing.

Which Hamilton County offices handle the tax bill?

The property appraiser, the tax collector and the clerk each own one step. The appraiser sets value and exemptions, the collector bills and collects, and the clerk runs the value adjustment board and tax deed sales.

  • Property appraiser: values every parcel, keeps the exemption rolls, and handles name, address and legal description changes. Call or visit the office in Jasper before March 1 to file for homestead.
  • Tax collector: online at hamiltontaxcollector.com, with a parcel search and online payment.
  • Clerk and value adjustment board: 207 NE 1st Street, Room 106, Jasper, phone 386-792-1288.
  • County commission: sets the county millage rate and handles questions such as the RV rule above.

Confirm office hours by phone before you drive in, since county offices post their own schedules.

What does the Hamilton County millage table show?

The tax collector publishes a table headed "Hamilton 2026 millage", in decimal form. Treat it as the collector's published listing and compare it with your TRIM notice and November bill.

Hamilton County millage lines as listed on the tax collector's property tax page
Taxing unitListed rate
County.00870250
School, required local effort.00307500
School, discretionary.00249800
Jasper.00795780
Suwannee River Water Management.00026950
Jennings.00700000
White Springs.00600000

Only one town line applies to a given parcel. A rural parcel carries the county, school and water lines, while a house in Jasper adds the Jasper line. Non-ad valorem assessments are separate, flat charges for services such as fire or solid waste, and they show up on the same bill.

The collector's glossary describes millage as one dollar per thousand dollars of taxable value, so each line shows how much one body adds. Appraisal is the value, assessment is the tax owed, and the tax lien dates from January 1 of the tax year, which is why a bill can follow a house across a sale.

What are the Hamilton County billing and late dates?

The collector mails statements by the first of November. Early payers get 4 percent off in November, then 3, 2 and 1 percent in the following three months. After March, the bill sits at full price until it goes late on the first of April, when real estate tax takes a 3 percent penalty and the parcel is listed in the local paper from May on. Unpaid business property accrues 1.5 percent monthly.

Unpaid real estate liens are sold online at the end of May or on June 1. Before any of that, the appraiser's January 1 valuation date, the March 1 exemption cutoff and the August TRIM notice come first. The state taxpayer page puts the window for a value petition at 25 days after TRIM, and the Department of Revenue lists the rest of the calendar.

How do I appeal a Hamilton County assessment?

You petition the value adjustment board through the clerk. The board only decides whether property is appraised at fair market value and whether an agricultural classification or exemption should be approved. It cannot change a value because you cannot afford the tax, and it has no control over rates.

  • The filing fee is $15, and $5 more for each extra parcel when contiguous parcels are combined on one petition.
  • If the property appraiser or tax collector denied a timely homestead exemption or homestead tax deferral, there is no fee.
  • Petitions need an original signature, and copies or faxes are not accepted.
  • A late petition is sent to the board attorney, and a hearing is set only for good cause.

The clerk encourages you to speak with the property appraiser before filing. The state form is DR-486, and a postmark by the deadline does not save a petition that arrives after it.

What relief programs matter to a Hamilton County seller?

Homestead is the main one, filed by March 1 and available only to the owner's permanent residence. The state guide limits the first layer of the exemption to $25,000 and lets a second layer reach up to $25,000 more, school taxes excluded.

A deferral under Form DR-570 is another route for owners with limited income, with the application due at the tax collector by March 31. For a seller, the cap that protected the old assessed value disappears when title changes hands, which explains why the buyer's bill is often higher than yours. If you are moving to another Florida home, ask the property appraiser there about carrying part of the cap forward.

What if a Hamilton County property goes to a tax deed sale?

The clerk conducts the auction once a certificate holder files an application. Hamilton County's tax deeds page says every property sells buyer beware and as is, with no promises on title, zoning, access or physical condition, and it cites s. 197.542(2) for the high bidder's nonrefundable cost deposit.

A holder may apply two years after April 1 of the issue year, and homestead land opens at the taxes due plus half its latest assessed value. Paying the collector before the sale takes the parcel off the block. If your house has an advertised date, plan the sale of the home around it.

How do I handle a Hamilton County sale when tax is unpaid?

Tell the closing agent about each unpaid year at the start. The agent gets a payoff from the collector and pays it from the sale proceeds, so you do not need cash in hand. Plan the timing around April 1, because the 3 percent penalty and the newspaper charge raise the payoff.

Ask for a draft settlement statement before the closing date and check that every tax line matches the collector's figure. Buyers who pay cash can often meet a tight schedule, a useful option when a certificate or sale date is near.

More questions about Hamilton County, FL Property Tax Guide

When does a Hamilton County bill go late?

On April 1. The collector adds a 3 percent penalty to real estate tax on that date and lists the parcel in the paper beginning in May.

How much is the Hamilton County early payment discount?

It starts at 4 percent for November and falls one point each month through February.

What does it cost to petition the Hamilton County value board?

$15, plus $5 for each added contiguous parcel. Petitions over a denied homestead or homestead deferral request have no fee.

Can a house with a tax certificate be sold in Hamilton County?

Yes. Closing pays the collector, the lien clears, and the buyer gets clean title. Ask for a payoff figure that includes interest.

Who decides the rate on my Hamilton County bill?

The taxing bodies decide, such as the county, school board, towns and the river district. The appraiser only sets value and handles exemptions.
