Who sends, collects and enforces a Franklin County tax bill?

Three offices share the work. The appraiser values the parcel, the tax collector bills it, and the clerk of court conducts any tax deed auction. The county commission, school board and the cities of Apalachicola and Carrabelle set the rates.

Franklin County lies in the northwestern Panhandle, roughly 80 miles southwest of Tallahassee, across 545 square miles and 348,800 acres. The county site cites more than 11,000 residents and a founding year of 1832. Outside the two cities, the commission serves as the local government.

  • Property appraiser: keeps the roll, takes exemption filings, mails TRIM notices in August. Per its home page, the office neither sets rates nor collects tax.
  • Tax collector: 33 Market Street, Suite 202, Apalachicola; (850) 653-9323. Prints bills, accepts payment, sells certificates.
  • Clerk: holds the courthouse auction of tax deeds and records your deed when you sell.

What is the Franklin County tax calendar?

Exemption paperwork comes first in the year, and the bill comes last. The table lists each step the county offices print on their own sites.

Franklin County property tax steps, from the appraiser and tax collector websites
WhenStepOffice
January 1 to March 1Window for homestead and agricultural classification filingsProperty appraiser
April 1Business personal property returns dueProperty appraiser
AugustTRIM notice, marked as a notice and not a billProperty appraiser
By November 1Statements mailedTax collector
November through FebruaryDiscount slides from 4% to 1%Tax collector
April 1 of the next yearReal estate bill late; 3% penaltyTax collector
On or before June 1Online lien auction for unpaid parcelsTax collector

Sources: the tax collector and the appraiser. Mailing a statement does not turn the TRIM notice into a bill, so wait for the November statement before paying.

What do the Franklin County millage lines mean?

Franklin County's tax collector posts a table labeled "Franklin 2025 millage". A millage figure is the tax per thousand dollars of taxable value, and the table prints it as a decimal. Ask the collector for the table covering the current year before you rely on these.

  • County: .00504590
  • School, local effort: .00194400
  • School, discretionary: .00224800
  • Northwest Florida Water Management: .00002070
  • Carrabelle: .00750000
  • Apalachicola: .00834570
  • Dog Island: .00400000
  • Eastpoint district: .00375000
  • Alligator Point: .00123040

Only one local line fits a given address. Eastpoint, Dog Island and Alligator Point appear as districts, and Carrabelle and Apalachicola are the two cities. County, school and water lines stack on top. Flat assessments for services are charged separately and print on the same statement, so check the lower portion of the bill too.

What reduces a Franklin County bill?

A permanent residence qualifies for the Florida homestead exemption of up to $50,000 of value, described in the Department of Revenue guide. The filing window runs January 1 to March 1 at the appraiser's office, and renting the house out ends eligibility.

Once a homestead is in place, a statutory cap restrains how fast its assessed value can rise. A sale wipes out that cushion for the next owner, so the buyer's first Franklin County bill may look much larger than yours did.

Can the bill be paid in pieces in Franklin County?

The state permits quarterly prepayment under s. 197.222 if you apply to the tax collector by May 1 of the assessment year, and low-income homestead owners can defer part of the tax with Form DR-570 by March 31. Both come from the state taxpayer page. Whether either route helps depends on your income and timing, so phone the collector at (850) 653-9323 before the dates pass. Mortgage escrow lenders normally settle the bill themselves.

What happens after April 1 on an unpaid Franklin County parcel?

A 3 percent penalty lands on the real estate bill at the start of April, and in May the parcel is listed in the paper for three straight weeks at the owner's expense. Business equipment and mobile home attachments follow a harsher path of monthly interest and warrants.

Around the end of May, the collector auctions a lien certificate online. Bidders start at 18 percent and bid the rate down, and the low rate wins. The winner pays your tax and holds a lien, and you owe them the bid rate. A buyer cannot take your house at that point. The glossary says a deed application is allowed two years after April 1 of the issue year, and the collector warns that a certificate left unredeemed for 22 months can end in a deed sale.

Homestead parcels owing under $250 are not offered to the public. The county holds those at 18 percent a year until the total passes $250.

How does a Franklin County tax deed sale work?

The clerk's office runs the sale. Franklin County sales, when scheduled, are generally held on the first Monday of the month at 11:00 AM inside the main courthouse at 33 Market Street, Apalachicola, and the clerk tells people to call to verify before attending. Notice runs in the Apalachicola Times once a week for four weeks.

  • You can redeem by paying the tax collector before the sale, or before the clerk receives the winning bidder's full payment.
  • For homestead property, the opening bid adds half of the latest assessed value to the taxes, interest and fees.
  • The winning bidder posts a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is greater, and pays the balance within 24 hours.
  • Documentary stamps of $.70 per $100 of the bid and recording fees are due from the bidder.
  • Some government liens survive the deed, and every property is sold as is.

The clerk's page adds cautions for anyone on either side. Governmental liens can survive the deed, and the clerk warns that most title insurers want a quiet title lawsuit before they will insure a tax deed property. The deed gives the buyer a right to immediate possession, but the clerk says legal action may still be needed to get it. For an owner, the lesson is simple: a sale that you close before the auction date avoids all of that, and your own buyer gets a normal title search instead.

What does a Franklin County seller do about taxes at closing?

An unpaid balance is a lien the buyer's title company will insist on clearing. The closing agent can send the payoff to the tax collector out of the seller's proceeds. Request a figure good through the closing day, since a bill past April 1 grows by a 3 percent penalty and newspaper advertising.

The state also taxes the deed itself. Documentary stamps run 70 cents on each $100 of consideration outside Miami-Dade, and every party to the document is liable, according to the Department of Revenue. The clerk takes the payment at recording.

More questions about Franklin County, FL Property Tax Guide

Which month is the cheapest to pay in Franklin County?

November. The tax collector prints a 4 percent discount for November, 3 percent for December, 2 percent for January and 1 percent for February.

Does the appraiser or the collector set my rate?

Neither. Per the appraiser's home page, that office does not set rates, and the tax collector's millage page says the county commission, school board and each city or district do.

Is a house with a tax certificate on it still sellable?

Yes. Closing pays the redemption to the tax collector, which then repays the certificate holder. Ask (850) 653-9323 for the redemption total.

When is the Franklin County exemption filing cutoff?

March 1. Filing opens January 1, and the appraiser notes the home must be your permanent residence.

How fast can a tax deed auction happen?

Slowly. A certificate holder waits two years after April 1 of the issue year to apply, and you can redeem up to the point the clerk receives the winning bidder's full payment.

Which office runs property tax in Washington County, Florida?

The tax collector in Chipley bills and collects, while the county property appraiser values each parcel. The collector's office is in Chipley and keeps weekday daytime hours, with a separate post office box for mail.

The collector's millage page spells out who sets what. The Board of County Commissioners sets the county rate, the School Board sets the school rates, each city council sets the rate for its municipality, and special districts set their own. The same page says the property appraiser establishes the value of real estate and tangible personal property.

That division is useful to a seller. A question about the value or an exemption belongs with the appraiser, and a question about the amount owed or a certificate belongs with the collector.

Which taxing bodies appear on a Washington County bill?

The collector's millage page lists seven levies for 2026: Chipley, Vernon, the county, Northwest Florida Water Management, and three school levies. The rates are printed as decimals, so a figure like .00850000 means 8.5 mills. Confirm which are final with the tax collector before you rely on them, since the page does not say the rates are adopted.

Levies listed on the Washington County millage page, year 2026
LevyRate as printed
County.00850000

Source: Washington County Tax Collector, millage rates. A parcel outside Chipley and Vernon does not pay a city levy. Which levies you pay turns on the parcel's location.

What are the Washington County tax deadlines?

Collection starts in November and runs through March 31, with a falling discount. The tax collector's deadline page sets out the year.

  • November: collection begins, with a 4% discount for payment by November 30.
  • December: 3% discount.
  • January: 2% discount. February: 1% discount.
  • March 31: gross amount due, and the final installment payment is due.
  • April 1: unpaid real property tax is delinquent and a 3% penalty is added.
  • April 30: applications for next year's installment plan are due.

Delinquent real property is advertised within 45 days, according to the page, and the cost lands on the bill. The list is advertised weekly for three weeks ahead of the certificate sale. It also says the sale date is set in March, ahead of the April 1 delinquency.

How does the Washington County installment plan run?

The plan is built on four payments through the year. The deadlines page puts the first due on or before June 1, with cancellation if it is not paid by June 30, the second before September 30, the third by December 31, and the fourth by March 31. Taxpayers already enrolled do not reapply.

The application window closes April 30 for the next year. Escrowed owners usually have no use for it, since the lender pays in full.

Statewide, an owner may apply to the tax collector by May 1 of the assessment year under s. 197.222, per the Department of Revenue. Ask the office which form and which amount applies to your parcel.

What does a tax certificate mean for a Washington County house?

A certificate is a lien created when someone pays your delinquent tax. It is not a purchase of the property. The collector sells them by June 1 for the previous year's unpaid taxes.

The page describes how the amount is built: unpaid real estate tax and non ad valorem assessments, a 3% penalty, a 5% collector commission and advertising costs. Bidding opens at 18% and goes down, and the winning rate is what the owner pays. If the interest earned is under 5%, a 5% minimum applies.

  • A homestead parcel whose face value is under $250 is not sold to the public. The certificate goes to the county at 18%.
  • Certificates are dated as of the first day of the sale and expire after seven years.
  • Redemption requires certified funds in US dollars.

The office warns that failing to redeem within the 22 month period set by law can result in loss of the property at a tax deed sale. The state counts two years from April 1 of the issue year before a holder can apply, per s. 197.502. The collector also runs an online tax sale site, taxcertsale.com/WashingtonTaxSale.

How do exemptions change what a Washington County buyer pays?

Exemptions stay with the owner and do not pass to a buyer. The appraiser's deadline is March 1, and the owner must have the home as a permanent residence by January 1, per the Department of Revenue's homestead guide.

The state's Save Our Homes cap ties yearly assessment growth to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change, and a sale resets the property to just value the following January 1, per the Department of Revenue. A buyer should not assume the seller's lower bill carries over.

A seller's final bill therefore tells the buyer very little about next year's bill. Ask the property appraiser for the value and exemptions on the parcel.

What should a Washington County seller do about unpaid tax?

Call the collector in Chipley and ask for the amount good through the planned closing date. Then give it to the title agent. The collector's page notes that the 3% penalty arrives April 1 and the advertising cost shortly after, so selling before that date is cheaper.

At recording, deed stamps go to the clerk. The state revenue agency prints the rate as 70 cents per $100 outside Miami-Dade and makes every party to the document liable, as its stamp tax page.

Can a Washington County owner challenge a value?

Yes, with a petition to the value adjustment board. State guidance says the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes arrives in August, and a value challenge is filed with the court clerk inside 25 days of that notice. A denial of an exemption, classification or portability has a separate 30 day window after the denial letter was mailed, per the Department of Revenue.

Non-homestead assessed value can rise no more than 10 percent a year, so a large jump on a rental or vacant lot may signal a change of ownership or new construction. Ask the property appraiser to explain the change before you file.

  • August: TRIM notice arrives with proposed taxes.
  • Within 25 days: file a value petition with the clerk.
  • September and October: taxing bodies hold budget hearings.
  • November: bills go out.

How does tangible personal property tax work in Washington County?

Business equipment is taxed on a separate account with its own penalty. The collector's deadline page says unpaid tangible personal property tax becomes delinquent April 1 with 1.5% interest per month, advertised in a local newspaper within 45 days, and the tax warrant process starts May 1.

Owners must file Form DR-405 with the property appraiser by April 1, per state guidance. A rental owner who sells a property and keeps the furniture or equipment should confirm that account is closed so a stray bill does not follow.

More questions about Washington County, FL Property Tax Guide

When are Washington County property taxes delinquent?

April 1. The Washington County Tax Collector's page says a 3% penalty is added to the gross amount on that date.

What is the first discount month in Washington County?

November, with a 4% discount on payments made by November 30. December is 3%, January 2% and February 1%.

Can a homestead owner lose a house over a small debt?

Not to a public sale of the certificate for a small amount. The collector says a homestead parcel with a face value under $250 is issued to the county at 18% interest instead of being sold.

How long does a certificate stay valid in Washington County?

Seven years. Certificates are dated from the first day of the sale and then expire.

Where do I find current Washington County millage rates?

On the tax collector's millage rates page, which lists the 2026 levies for the county, Chipley, Vernon, the school board and the water management district. Ask the office to confirm which rates are final.
